# 1.4.4 wBG Polymers Based on Benzotriazole (BTA) Derivatives

BTA with a unique triazole structure has a relatively weak electron-withdrawing ability due to the lone-pair electrons on the 2-position of N contribute to the fused-triazole and its photovoltaic materials generally have strong self-aggregation and $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking effects [204]. Therefore, the BTA-based polymer donors usually show a WBG, high crystallinity, high extinction coefficient, and good hole mobility. Consequently, the BTA-based polymer donors have developed rapidly and have been widely used for the efficient OSCs based on LBG SM acceptors in the past few years [205-208]. In the early studies, the high HOMO levels of BTA-based polymer donors limit their application in photovoltaic materials. To decrease the HOMO level of BTA-based polymers donors, You and coworkers synthesized a difluorinated benzotriazole (2fBTA) unit and developed a WBG polymer P263 [209]. Compared with its fluorine-free analog (P262), P263 obtained a dramatically improved PCE from ${ \sim } 4 \%$ to ${ \sim } 7 \%$ , owing to the higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and FF values. Recently, Li and coworkers designed and synthesized a series of thienyl BDT (BDT-T)-alt-2fBTA-structured high-performance polymer donors with WBG and deep HOMO level by modifying the 2D-conjugated thienyl of BDT unit [206-208, 210-212]. For example, polymer P265 was synthesized by introducing alkylthio substitutions into 2D-conjugated thienyls, targeting a deep-shifted HOmO level and improved crystallinity. Blending with ITIC, the P265-based OSCs obtained a PCE of $9 . 5 3 \%$ [206]. Subsequently, Fan et al. synthesized a polymer, P269 [207], via side chain engineering of P265. Compared with P265, P269 showed the increased steric hindrance on the BDT-T donor unit and the decreased steric hindrance on the 2fBTA acceptor unit, which resulted in stronger intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ interactions, and more efficient charge separation and transport in its OSCs. Thus, the P269:ITIC-based OSCs achieved an improved PCE of $1 0 . 5 \%$ Another 2fBTA-based polymer donor P266 was synthesized by attaching trialkylsilyl side chains into the 2D-conjugated thienyls [208]. Thanks to the $\sigma ^ { * }$ (Si)- $\pi ^ { * }$ (C) interaction deep-shifted the molecular HOmO level and increased absorption coefficient of P266, both higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ values were achieved in its OSCs. Fluorination of the 2D-conjugated thienyl on BDT unit has been convincingly established to be beneficial for deep-shifting molecular HOMO level and improving optical absorption, crystallinity, and charge transport of photovoltaic materials [169, 210, 211, 213]. Fan et al. reported a WBG polymer P268 based on difluorinated BDT-TF donor unit with mono-fluorinated thienyls and 2fBTA acceptor unit and found that the corresponding OsCs achieved improved photovoltaic parameters compared with those of the P270-based OSCs [210]. Subsequently, Xue et al. synthesized a tetra-fluorinated BDT-T2F donor unit with difluorinated thienyls and then developed another WBG polymer P267 with BTA unit [211]. In addition to deep-shift the molecular HOMO level and increasing absorption coefficient and hole mobility, fluorination on 2D-conjugated nienyis or ine posymers couia suppress tripiet rormauon to reauce cnarge carrier recombination in OSCs. With these favorable advantages, the P267:m-ITIC-based OSCs achieved a high PCE of $1 1 . 6 3 \%$ . It is well known that the introduction of chlorine atom and silicon atom substitutions into molecular backbone are two important strategies to deep-shift molecular HOMO level, improve absorption coefficient, and increase charge mobility of photovoltaic materials [208, 214]. By combining the chlorine and alkylsilyl substitutions into the 2D-conjugated thienyls of BDT-T unit, a BTA-based WBG polymer P272 was synthesized by Fan and coworkers and achieved a high PCE of $1 2 . 8 \%$ in its OSCs [212]. Yang and coworkers synthesized two BTA-based WBG polymer donors 273 and P274 with alkyloxy- or alkylthio-substituted 2D-biphenyl BDT units [215]. Using alkylthio chains instead of alkoxy chains, P274 showed a deeper HOmO level by over $0 . 2 0 \mathrm { e V }$ compared to its counterpart P273, resulting in a significantly improved $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . Blending with ITIC, P274 achieved a higher PCE of $1 2 . 0 9 \%$ in its OSCs compared to the counterpart polymer P273 $( 9 . 2 0 \% )$ . In the same year, Yang and coworkers synthesized a $2 \mathrm { D } { - } 2 \mathrm { D }$ asymmetric BDT monomer [216]. The studies showed that this asymmetric structure had unique advantages in comparison with the conventional 2D symmetric BDT unit. The 2D-conjugated thienylthiol side chain on the BDT unit could reduce molecular HOMO level, broaden absorption spectra, and improve solubility. The bare rigid aryl of naphthalene as another 2D-conjugated side chain could be regarded as lever arms to stir up well the elongated ITIC and weaken the entanglements among polymer chains during the spin-coating process, which enabled a favorable morphology without post treatment. As a result, the corresponding BTA-based wBG polymer donor P275 with a 2D-2D asymmetric structure yielded a high PCE of $1 1 . 5 6 \%$ in its as-cast OSCs [216]. Currently, most high-performance WBG polymer donors are based on BDT units. Recently, Sun and coworkers developed a benzodifuran (DF)-based polymer P276 [217], in which chlorinated thienyl BDF and BTA building blocks were used as the electron-donating and electron-withdrawing units, respectively. Blending with TTPT-T-4F, P276 obtained a remarkably higher PCE of $1 4 . 0 \%$ in OSCs compared to its analog BDT-based polymer P271 $( 1 2 . 7 2 \% )$ . Yan and coworkers reported a polymer P277 with a WBG of $2 . 0 5 \mathrm { e V }$ and strong aggregation properties, which was based on a BDT donor unit and a BTA acceptor unit [218]. Different with conventional BDT-based polymers with a BDT unit linked via the $\alpha$ positions of the thiophene units, the BDT units in P277 were connected via the phenyl group of the BDT unit. In the P277:O-IDTBR blend film, both the donor and acceptor could maintain their crystallinity and form small domains. With these favorite properties, P277 achieved a PCE of $1 1 . 6 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 8 \mathrm { V }$ in its OSCs. By introducing a siloxane-terminated side chain into BTA building block and its BTA-fused derivative, Huang and coworkers developed two WBG polymer donors P278 and P279 [219]. The resulting two polymers were successfully used to fabricate efficient ternary all-polymer OSCs with a LBG polymer acceptor N2200 and achieved a PCE of $9 . 1 7 \%$ with an active layer thickness of $3 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ . Subsequently, the P279:N2200-based all-polymer OSCs obtained a significantly improved PCE of $1 1 . 7 6 \%$ by the meticulous optimization of blend morphology in Liu's group [220].

To match the deep LUMO levels of the LBG SM acceptors, Huang and coworkers further reduced the HOMO levels of the polymer donor PTzBI series consist of a BDT electron-donating unit and a pyrrolo $[ 3 , 4 - f ]$ benzotriazole- $5 , 7 ( 6 H )$ dione (TzBI) electron-withdrawing building block by introducing two 2D-conjugated difluorophenyl units on the 3,6-positions of BDT unit. The resulting WBG polymer donor P280 with 3-branched alkyl side chains of the TzBI unit showed the optimized molecular orientation and crystallinity [221]. Matching with SM acceptor IT-4F, the P280-based OSCs achieved a certified high PCE of $1 2 . 2 5 \%$ with both improved $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ on a device area of $1 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ . Notably, Huang and coworkers selected another SM acceptor Y6 with a similar LUMO level but a lower bandgap to match P280 for more complementary absorption and well-matched energy levels, the corresponding OsCs obtained an impressive PCE over $1 6 \%$ [222]. Recently, two BTA units-fused naphtho[1,2-c:5,6-c]bis(2-octyl[1-3]triazole) (TZNT) was also used as electron-withdrawing building block to construct high-performance WBG polymer donors [223, 224]. Peng and coworkers synthesized two WBG polymers, non-fluorinated P281 and fluorinated P282 with a backbone of TZNT-alt-bithiophene (DT) [223]. Compared to P281, P282 had a higher crystallinity, stronger absorption coefficient, and deeper HOMO level, leading to the higher PCEs of $1 0 . 6 0 \%$ and $1 1 . 4 8 \%$ in binary and ternary blend OsCs, respectively. Soon afterward, Peng and coworkers developed the others two TZNT-based WBG polymer donors P283 and P284 by using 2-alkylthio-substituted thienyl BDT (BDT-TS) unit or 2-alkylthio-3-fluorine-substituted thienyl BDT (BDT-TSF) unit instead of DT unit [224]. The rigid planar backbone of BDT-T and TZNT units imparted high crystallinity and good molecular stacking properties to these polymers. Using IT-4F as SM acceptor, the P284-based OSCs obtained a high PCE of $1 3 . 2 5 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { V }$ and a low $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ of $0 . 5 9 \mathrm { e V } .$ Furthermore, the P284:IT-4F-based homo-tandem devices with improved light-harvesting ability achieved a further increased PCE of $1 4 . 5 2 \%$ , which was the best value for homo-tandem OSCs. The chemical structures of the polymer donors based on BTA derivatives are showed in Figure 1.37, and the corresponding photovoltaic parameters of OSCs are summarized in Table 1.28.

# 1.4.5 WBG Polymers Based on Thiazole, Pyrazine, and Their Derivatives Containing N-Heterocycles

$N$ -heterocycles-based acceptor building blocks with a weak electron-withdrawing ability, strong intramolecular noncovalent bonds and intermolecular interaction, such as bisthiazole (BTz) [225-227], thiazolo[5,4-d]thiazole (TTz) [228-231], benzo[1,2-d:4,5-d']bis(thiazole) (BBTz) [232], 1,3,4-thiadiazole (TDz) [233], 1,3,4-oxadiazole (ODz) [234], pyrazine (PAz) [235], quinoxaline $\left( \mathbf { Q x } \right)$ [236, 237], dithieno[3,2-f:2'] $3 ^ { \prime }$ -h]quinoxaline (DTQx) [238], 1,2,4,5-tetrazine (TAz) [239], and related derivatives, have been widely used for constructing high-performance WBG polymer donors with a good planarity, deep HOMO level, high absorption coefficient, and strong crystallinity. In 2011, Zhang et al. reported a polymer donor P285 with a WBG of $2 . 0 7 \mathrm { e V }$ by combining BTz as electron-withdrawing unit and alkyl-substituted IDT as weak electron-donating unit [225]. Blending with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ its OSCs achieved a low PCE of $2 . 7 7 \%$ due to the limited absorption spectrum.

><td>5.48/3.37</td><td>TTPT-T-4F</td><td>0.85</td><td>21.25</td><td>0.701</td><td>12.72</td><td>[217]</td></tr><tr><td>P277</td><td>2.05</td><td>5.47/3.42</td><td>O-IDTBR</td><td>1.08</td><td>16.26</td><td>0.636</td><td>11.6</td><td>[218]</td></tr><tr><td>P278</td><td>1.93</td><td>5.23/2.93</td><td>N2200</td><td>0.81</td><td>15.35</td><td>0.5638</td><td>7.00</td><td>[219]</td></tr><tr><td>P279</td><td>1.93</td><td>5.31/3.10</td><td>N2200</td><td>0.84</td><td>16.82</td><td>0.5187</td><td>7.34</td><td>[219]</td></tr><tr><td>P279</td><td>1.93</td><td>5.31/-3.10</td><td>N2200</td><td>0.88</td><td>17.62</td><td>0.7578</td><td>11.76</td><td>[220]</td></tr><tr><td>P280</td><td>1.85</td><td>5.38/-3.06</td><td>IT-4F</td><td>0.891</td><td>19.65</td><td>0.7409</td><td>12.96</td><td>[221]</td></tr><tr><td>P280</td><td>1.85</td><td>5.38/3.06</td><td>Y6</td><td>0.81</td><td>26.68</td><td>0.7411</td><td>16.02</td><td>[222]</td></tr><tr><td>P281</td><td>1.94</td><td>5.16/-3.10</td><td>IT-M</td><td>0.75</td><td>10.15</td><td>0.581</td><td>4.42</td><td>[223]</td></tr><tr><td>P282</td><td>1.84</td><td>5.24/3.23</td><td>IT-M</td><td>0.80</td><td>17.33</td><td>0.725</td><td>10.05</td><td>[223]</td></tr><tr><td>P283</td><td>1.99</td><td>5.39/3.30</td><td>IT-4F</td><td>0.88</td><td>18.65</td><td>0.689</td><td>11.31</td><td>[224]</td></tr><tr><td>P284</td><td>1.97</td><td>5.45/3.41</td><td>IT-4F</td><td>0.93</td><td>19.23</td><td>0.741</td><td>13.25</td><td>[224]</td></tr></table>

Subsequently, using multi-alkyl thienyl-BDT unit instead of IDT unit, Zhang and coworkers reported another BTz-based WBG $( 1 . 8 9 \mathrm { e V } )$ polymer donor P286 [226]. Compared to P285, P286 shows a red-shifted absorption onset from 600 to $6 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ significantly improved planarity and crystalline structure, as well as increased hole mobility, leading to a higher PCE of $6 . 0 9 \%$ in the $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ -based OSCs. Soon afterward, by replacing multi-alkyl thienyl-BDT unit with multi-alkoxyl phenyl-BDT unit in polymer backbone, Zhang and coworkers developed an efficient BTz-based polymer donor P287 [227]. Compared to P286, P287 exhibits a wider bandgap of $2 . 0 \mathrm { e V }$ with strong absorption in the range of $3 0 0 \sim 6 2 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and a lower-lying HOMO level of $- 5 . 3 6 \mathrm { e V } .$ The OSCs based on $\mathrm { P } 2 8 7 { \mathrm { : P C } } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ showed a PCE of $8 . 1 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 6 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 0 . 9 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a high FF of $7 6 . 7 \%$ , which was among the highest values for the OSCs combined fullerene derivatives and polymer donors with a bandgap near to $2 . 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ Moreover, blending with a LBG SM acceptor ITIC, its OSCs achieved a higher PCE of $1 0 . 3 \%$ with both improved $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 1 \mathrm { V }$ and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 4 . 1 \mathrm { m A } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$

Compared to BTz unit, TTz unit has a larger fused-ring rigid structure, resulting in the stronger intermolecular aggregation and interaction of the corresponding polymers [228-230]. In 2016, Zhang and coworkers synthesized a polymer donor named PTZ1 (P288) by polymerizing BDT-T electron-donating unit and TTz electron-withdrawing unit for photovoltaic applications [228]. P288 with high crystallinity and favorable backbone orientation shows a desirable WBG of $1 . 9 7 \mathrm { e V } ,$ a deep HOMO level $- 5 . 3 1 \mathrm { e V } ,$ and a relatively high hole mobility $> 1 0 ^ { - 3 } \thinspace \mathrm { c m ^ { 2 } V ^ { - 1 } \thinspace s ^ { - 1 } }$ Consequently, single-junction OSCs based on $\mathrm { P } 2 8 8 { \mathrm { : P C } } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ obtained a PCE of $7 . 7 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 4 \mathrm { V } .$ Moreover, its tandem PSCs based on P288 as a donor material in the front cell achieved an improved PCE of $1 0 . 3 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 6 5 \mathrm { V } .$ Blending P288 with IDIC, the fabricated OSCs achieved the highest PCE of $1 1 . 5 \%$ , while the OSCs still obtained a PCE of $9 . 6 \%$ with an active layer thickness of $2 1 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and a relatively high PCE of $1 0 . 5 \%$ with a device area of up to $0 . 8 1 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ [229]. By incorporating a sulfur atom into 2D-conjugated alkylthienyl groups, Su et al. reported another similar WBG (1.96 eV) polymer P289 [230]. The P289-based OSCs with SM acceptors ITIC or IDIC achieved PCEs more than $8 \%$ Moreover, by inserting ITIC into the binary P289:IDIC system, the active layer shows smooth and gradient energy levels, improved crystallinity, and optimized morphologies, which results in efficient exciton separation, charge transport and collection. Consequently, the optimized ternary OSCs based on P289:ITIC:IDIC $( 1 : 0 . 1 : 0 . 9 )$ obtained a higher PCE of $1 1 . 1 \%$ in comparison with those of binary OSC systems. Recently, Huang and coworkers reported a series of wBG polymer donor analogs (P290 and P291) composed of thienothiophene (TT) or TTz units [231] and studied their device performance with N2200 in all-polymer OSCs. Results show that all-polymer OSCs with the TTz-based P291 achieved a PCE as high as $8 . 4 \%$ , which largely outperform the analog P290-based ones with a PCE of only $0 . 7 \%$ . In 2019, Yang and coworkers developed a WBG $( 2 . 1 \mathrm { e V } )$ polymer donor P292 with a backbone of BDT-T-alt-BBTz [232]. Compared to TTz unit, BBTz unit has a further enlarged fused-ring rigid structure by inserting a benzene ring into TTz unit, resulting in the weaker electron-withdrawing ability, deep HOmO level, and stronger intermolecular aggregation and interaction of the corresponding polymers. Blending P292 with a LBG SM acceptor ITIC-F, the OSCs obtained a high PCE of $1 3 . 3 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 0.91 V, a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 . 9 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an FF of 0.70. TDz unit with high polarizability and relatively weak electron-withdrawing ability, has been widely studied in optoelectronic field. By polymerizing BDT and TDz building blocks, Peng and coworkers synthesized a polymer donor P293 with a WBG over $2 . 0 7 \mathrm { e V }$ and a low-lying HOMO level of $- 5 . 3 5 \mathrm { e V }$ [233], which matches well with the typical LBG SM acceptor ITIC. By using a single green solvent of o-xylene, the as-cast OSCs achieved a large $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ up to $1 . 1 0 \mathrm { V }$ and an extremely low $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ of $0 . 4 8 \mathrm { e V } ,$ as well as the desirable $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 7 . 7 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and FF of $6 5 . 4 \%$ , leading to a high PCE of $1 2 . 8 0 \%$ . When adopting a homo-tandem device architecture, the PCE is further improved to $1 3 . 3 5 \%$ with an improved $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $2 . 1 3 \mathrm { V } .$ After that, by using ODz instead of TDz, Peng and coworkers reported another polymer donor P294 [234]. Compared to the TDz-based P293, P294 with a similar backbone has a wider bandgap of $2 . 1 2 \mathrm { e V }$ and a deeper HOMO level of $- 5 . 6 8 \mathrm { e V . }$ By adding $4 \%$ of copper(I) iodide as an additive to form coordination complexes with P294 for optimizing blend morphology, significantly improved device performances are achieved due to the improved absorption and crystallinity of photovoltaic materials. As a result, the PCE is elevated from $1 0 . 1 2 \%$ to $1 2 . 3 4 \%$

N-heterocyclic benzene derivatives, such as PAz [235], Qx [236, 237], DTQx [238], and TAz [239], also have been applied in the synthesis of WBG photovoltaic materials. Chen et al. firstly introduced F atom into PAz-based electron-withdrawing unit and successfully applied it in constructing a polymer donor P296 for OSCs [235]. Compared to its non-fluorinated counterpart P295, P296 had a better planarity, improved absorbance with red-shifted spectrum and higher absorption coefficient, reduced HOmO level, and optimized molecular packing and morphological properties. Blending with MeIC, the P296-based OSCs delivered a PCE of $1 2 . 3 \%$ , which was much higher than that of the P295-based control OSCs $( 1 0 . 2 \% )$ . In addition to high efficiency and good stability, the application of OsCs requires the realization of 1ow-cost devices. Sun et al. demonstrated a low-cost WBG polymer donor P297 with a simple backbone of thiophene-alt-(6,7-difluoro-2-(2-hexyldecyloxy)quinoxaline), which was synthesized by only two-step simple reactions with high overall yield of $8 7 . 4 \%$ from cheap raw materials [236]. More important, the P297-based OSCs achieved a high PCE of $1 2 . 7 0 \%$ , and the corresponding as-cast devices with thickness insensitivity also obtained a high PCE of $1 0 . 4 1 \%$ , which indicated that P297 was a promising polymer donor for commercial application of OsCs. By attaching an additional methyl substituent in the Qx unit of low-cost polymer donor P297, Sun et al. reported another similar polymer donor P298 [237]. Compared to P297, P298 showed an upshifted HOMO level of $- 5 . 5 2 \mathrm { e V } ,$ stronger molecular crystallization, and better hole transport capability. Impressively, the OsCs based on P298:TPT10 with near zero HOMO offset achieved a high PCE of $1 6 . 3 2 \%$ due to the efficient exciton dissociation and hole transfer. Recently, Hou and coworkers fused two thiophene units along with Qx to design DTQx, which is quite similar with DTBT [238]. The resulting polymer P299 achieved a high PCE of $1 8 . 0 \%$ in the ternary devices using BTA3 and BTP-eC9 as the acceptor materials. In 2019, Peng and coworkers synthesized a TAz-containing WBG polymer P300 [239]. The studies showed that P300 had a strong aggregation property, which resulted in serious phase separation and large domains when blending with Y6. To address the above defect, Peng and coworkers developed a new strategy of platinum(I1) complexation to regulate molecular crystallinity and packing of TAz-based polymers, optimize blend morphology, and improve PCE of the resulting OSCs. Compared to binary polymer P300, the TAz-based ternary polymer P301 had bulky benzene ring on the platinum(II) complex to increase steric hindrance along the polymer main chain, which was beneficial to inhibit molecular aggregation strength and regulate blend morphology, and thus improved PCE to $1 6 . 3 5 \%$ in OSCs [239]. The chemical structures of the polymer donors based on thiazole, pyrazine, and their derivatives containing $N$ heterocycles are showed in Figure 1.38, and the corresponding photovoltaic parameters of OSCs are summarized in Table 1.29.

# 1.4.6 wBG Polymers Based on Benzodithiophene-4,8-dione (BDD) Derivatives

Benzodithiophene-4,8-dione (BDD) and its derivatives with a rigid large planarity and two fused electron-withdrawing ${ \mathrm { C } } { = } { \mathrm { O } }$ bonds have been widely used to construct high-performance polymer donors for photovoltaic applications [240-244]. Among these BDD-based polymers, the polymer donors (namely PBDB-T series) with a molecular backbone of BDT-alt-BDD display some unique properties, such as high absorption coefficient, wBG, temperature-dependent absorption spectra, deep-lying HOMO level, and high carrier mobility [240-251]. In 2012, Hou and coworkers developed a BDD-based WBG $\left( 1 . 8 0 \mathrm { e V } \right)$ polymer donor with a 2D-conjugated thienyl BDT derivative, namely PBDB-T (P302) [241]. P302 displayed a strong aggregation effect in solution state, and the studies indicated that device efficiency of the $\mathrm { P } 3 0 2 { \mathrm { : P C } } _ { 6 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ -based OSCs could be easily affected by the processing temperature used in solution preparation. By matching P302 with a LBG SM acceptor ITIC, Hou and coworkers reported a high PCE ot $1 1 . 2 1 \%$ [252]. Atter that, the following-up reports using P302 congeners sprang up in fullerene-based and SM-acceptor-based OSCs. In 2015, Zhang et al. synthesized a PBDB-T derivative, namely PM6 (PBDB-TF, P303) [242], by attaching a fluorine atom on 2D-conjugated thienyl substituents of polymer. Compared to P302, fluorinated P303 showed obviously downshifted HOMO level, stronger crystallinity, and smaller $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance. Matching with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ , its OSCs obtained a PCE of $9 . 2 \%$ . P303 also could match different types of LBG SM/polymer acceptors very well with respect to absorption, energy levels, and morphological compatibility. In this regard, blending P303 with typical SM acceptor ITIC, the OSCs achieved a PCE of $9 . 7 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ up to $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V }$ [253]; with a strongly crystalline SM acceptor IDIC, the as-cast OSCs achieved the PCEs exceeded $1 1 \%$ with different active layer thicknesses [254]; with a tetra-fluorinated SM acceptor IT-4F, the OSCs delivered a PCE of $1 3 . 5 \%$ [255]; and with polymerized small molecular acceptors (PSMAs) such as PZ1 [256], PF1-TS4 [257], PF2-DTSi [258], PF3-DTCO [259], PFBDT-IDTIC [260], PN1 [261], and PYT [262], the all-PSCs provided the PCEs of $9 \sim 1 3 \%$ . Notably, matching P303 with the star SM acceptors of Y6 series, the OSCs have achieved promising PCEs of up to $1 5 \sim 1 8 \%$ [263-265]. Compared to fluorine atom, chlorine atom is more easily introduced into photovoltaic materials by low-cost strategy [214]. Fan et al. developed another P302 derivative, namely PM7 (PBDB-TCl, P304) [243], by attaching a chlorine atom on 2D-conjugated thienyl substituents of polymer. Compared to the halogen-free P302, P304 showed lower HOMO level, higher absorption coefficient, enhanced crystallinity, and higher carrier mobility. Moreover, the P304:IT-4F-based OSCs achieved a high PCE of $1 3 . 1 \%$ , which was much higher than the P302:IT-4F-based ones $( 5 . 8 \% )$ . By combining the advantages of sulfur atom and fluorine atom substituents on thienyl BDT, Hou and coworkers synthesized a WBG polymer donor P305 with high absorption coefficient and deep HOMO level, and the corresponding P305:IT-4F-based OSCs also achieved a PCE more than $1 3 \%$ [244]. Introducing halogen atoms, such as fluorine and chlorine, on the 4-position of thiophene $\pi$ -bridges of P302, the synthesized polymers P307 [245] and P309 [246] exhibited deeper HOMO level and smaller bandgap of ${ \sim } 1 . 7 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ leading to improved photovoltaic performance in OsCs. Aiming to enhance the carrier transport ability, Qin et al. enlarged the 2D-conjugated side groups of P302 from thiophene to benzo[b]thiophen and synthesized a new polymer P310 [247]. Due to P310 had good solubility and enhanced aggregation effect in tetrahydrofuran (THF), the THF-processed P310:IT-M-based OSCs achieved a PCE of $1 2 . 1 0 \%$ . Liu et al. synthesized a series of PBDT-T derivatives, P311-P313 and found that the subtle atom changes in 2D-benzene on BDT unit can profound effect the electronic structure and self-assembly of polymers [248]. Among these polymers, P311 achieved a much higher PCE of $1 0 \%$ with a record FF of $8 0 . 5 \%$ in the $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ -based OSCs due to the formation of optimal interpenetrating network morphology. By further attaching two chlorine atoms on the thiophene $\pi$ -bridges of P311, an optimized WBG polymer donor P314 with a deeper HOMO level and improved crystallinity was synthesized by Ye et al. and achieved a higher PCE of $1 2 . 7 \%$ [249]. Moreover, Li et al. found that introducing fluorination on 2D-benzene on BDT unit also could significantly reduce the HOMO level of polymers, and the resulting WBG polymer donor P315 with 2D-conjugated alkoxyl-fluorophenyl side chains obtained an increased PCE of $1 1 . 7 \%$ in comparison with non-fluorinated P312 $( 6 . 2 \% )$ [250]. Xu et al. designed a WBG polymer donor P316 based on 2D-conjugated $m$ -alkoxyphenyl BDT and BDD units [251]. Matching with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ , the P316-based OSCs achieved a PCE of $8 . 4 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 5 \mathrm { V }$ Consequently, the photovoltaic performance of P316 in devices was further improved by pairing it with ITIC, and the related OSCs achieved a PCE of $1 0 . 8 \%$ [266].

In addition to optimizing 2D-conjugated groups on BDT unit and introducing halogen atoms into thiophene $\pi$ -bridges of P302, the modification of fused-ring building blocks of BDT and BDD units also have attracted great attentions. Chao et al. synthesized a new electron-withdrawing fused-ring building block of 2,3-bis(2-ethylhexyl)benzo[1,2-b:4,5- $c ^ { \prime }$ dithiophene-4,8-dione (TTDO) via the design of cyclohexane-1,4-dione embedded into a thieno[3,4-b]thiophene [267]. Then, by polymerizing TTDO with fluorinated thienyl BDT, they developed a WBG $\left( 1 . 8 0 \mathrm { e V } \right)$ polymer donor, P317. Blended with SM acceptor Y6, the P317-based OSCs obtained a PCE of $1 6 . 1 \%$ with a high FF of $7 7 . 1 \%$ . Compared to BDT unit, dithieno $[ 2 , 3 - d ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } - d ^ { \prime } ]$ ]benzo[1,2-b;4,5-b']dithiophene (DTBDT) with extended $\pi$ -conjugation and larger molecular planarity could effectively improve the charge carrier transport of the related photovoltaic materials. Inspired these, Huo et al. reported a WBG $( 1 . 8 5 \mathrm { e V } )$ polymer P318 by polymerizing an electron-rich DTBDT unit and an electron-deficient BDD unit [268]. P318 had a highly rigid backbone since both DTBDT and BDD units were rigid and planar, and its OSCs with a $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ acceptor achieved a high PCE of $9 . 7 \%$ , which was the highest value reported in the OSCs based on WBG polymer donors. By using NDT with extended $\pi$ -conjugation and larger molecular planarity as electron-donating unit, Peng and coworkers developed wBG polymer donors P319 and P320 for efficient OSCs [269, 270]. Compared to its analogous polymers (P302 and P306), P319 and P320 showed higher crystallinity and stronger aggregation, which induced large phase separation with poorer morphology. To optimize the morphology, P319 and P306 were blended with SM acceptor Y6-T for forming the ternary blend devices. As expected, the optimized ternary OSCs achieved a PCE as high as $1 6 . 5 7 \%$ . Ternary copolymerization strategies have proven advantageous in boosting the photovoltaic performance of OSCs [271]. Cui et al. reported a WBG terpolymer P321 by incorporating an electron-withdrawing unit of ester-substituted thiophene into polymer P303 to downshift molecular HOMO level and broaden absorption [272]. In the P321:IT-4F-based OSCs, a high PCE of $1 5 . 1 \%$ was obtained. Soon afterward, Sun et al. synthesized a fluorine and ester-functionalized thiophene (FE-T) with electron-withdrawing ability and then developed another WBG terpolymer donor P322 by incorporating FE-T as the third component into polymer P303 to fine-tune the energy levels and crystallinity [273]. Blending P322 with an SM acceptor Y6, the OSCs achieved a high PCE of $1 6 . 4 \%$ with a small $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ of $0 . 5 3 \mathrm { e V } .$ Moreover, by incorporating $1 \mathrm { m o l } \%$ concentration of iridium (Ir) complexes into the polymer-conjugated backbone of P303, Wang et al. developed a WBG terpolymer donor P323 [274]. The studies indicated that the introduction of small amount

Ir-complexes could rationally modify the molecular aggregations and carefully control the corresponding blend morphology and physical mechanisms. As a result, the P323:Y6-based OSCs delivered a high PCE of $1 7 . 3 2 \%$ , which was much better than that of the P303:Y6-based ones $( 1 5 . 3 9 \% )$ . The chemical structures of the polymer donors based on BDD derivatives are showed in Figure 1.39, and the corresponding photovoltaic parameters of OSCs are summarized in Table 1.30.

# 1.4.7 Other WBG Polymers

In addition to the above-summarized wBG polymers with some typical acceptor units, there still has many other building blocks employed to construct high-performance WBG polymer donors (Figure 1.40, Table 1.31). Cao et al. synthesized a fused pentacyclic aromatic lactam building block (thieno $[ 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } ; 5 , 6 ]$ pyrido[3,4-g]thieno[3,2-c]isoquinoline-5,11(4H,10H)-dione [TPTI]) with weak electron-withdrawing ability and then developed a D-A conjugated polymer donor P324 with a backbone of TPTI-alt-thiophene [275]. P324 possessed a WBG $( 1 . 8 6 \mathrm { e V } )$ and a deep HOMO level, and the corresponding $\mathrm { P } 3 2 4 { \mathrm { : P C } } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ -based OSCs afforded an outstanding PCE up to $7 . 8 0 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 7 \mathrm { V } ,$ which was one of the best PCEs in OSCs based on WBG polymer donor. Liao et al. reported a series of readily accessible and scalable polymer donors (P325-P328) with a backbone of BDT-alt-2,5-dithienyl TPD for application in OSCs blended with IT-4F [276]. All polymers readily dissolved in non-chlorinated solvents, and the corresponding active layers could be processed in ambient from xylene as solvent to fabricate OSCs with PCEs of $12 \sim 1 4 \%$ In the P328:IT-4F-based OSC modules processed in ambient from a benign solvent, a certified PCE of $1 0 . 1 \%$ for a device area of $2 0 . 4 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ was achieved. Moreover, the same module also delivered a power of ${ \sim } 4 0 \mu \mathrm { W } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ (PCE $\sim 2 2 \%$ ) under indoor lighting. Liu et al. designed a fused building block of 5H-dithieno ${ \ : } 3 , 2 { \cdot } b { : } 2 { ^ { \prime } } , 3 { ^ { \prime } } { \cdot }$ d]pyran-5-one with weak electron-withdrawing ability and then synthesized a polymer donor P329 with a WBG of $1 . 9 6 \mathrm { e V }$ and a deep HOMO level of $- 5 . 4 5 \mathrm { e V }$ [277]. Blending P329 with Y6, the OSCs provided a PCE over $1 4 \%$ . To fully exploit the potential of P329 series polymers, Ding and coworkers developed another WBG polymer donor P330 with a thiolactone unit of 5H-dithieno $[ 3 , 2 - b ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } ]$ d]thiopyran-5-one [278]. From P229 to P330, the simple replacement of lactone with thiolactone enhanced molecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking, gifting P330 a higher hole mobility. When matched with Y6, its OSCs gave a high PCE up to $1 6 . 7 2 \%$ . The mechanism that how noncovalent conformation locked to improve the photovoltaic performance of WBG polymer donors was also investigated. By developing a model system with three structure-related polymers P331-P333, a clear correlation was found between the locking strength in polymer backbone and the photovoltaic performance [279]. Among three polymers, P331 with the strongest S. . -O and F. . .H double-side locking showed improved planarity, packing, crystallinity, and hole mobility compared to these of P332 with a S. : .O single-side locking and P333 with a weakened $\mathrm { { s } \cdot \cdot \mathrm { { o } } }$ locking caused by Cl-H steric repulsion, which gave the highest PCE of $1 6 . 2 3 \%$ in the P331:Y6-based OSCs, while the OSCs based on P332:Y6 and P333:Y6 achieved PCEs of $1 1 . 7 3 \%$ and $0 . 9 2 \%$ , respectively. He and coworkers reported a new electron-deficient monomer naphthalenothiophene imide (NTI) and NTI-based copolymer P334 [280]. The strong electron-withdrawing ability of NTI could effectively lower the HOMO level of the polymer $( - 5 . 5 2 \mathrm { e V } )$ The polymer chain modification resulted in the closed $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking and ordered polymer packing of P334 and was proven to be an effective strategy to increase the device performance. OsC devices for P334:Y6 exhibited an efficiency of $1 6 . 7 2 \%$ which was further enhanced to $1 7 . 3 5 \%$ by the third component $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$

# 1.5 Summary and Outlook

In this part, we have summarized several representative types of LBG, MBG, and WBG polymer donors and discussed the relationship between the chemical structures and the optical, electronic, and device performance. With the rapid development of non-fullerene acceptors, the number of publications of LBG and MBG polymers is far behind than WBG polymers in recent years, but it is undeniable that LBG and MBG polymers have made great contributions to the field of OSCs. Although WBG polymers have dominated the high performance in the current fullerene-free PSCs, LBG and MBG polymer donors will continue play an important role in OSCs, especially in semi-transparent, ternary, and tandem devices.

# $\pmb { p }$ -Type Molecular Photovoltaic Materials

Qihui $\gamma _ { U e ^ { 1 , 2 } }$ and Xiaozhang Zhu1,2

1 Chinese Academy of Sciences, Institute of Chemistry, Beijing National Laboratory for Molecular Sciences, CAS Key Laboratory of Organic Solids, Zhongguancun North First Street 2, Haidian District, Beijing 100190, P.R. China   
2University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Yuquan Road No. 19(A), Shijingshan District, Beijing 100049, P.R. China

# 2.1 Introduction

Organic solar cells (OsCs) have unique advantages such as light weight, flexibility, diverse material choices, and large-area processability and have received wide attention in recent years [1-3]. The research on active layer materials is the key and basis of the boost of OSCs. According to the type of active layer materials, OSCs can be divided into polymer type (PSCs) and small-molecule type (SMSCs). Compared with polymers, small molecules have distinct characteristics: (i) the well-defined molecular structure with definite molecular weight that avoids batch-to-batch problems, ensuring the device performance reproducibility, benefiting the understanding of structure-property relationship; (ii) the synthesis simplicity that makes the structure highly controllable; and (ii) the strong crystallinity that brings a high mobility, which is conducive to charge transport [4, 5]. The research on SMSCs can be traced back to 1959 [6]. Anthracene crystal was sandwiched between two electrodes, but due to the poor exciton dissociation, the device gave a low power conversion efficiency (PCE). Then, Tang reported a planar heterojunction (PHJ) device, which was the key breakthrough, in which copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) and perylenetetracarboxylic bis-benzimidazole (PTCBI) were vacuum-deposited layer by layer [7]. In this device, excitons were dissociated at the interface of the two layers, and PCE reached $1 . 0 \%$ , indicating that the combination of electron donors and electron acceptors could effectively increase the exciton dissociation and thus the PCEs. Since then, the development of $p$ -type and $n$ -type molecular photovoltaic materials, also called small-molecule donor materials (SMDs) and small-molecule acceptor materials (SMAs), has been a primary issue in SMSCs. In the early stage, researchers mainly developed materials, especially SMDs, for vacuum-deposited small-molecule solar cells (VD-SMsCs). These materials often exhibited good thermal stability and proper molecular weight. Then, since bulk heterojunction (BHJ) structure that could greatly increase the interface area between the donor and acceptor and benefit the exciton dissociation was proposed, solution-processed PSCs have developed rapidly [8]. However, for solution-processed small-molecule solar cells (SP-SMSCs), the poor film-forming property and low solubility as well as the low molar absorption coefficients of traditional SMDs limited the development, and much effort has been devoted to overcome these shortcomings and great progress was achieved. In the research of SMsCs based on fullerene acceptors, PCEs of over $1 0 \%$ have been realized in both VD- and SP-SMSCs [9-13]. Later, high-performance nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) promoted the PCEs of SP-SMSCs to over $1 5 \%$ [14-18].

In this chapter, some representative SMDs used in fullerene-based SMSCs will be introduced, including their design, photoelectronic property, and photovoltaic performance. Current progress on SMSCs based on NFAs will also be stated. Finally, aiming at the future of SMsCs, challenges and possibility will be discussed.

# 2.2 $\pmb { p }$ -Type Molecular Photovoltaic Materials Used in Vacuum-Deposited Solar Cells

Vacuum deposition refers to the process of vaporizing the material with thermal evaporation in vacuum, then depositing the material onto the substrate. This also reflects the requirements of materials used: suitable molecular weight and considerable thermal stability. Utilizing vacuum deposition has unique advantages: (i) VD-SMSCs can take advantage of the mature technology of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) but the requirements for the mask need not to be so harsh; (ii) the film formation is simple, especially for multilayer devices. And the organic solvent use and liquid waste treatment can be avoided; (iii) the thickness of the active layers and interlayers can be precisely controlled, even with a thickness of only a few nanometers; (iv) the film morphology can be well controlled by regulating the deposition conditions; (v) the film is of good quality with high purity, compactness, and reproducibility, favoring high and steady performance; and (vi) good device stability can be expected [19].

In VD-SMSCs, fullerenes $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ and $\mathrm { C } _ { 7 0 }$ as acceptors significantly improved the PCE because of their great thermal stability, high electron affinity, strong aggregation, as well as high electron mobility. The device structure optimization, such as BHJ and planar-mixed heterojunction (PM-HJ) structures, also did contribution. Nowadays, VD-SMSCs have realized PCEs of over $1 0 \%$ [9-11], and it deserves to be mentioned that Heliatek GmbH, which devotes much to the organic photovoltaic commercialization, announced a multijunction VD-SMSC with a high PCE of $1 3 . 2 \%$ in 2016 [20]. Among the various SMDs, oligothiophenes (OTs), $\mathrm { D - A { - } A ^ { \prime } }$ type SMDs (D and A represent electron-donating and -accepting moieties, representatively), borondipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) are the most common, which will be described in detail.

# 2.2.1 Oligothiophene-Based Molecular Donors

Thiophene is an electron-rich unit and OT derivatives are widely used in organic optoelectronic devices due to the great charge transport property. Quinoidization and D-A strategies can easily tune the photoelectronic properties of OT-based SMDs.

In A-D-A-type OTs, the push-pull effect between D and A can enhance the intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) effect and red-shift the absorption, favoring a high short-circuit current density $( J _ { \mathrm { s c } } )$ , and the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) or the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy levels can be controlled separately by changing D or A, respectively, favoring for a high open-circuit voltage $( V _ { \mathrm { o c } } )$ , and the side chains can greatly influence the molecular stacking in the thin film. One representative material, DCv5T-Bu2,2,4,4 with $n$ -butyl-substituted quinquethiophene as D and dicyanovinyl (DCV) as A (the number in subscript indicates the substituent's position), was reported by Bauerle and coworkers [21]. It exhibited an optical bandgap $( E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } )$ of $1 . 7 7 \mathrm { e V }$ in the solid state and well-matched energy levels with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , yielding an outstanding PCE of $3 . 4 \%$ in the device, which was further promoted to $5 . 8 0 \%$ through buffer layer engineering [22]. To investigate the structure-property relationship more detailly, efforts were devoted to varying the conjugation length, and the side chain. Research on the terminal effect was also executed [23].

Pfeiffer and coworkers reported DCVnTs-Bu $\mathit { \Delta } _ { \mathcal { n } } = 3 _ { 2 , 2 }$ $4 _ { 1 , 1 , 4 , 4 }$ $5 _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ $6 _ { 2 , 2 , 5 , 5 } )$ [22]. With the conjugation length increasing, LUmO energy level fluctuated tinnily but HOMO energy level was significantly upshifted, which might lead to a decrease in $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ but more efficient charge generation. $\mathrm { D C V } 3 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { B u } _ { 2 , 2 }$ -based and DCV4T- $\mathrm { \cdot B u } _ { 1 , 1 , 4 , 4 }$ -based devices gave poor PCEs, while the other two devices showed small differences in $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and fill factor (FF), but the high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of DCV5T- $\mathtt { B u } _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ -based device led to its best PCE of $5 . 8 0 \%$ . Bauerle designed DCVnTs $\begin{array} { r } { n = 1 - 6 , } \end{array}$ without any side chain [24]. With the $n$ increasing, maximum absorptions red-shifted, accompanied with enhanced molar extinction coefficients. Since the energy levels of DCVnTs ( $n = 4 – 6$ were well matched with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , they were chosen to fabricate PHJ devices, and PCEs of $1 . 2 \%$ $2 . 6 \%$ $2 . 8 \%$ were realized, respectively. By using BHJ device structure, the PCE of DCv5T-based device was promoted to $5 . 2 \%$ . Bridging the thiophenes of DCV3T with nitrogen atoms offered DCV-SN5-1, -2, and $^ { - 3 }$ among which the difference was the substituent on the nitrogen (propyl/hexyl/tolyl) [25]. DCV-SN5 SMDs exhibited decreased $E _ { \mathbf { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ and increased molar extinction coefficients because of the planarization and rigidification of the central core, but DCV-SN5-3 exhibited a weaker and blue-shifted absorption compared with the other two, which was due to a distortion between the bulky substituent and the backbone. In blends, DCV-SN5-1-based one exhibited the most obvious interconnected networks, benefiting charge transport and leading to the best PCE of $6 . 5 \%$ . Linking two methyl and two ethyl groups on the terminal thiophenes of DCV4T, DCV4T-Me, and -Et were offered [26]. DCV4T-Me showed the most obvious red-shift between the absorptions of solution and film, indicating its better ordering in the film. Its single crystal showed the best coplanarity with strong $\pi { - } \pi$ interactions while in the blend, DCV4T-Me could form a crystalline homo-phase with similar molecular packing, leading to a high PCE of $3 . 8 \%$ . Based on $\mathrm { D C V } 5 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { B u } _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ , by replacing the $n$ butyl with ethyl, $\mathrm { D C V } 5 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { E t } _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ had similar photoelectronic properties but lower hole mobility, leading to a lower PCE of $2 . 5 \%$ [27]. While replacing with methyl and regulating their position and number, DCV5T- $\mathsf { M e } ( _ { 1 , 1 , 5 , 5 } , _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ and $_ { 3 , 3 }$ were obtained [28]. Comparing the absorptions between the solutions and films, red-shifted maximum absorption peaks $\left( 5 0 - 7 2 \mathrm { n m } \right)$ were observed, among which the red-shift of $\mathrm { D C V } 5 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { M e } _ { 3 , 3 }$ was most obvious, indicating its highly ordered stacking. From the DCV5T- $\mathrm { M e } _ { 1 , 1 , 5 , 5 }$ to $\mathbf { \bar { \mathbf { \rho } } } _ { - \mathrm { M } \mathbf { e } _ { 3 , 3 } }$ -based blend films, crystallites of both donor and acceptor became bigger and phase separation became larger, favoring charge transport, and the PCE was promoted from $4 . 8 \%$ to $6 . 9 \%$ with significantly increased $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ . And based on $\mathrm { D C V } 5 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { M e } _ { 3 , 3 }$ , a record PCE of $9 . 7 \%$ was realized in a triple-junction homo-tandem device [29]. DCV6T- $\mathrm { E t } _ { 2 , 2 , 5 , 5 }$ and $\mathtt { - B u } _ { 1 , 2 , 5 , 6 }$ were both derived from $\mathrm { D C V } 6 \mathrm { T } { \cdot } \mathrm { B u } _ { 2 , 2 , 5 , 5 }$ giving PCEs of $3 . 8 \%$ and $4 . 9 \%$ , respectively [30, 31]. It is worth noting that heat substrate was needed during the fabrication of the devices above, aiming at the formation of better phase separation.

Another type is $\alpha$ OT. $\scriptstyle { \mathtt { a } } \mathrm { - } 6 \mathrm { T }$ is one of the most representative examples. $\alpha$ 6T exhibited high-lying energy levels, therefore, when it was matched with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ with a low-lying LUMO energy level, due to the large energy offsets and limited absorption, the performance was not ideal, with a PCE of only $1 . 5 \%$ in the PHJ device [32].

OT-based SMDs (as shown in Figure 2.1 and Table 2.1) perform quite well in VD-SMSCs; however, the main weakness is that the film needs to be quite thin, otherwise FF will suffer. Therefore, the mobility should be increased to ensure that the active layer can harvest sufficient light while having little effect on FF.

# 2.2.2 D-A-A'-Type Molecular Donors

In $\mathrm { D - A { - } A ^ { \prime } }$ -type SMDs, ICT effect can be adjusted to a desired degree by manipulating the three groups. These SMDs exhibit relatively large dipole moments along the backbone and tend to stack into an antiparallel dimeric configuration parallel to the substrate, facilitating charge hopping and vertical charge transport. In the blends, favorable phase separation can be formed due to the homo-aggregation of these SMDs.

In 2011, Wong and coworkers designed DTDCTB, in which the dihedral angle between the thiophene of diarylaminothienyl and benzothiadiazole (BT) units was only $5 . 5 ^ { \circ }$ , indicating the good coplanarity and enhancing the ICT [33]. The absorption of DTDCTB was extended to the near-infrared (NIR) region, greatly increasing the light harvest. And due to the strong electron-withdrawing ability of BT and DCV units, a low-lying HOMO energy level was observed, favoring a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . The relevant PM-HJ device achieved a PCE of $5 . 8 1 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 7 9 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 4 . 6 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an FF of 0.50. Using a BHJ structure, an improved PCE of $8 . 0 \%$ was given [34]. Further applying it as the front cell in a triple-junction device that contains two $\mathrm { D B P : C _ { 7 0 } }$ -based subcells, a PCE of $1 1 . 1 \%$ was achieved [9]. Modifying the diarylaminothienyl unit, DPDCTB, DTDCPB, and DPDCPB were obtained [35]. Compared with DTDCTB, DTDCPB with diarylaminophenyl as D unit exhibited a highly distorted conformation with a dihedral angle of $2 4 . 7 ^ { \circ }$

/td></tr></table>

Due to the electron-rich nature and the better quinoidal propensity of thiophene, DPDCTB and DTDCTB showed red-shifted absorptions and higher lying HOMO energy levels compared with DPDCPB and DTDCPB, respectively. Also, due to the strong electron-donating ability of $p$ -tolyl, DTDCPB and DTDCTB exhibited red-shifted absorptions and higher lying HOMO energy levels compared with DPDCPB and DPDCTB, respectively. Ultimately, DTDCPB-based device obtained a balance between $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , delivering the highest PCE of $6 . 8 \%$ . By further optimizing the device structure, DTDCPB-based device achieved an outstanding PCE of $9 . 6 \%$ [34]. Combining it with a solution-processed cell, an excellent PCE of $1 5 \%$ was stated [36]. Wong and coworkers also reported series SMDs DTCPB, DTCTB, DTCPBO, and DPCTBO with cyano as terminal [37]. Due to the weaker electron-withdrawing ability of cyano, the LUMO energy levels were upshifted; meanwhile, the ICT effects were reduced, leading to blue-shifted absorptions and lower extinction coefficients. Compared with DTCPB and DTCTB, DTCPBO and DPCTBO exhibited red-shifted absorptions and lower-lying LUMO energy levels, attributed to the stronger electron deficient property of their A units. DTCPB-based blend showed the most suitable nanomorphology, reducing the recombination and demonstrating the highest FF, $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , and PCE $( 6 . 5 5 \% )$ in the device.

Coplanar dithienopyrrole (DTP) as D unit has also been introduced into this type of SMDs. Due to the lack of nitrogen contributions to the conjugated backbones, blue-shifted absorptions were observed, but larger absorption coefficients could compensate the light harvest loss. Linking $p$ -tolyl substituted DTP with pyrimidine (PM)-DCV and BT-DCV, respectively, TDPM and TDBT were obtained, between which TDBT exhibited a smaller $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ and a higher-lying HOMO energy level [38]. The relevant devices gave similar $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } \mathbf { s }$ and FFs, but the higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of TDPM-based one led to a higher PCE of $5 . 5 \%$ . Later, two isomers antiBTDC and synBTDC were offered by fusing a benzene ring with DTP and linking it with BT-DCV [39]. antiBTDC had a longer effective conjugation length, a smaller dihedral angle, and a smaller intermolecular interfacial distance and exhibited a cofacial $\pi$ stacking that made each D unit be close to an A unit in the dimer, leading to a more homogeneous electron density distribution. These facilitated intra- and intermolecular charge transfer, leading to a red-shifted absorption with an enhanced extinction coefficient and a higher-lying HOmO energy level. Also, the strong $\pi { - } \pi$ interactions and the diminished molecular dipole of antiBTDC could facilitate the charge transport. The device based on antiBTDC delivered a PCE of $7 . 2 \%$ , with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 1 \mathrm { V } _ { : }$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 4 . 2 \mathrm { m A } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an FF of 0.56. To further increase the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ , PYDC was designed by replacing the BT with PM, based on which the device gave a PCE of $5 . 1 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 6 \mathrm { V } .$ Starting from antiBTDC and varying the substituents offered iBuBTDC and nBuBTDC [40]. The two SMDs showed greater coplanarity and stacked more compactly, and such high stacking densities contributed to higher absorption coefficients. However, the orthogonal stack mode of nBuBTDC hindered the intermolecular charge transfer. nBuBTDC-based device exhibited comparable performance to antiBTDC-based one, while iBuBTDC-based one achieved a PCE of $9 . 3 \%$ with a higher FF of 0.60, attributed to the high ratio of face-on $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking. Recently, bi-ternary devices with two BHJ layers: DTDCPB $\mathrm { C } _ { 7 0 }$ and $i \mathrm { B u B T D C } { : } \mathrm { C } _ { 7 0 }$ were constructed, achieving a PCE of $1 0 \%$ [11].

Molecular structures and performance parameters were shown in Figure 2.2 and Table 2.2. This type of SMDs often show higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } \mathbf { S }$ due to the smaller $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ , and the device performance has a great correlation with the molecular stacking, phase separation, as well as the device structure. The improvement of FFs is a focus and increasing hole mobility to realize more balanced carrier transport is favorable.

# 2.2.3 Borondipyrromethenes-Based Molecular Donors

BODIPYs exhibit a variety of modification positions, making the photoelectronic property highly tunable, and they show strong NIR absorptions and delocalized molecular orbitals, making them promising photovoltaic molecular donors.

$\mathrm { P h } _ { 2 }$ -benz-BODIPY is a typical example, and its absorption could reach $9 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ And it gave PCEs of $3 . 8 \%$ and $2 . 3 \%$ in the opaque and semitransparent devices, respectively [41, 42]. To make better use of NIR light, Leo and coworkers extended the conjugation length, introduced trifluoromethyl, and synthesized BDP-H, BDP-Me, BDP-OMe [10]. Because of the stronger electron-donating ability from hydrogen to methyl and to methoxyl, solution absorptions were red-shifted, while in the solid state, the absorptions were obviously broadened and red-shifted, indicating the ordered stacking. BDP-H and BDP-OMe had more $J$ -aggregation characters, but BDP-Me was more $H$ -aggregated. BDP-OMe performed best in the device with a PCE of $6 . 1 \%$ , attributed to the enough interfaces and interpenetrating pathways in the blend, and when the device was matched with DCV5T $\mathbf { \cdot } \mathbf { M } \mathbf { e } _ { 3 , 3 }$ -based device in series, a PCE of $1 0 \%$ was achieved. Modifying BDP-OMe by replacing the trifluoromethyl with perfluorinated ethyl and $n$ -propyl, BDP-2, and BDP-3 were obtained with $J$ -aggregation characters [43]. They showed similar absorptions and energy levels, but because of the favorable morphology in the BDP-2-based blend, the device delivered a higher PCE of $6 . 4 \%$ . To investigate the effect of aggregation mode on the performance, BDP- $\cdot \mathrm { H } ^ { \prime }$ and BDP-J were designed [44]. They showed similar solution absorptions and energy levels, but in the solid films, BDP. $\cdot \mathrm { H } ^ { \prime }$ was more $H$ -aggregated while BDP-J preferred $J$ -aggregation. In the devices, BDP-J-based one gave a PCE of $4 . 2 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 0 \mathrm { V }$ while BDP- $\cdot \mathrm { H } ^ { \prime }$ -based one gave a PCE of $5 . 5 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 3 \mathrm { V } .$ It was noting that BDP-J-based device exhibited a high external quantum efficiency (EQE) even at a small driving force $( 0 . 1 7 \mathrm { e V } )$ and a lower nonradiative energy loss $( 0 . 3 2 \mathrm { e V } )$

From Table 2.3, it can be found that these SMDs exhibit small $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ , making them promising candidates for the rear cell of a tandem device [10]. However, the $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } \mathbf { s }$ are not satisfactory, and the FFs also need to be improved, which need further optimization on molecular structure, morphology, and device engineering.

Merocyanines (MCs) are typical D-A-type dyes and the photoelectronic property as well as the molecular dipole moment strongly depend on the length of the polymethine chain and the kind of the D and A moieties. To compare the difference between VD- and SP-SMsCs based on MCs, Wurthner and coworkers utilized HB194, of which the maximum absorption peak was at $6 1 6 \mathrm { n m }$ , to match with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ and $\mathrm { P C } _ { 6 0 } \mathrm { B M }$ to construct BHJ OSCs, respectively [45]. Since $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ exhibited a higher electron affinity and slower growth conditions during the vacuum deposition led to more aggregation, the VD-SMSC gave a lower $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ but a higher PCE of $4 . 5 \%$ (compared with the PCE of $3 \%$ in the SP-SMSC), attributed to the favorable blend morphology. Further optimizing the device structure and the ratio of donor and acceptor, the PCE was promoted to $6 . 1 \%$ with simultaneously increased parameters [46]. To investigate the effect of the buffer layers on the performance, the same group compared the performance of $\mathrm { H B } 3 6 4 / \mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ -based PHJ devices with ${ \bf V } _ { 2 } { \bf O } _ { 5 }$ $\mathbf { M o O } _ { 3 }$ and ${ \mathrm { W O } } _ { 3 }$ buffer layers. ${ \bf V } _ { 2 } { \bf O } _ { 5 }$ layer could induce a high degree of crystallization of HB364, leading to the highest $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and FF and the PCE $( 2 . 7 \% )$ [47]. Besides, they utilized $\mathrm { I D } 5 8 3 / \mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ PHJ devices to explore the molecular orientation's effect on the performance by differing the substrate temperature [48]. ID583 preferred to stand along their long axis perpendicular to the substrate, however, when the substrate was heated at a temperature above the glass transition temperature, they tended to align their long molecular axes along $4 5 ^ { \circ }$ relative to the surface. The latter orientation improved the exciton dissociation, leading to a better performance.

Phthalocyanines (PCs) demonstrated excellent thermal stability and high absorptions, making them promising candidates for VD-SMSCs. For metal-containing PCs, copper, and zinc are most common centers, based on which the SMDs exhibit an $1 8 ~ \pi$ -electrons coplanar structure. Forrest and coworkers constructed a PHJ device based on CuPc and $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , which delivered a PCE of $3 . 6 \%$ [49]. Riede and coworkers found that in $Z _ { \mathrm { n } } \mathrm { P c } { : } \mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ -based BHJ devices, the hot substrate was favorable for the formation of phase separation, contributing to a high PCE of $3 \%$ (compared with the PCE of $1 . 4 \%$ obtained in the device based on a room-temperature substrate) [50]. To obtain a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ , the same group designed $\mathrm { F _ { 4 } Z n P c }$ by introducing four fluorine atoms into ZnPc to downshift the HOMO energy level, based on which the device gave comparable $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF but a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 6 9 \mathrm { V } _ { : }$ leading to a better PCE of $4 . 6 \%$ [51]. However, further fluorination did not lead to an improved PCE due to the unfavorable morphology or the unmatched energy level [56]. On the other hand, SubPc, which is a $1 4 \pi$ -electrons aromatic macrocycle containing a boron core and a nonplanar cone-shaped structure with the tetrahedral boron center out of plane with the aromatic ligand, is one of the most representative metal-free PCs. Compared with CuPc and $\mathrm { z n P c }$ , the lower-lying HOMO energy level of SubPc favored a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ The $\mathrm { S u b P c / C _ { 6 0 } }$ -based PHJ cell gave a PCE of $2 . 1 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of approximately $_ { 1 \mathrm { V } }$ and the PCE could be promoted to $4 . 5 \%$ after device structure optimization [52, 53]. However, the absorption of SubPc was in the range of $4 5 0 { \mathrm { - } } 6 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , therefore, to increase the light utilization, $\pi$ -extended SubNc was designed, based on which a PCE of $2 . 5 \%$ with an enhanced $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ was obtained [54].

There are other SMDs that also realized nice performance in the VD-SMSCs. For example, DBP-based BHJ device demonstrated a PCE of $7 . 4 \%$ [34], and TAPC-based device delivered a PCE of $5 . 2 3 \%$ even at a low donor concentration of $5 \%$ [55].

# 2.3 $\pmb { p }$ -Type Molecular Photovoltaic Materials Used in Solution-Processed Solar Cells

After the proposal of BHJ structure, solution-processing became a new trend in the fabrication of OsCs [8]. The solution-processing method refers to forming a thin film on the substrate by spin-, blade-coating, or slot-die printing with material solutions. Compared with VD-SMSCs, SP-OSCs developed more rapidly because of the large material base (both small molecules and polymers) and the simple and low-cost fabrication process. However, due to the poor film-forming property of traditional small molecules, SP-sMsCs developed slowly. In recent years, through proper molecular design, morphology control, and device optimization, SP-sMsCs have achieved rapid progress. This section will focus on the solution-processed $p$ -type molecular photovoltaic materials and introduce the molecular design and the device results.

In the early stage, the match of soluble PCs and hexabenzocoronene with perylenes was reported, but the performance was much worse than the polymer systems [57, 58]. Since then, there had been few related reports. Until 2006, star-shaped OTs appeared, of which the structure could increase the intermolecular interaction and obtain a high mobility, but the final performance was not ideal (PCE of $1 \%$ ) due to the limited absorption and poor phase separation [59, 60]. Polycyclic arenes were also reported, but the similar problems limited the performance [61]. To improve the light utilization, D-A strategy was used. The early D-A molecules have been summarized in some excellent reviews [62, 63]. Some representative high-performance SMDs, including A-D-A-, D1-A-D2-A-D1- and porphyrin molecules, will be introduced in detail.

# 2.3.1  A-D-A-Type Molecular Donors

As mentioned above, D-A strategy is an effective way to reduce $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ to improve the sunlight utilization. Based on the same strategy, solution-processible donors are designed and synthesized. With regulation of the moieties including $\mathrm { D } / \mathrm { A }$ moiety, $\pi$ -linker and side chain, molecular solubility, photoelectronic properties, and stacking can be well adjusted. By optimizing the design of the A-D-A-type SMDs, coupled with device engineering, the related SMSCs have achieved PCEs of over $1 0 \%$ [12, 13].

# 2.3.1.1 Oligothiophene-Based A-D-A-Type Molecular Donors

Starting from DCV5T- $\mathtt { B u } _ { 2 , 2 , 4 , 4 }$ , Chen and coworkers introduced $n$ -octyl side chains to offer DCN3T, DCN5T, and DCN7T [64, 65]. With increased conjugation length, the upshifted HOMO energy levels and the red-shifted absorptions were observed. DCN7T-based device gave a PCE of $3 . 7 0 \%$ with a poor FF of 0.34, which was due to the large phase separation. To further increase the solubility, cyanoacetate derivatives were used to offer DCAE7T, DCAO7T, and DCAEH7T, which all delivered PCEs of over $4 \%$ [66]. The significant improvements on FF were attributed to the improved morphology. Chen and coworkers also attempted many A moieties: when 3-ethylrhodanine (RD), a moiety with a stronger electron-accepting ability, was applied, DERHD7T showed a smaller $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 9 \mathrm { e V }$ compared with DCAO7T. And the device obtained a PCE of $6 . 1 0 \%$ with a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 3 . 9 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ [67]. Using dicyanomethylene group to replace thio group in RD, DRCN7T showed a red-shifted absorption and more ordered stacking in the film, and the PCE reached a record of $9 . 3 0 \%$ , with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 1 \mathrm { V } _ { : }$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 4 . 8 7 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.69 [68]. Further enhancing the electron-accepting ability of A unit, several SMDs with smaller $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ were obtained, but the performance varied from $0 . 6 \%$ to $5 \%$ [69]. In addition, examples of barbiturate as the A unit were reported, but the performance was not ideal [7o]. These results indicated that photoelectronic properties can be effectively adjusted by regulating A moiety; however, the energy-level alignment and the blend morphology are also in great correlation to the final performance.

The adjustment of the central core is also of great importance. To investigate the influence of the conjugation length and spatial symmetry on the photoelectronic properties and the performance, based on DRCN7T, Chen and coworkers designed DRCNnT $\mathit { n } = 4 { - } 9$ , where $n$ is the number of thiophene [12]. Compared with DRCN4T, DRCN5T-9T showed the same absorption peaks at $5 3 0 \mathrm { n m }$ in solution, indicating that the quinquethiophene backbone had reached the effective conjugation length. However, in solid state, red-shifted absorptions with various patterns were observed, which was due to the different molecular stacking. DRCN5T showed a broader absorption with an obvious shoulder peak, indicating more effective molecular stacking. With the increase in $n$ , these SMDs exhibited similar LUMO but upshifted HOMO energy levels. DRCN4T-based device only gave a low PCE of $0 . 2 4 \%$ due to the poor film-forming property, while DRCN5T-9T-based devices all achieved good results, among which the DRCN5T-based one delivered a champion PCE of $1 0 . 0 8 \%$ . And devices based on axisymmetric DRCN5/7/9T showed higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } \mathbf { s }$ due to the larger dipole moment differences between the ground state and the excited state $( \Delta \mu _ { \mathrm { g e } } )$ , which could lower the Coulombic binding energy of the exciton and facilitate charge dissociation. Besides, the introduction of substituents or new structural units is also an important aspect in the core adjustment. To investigate the effect of fluorination on the properties, Peng and coworkers designed TTH-D3TRh and TTF-D3TRh, among which TTF-D3TRh with fluorine atoms showed a deeper HOmO energy level, more favorable molecular stacking and a higher mobility, leading to a higher PCE [71]. Zhu and coworkers reported STDR-TbT by introducing a thieno[3,4 $^ { b }$ |thiophene (T34bT)-based moiety into OT core [72]. Due to the quinoidization effect of T34bT, STDR-TbT showed a reduced $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 0 \mathrm { e V }$ compared with OT core-based STDR $( E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 7 0 \mathrm { e V } )$ This increased light absorption, bringing a higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and PCE. Units like furan, selenophene and thieno[3,2-b]thiophene $( \mathrm { T } 3 2 b \mathrm { T } )$ were also widely used to replace thiophene [73, 74].

Molecular structures and performance parameters of OT-based A-D-A-type SMDs mentioned above are showed in Figure 2.5 and Table 2.5. They exhibit wide $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ and when matched with fullerenes, the devices often give high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } \mathrm { s }$ but there is room for $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF improvement, which needs proper molecular design and device engineering.

# 2.3.1.2 Benzodithiophene-Based A-D-A-Type Molecular Donors

Benzodithiophene (BDT) with a large conjugated plane, good planar symmetry, and superior charge transport property is a popular unit used in SMDs. Design strategies on BDT-based A-D-A-type SMDs (Figure 2.6) are analyzed as follows.

Modification on BDT Modification on BDT unit includes the side chain engineering and the backbone adjustment, which will affect not only the solubility but also the photoelectronic properties and the molecular stacking.

Chen and coworkers linked alkoxy, alkyl, and alkylthio to BDT to offer DR3TBDT, DR3TDOBDT, and DR3TSBDT [75-77]. They showed strong absorptions with obvious shoulder peaks in the range of $3 5 0 \mathrm { - } 7 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , indicating good molecular stacking. The device based on DR3TBDT gave a PCE of $7 . 3 8 \%$ [75]. Due to the weaker electron-donating ability of alkyl/alkylthio, HOMO energy levels of DR3TDOBDT and DR3TSBDT were deepened, leading to increased $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } \mathbf { s } .$ Through thermal annealing (TA) and solvent vapor annealing(SVA), interpenetrating networks were formed, benefiting exciton diffusion and charge transport, and the devices realized PCEs of $8 . 2 6 \%$ and $9 . 9 5 \%$ , respectively [76, 77]. It is worth noting that the DR3TSBDT-based one could achieve a PCE of $8 \%$ even at a thickness of $3 7 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , attributed to its improved crystallinity. To form better $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking and facilitate charge transport, it is effective to introduce conjugated side chains to make the $\pi$ -electrons delocalized. Based on DR3TBDT, Chen and coworkers reported DR3TBDTT, DR3TBDTT-HD, and DR3TBDT2T with thiophene or bithiophene-based chains on BDT [78]. They showed similar absorptions and energy levels with DR3TBDT. And the device based on DR3TBDTT gave the best PCE of $8 . 1 2 \%$ , which could be further improved to $9 . 5 8 \%$ with SVA of ${ \mathrm { C S } } _ { 2 }$ [79]. Moreover, when DR3TBDTT-E was added into this binary system, a PCE up to $1 0 . 0 2 \%$ was achieved [80]. The DR3TBDTT-HD-based device showed a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ due to the weakened intermolecular interaction led by the bulky long chains, and DR3TBDT2T-based device delivered a nice FF, attributed to the enhanced $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking. Using alkoxy-, and alkylthio-thienyl is also feasible, reaching PCEs of $6 { - } 9 \%$ [81, 82]. Compared with DR3TBDTT, DR3TBDTTF with fluorinated side chains exhibited a deeper HOMO energy level and enhanced crystallinity, favoring $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ elevation and charge transport, and realized a PCE of $9 . 2 4 \%$ which, after SVA, was promoted to $9 . 8 0 \%$ [83]. Chen and coworkers also introduced alkyl/alkylthio-substituted $\mathrm { T } 3 2 b \mathrm { T }$ as side chains to get DRBDT-TT and DRBDT-STT, which both gave PCEs of over $8 \%$ [84]. A nematic liquid crystalline SMD, BTR, with $n$ -hexyl-substituted alkylthienyl side chains was also reported, which achieved a PCE of $9 . 3 \%$ [85]. And even at a thickness of $4 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , PCE remained $8 \%$

![](images/2289342b752c8e526f3c605ee3efeee252543997ae13b57809323753bd995c49.jpg)  
Figure 2.6Molecular structures of the BDT-based A-D-A-type SMDs. Source: Qihui Yue.

Dithienobenzodithiophene (DTBDT) and naphthodithiophene (NDT) derived from BDT are also popular cores. The extended conjugation backbone can enhance the planarity and $\pi { - } \pi$ interactions, favoring charge delocalization and transport, leading to good photovoltaic performance [86, 87].

Design of the $\pmb { \pi }$ Linkers The design of $\pi$ -linker also includes the substituent change and the structural variation, which in turn affects the solubility and crystallinity.

The most commonly used $\pi$ -linker is thiophene-based unit. DO1 and DO2 with thiophene and bithiophene as $\pi$ linkers had similar $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ but DO2 showed a stronger absorption and a higher mobility, leading to a higher PCE of $5 . 1 1 \%$ [88]. TBDTCNR, based on terthiophene $\pi$ -linker with $n$ -octyl on each thiophene, gave a PCE of $5 . 4 2 \%$ with high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and FF but a moderate $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ [89]. Removing alkyl chains on the $\pi$ -linker of TBDTCNR offered BDT-3T-CA [90]. The improved planarity, strong intermolecular interactions, and highly ordered stacking led to its high FF of 0.75. By removing the $n$ -octyl on the end thiophene of the $\pi$ -linker, DCA3T(T-BDT) was reported and delivered a PCE of $8 \%$ [91]. Introducing $\mathrm { T } 3 2 b \mathrm { T }$ into the $\pi$ -linker also achieved good results [92].

Besides, with BDT as $\pi$ -linker, $\mathrm { D R B D T } _ { 3 }$ exhibited a wide $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 9 7 \mathrm { e V }$ due to the unfavorable conjugation and stacking by the rigid structure of BDTs, giving a PCE of $4 . 0 9 \%$ [93]. STB-3 with $\mathrm { T } 3 4 b \mathrm { T }$ as $\pi$ -linker showed ordered molecular stacking, well-defined phase separation and high domain purity when matched with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ and achieved a PCE of $9 . 2 6 \%$ [94]. Other $\pi$ -linkers such as cyclopentadithiophene (CPDT) and phenoxazine (POZ) have also been reported [95, 96].

Terminal Moiety Variation Terminal unit has effects on energy levels, especially the LUMO energy level, and molecular stacking. Cyanoacetate, RD, 1H-indene-1, $3 ( 2 H )$ -dione (IN) are widely used.

Compared with DCAO3TBDT with cyanoacetate, DR3TBDT with RD showed a lower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ and an improved absorption coefficient. Attributed to the strong absorption and suitable phase separation, DR3TBDT-based device gave a higher PCE of $6 . 3 8 \%$ with simultaneously enhanced $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF than that of DCAO3TBDT-based device [75]. Wei and coworkers reported BTID-0F, -1F, and -2F with IN, fluorinated, and difluorinated IN [92]. With the increase of fluorine atoms, red-shifted absorption and deepened energy levels were observed. In the blends based on BTID-1F and -2F, hierarchical morphology existed, facilitating charge separation and transport; meanwhile, the favorable vertical phase distribution contributed to charge collection. Excellent PCEs of $1 0 . 4 \%$ and $1 1 . 3 \%$ were realized, respectively. Peng and coworkers designed a medium-sized SMD, BDTSTNTTR, with RD as terminal, which showed a strong absorption in the range of $6 0 0 { - } 8 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and a low-lying HOMO energy level. A record PCE of $1 1 . 5 3 \%$ was achieved with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 2 1 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an FF of 0.77 [13].

As shown in Table 2.6, BDT-based SMDs exhibit wide $E _ { \mathbf { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ , and the relevant devices can deliver high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } \mathrm { s }$ and FFs, and they are also good choices for tandem devices [97]. Though the $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } \mathbf { s }$ have been promoted compared with that of OT-type SMDs-based devices, they are still far from satisfactory. Adjusting molecular structure, manipulating blend morphology, and optimizing device technology are urgently needed.

# 2.3.1.3 Dithienosilole-Based A-D-A-Type Molecular Donors

Dithienosilole (DTs) exhibits a strong electron-donating ability and a coplanar skele.   
ton due to the reduced steric hindrance of the side chains by the long C--Si bond.

These make the related SMDs exhibit strong absorptions in the visible range and ordered stacking in solid state. Since the design strategies are similar with those in OT- and BDT-based SMDs, herein, we only give some representative examples as shown in Figure 2.7, and the parameters are listed in Table 2.7.

DCAO3TSi with octyl cyanoacetate terminal showed a strong absorption in the range of $4 5 0 \mathrm { - } 7 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , while DR3TDTS with RD terminal exhibited an obvious red-shifted absorption [98, 99]. And the PCEs were $5 . 8 4 \%$ and $8 . 0 2 \%$ , respectively, of which the better performance was attributed to the favorable absorption and morphology. C8-ester and C8-amide were designed with cyanoacetate and cyanoacetamide as terminals, respectively [1oo]. Due to the intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions, C8-amide showed denser stacking but was oriented more randomly, which led to good miscibility with fullerene. However, this resulted in the poor phase separation in blend, making the PCE unideal with a value of $3 . 2 2 \%$ . By using DCV terminal and bithiophene $\pi$ -linker, SMD1 was obtained and gave a PCE of $3 . 8 1 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 2 \mathrm { V }$ [101]. RHO-tDTS containing three DTS units and two RD terminals exhibited a smal $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 7 \mathrm { e V } ,$ giving a PCE of $7 . 5 6 \%$ with a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 2 . 6 9 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ [102].

# 2.3.1.4 Dithienopyrrole-Based A-D-A-Type Molecular Donors

DTP has a strong electron-donating ability, leading to a high-lying HOMO energy level, and thus a low $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . By regulating the backbone, side chain and terminal, photoelectronic properties, and device performance can be well controlled.

Linking alkyl-substituted DTP with DCV and bithiophene, Bauerle and coworkers reported various SMDs [103]. The results showed that SMDs with alkyl chains of the $\pi$ -linker biased toward DTP often exhibited better solubility and lower-lying energy levels. And device based on SMD2 and SMD3 gave PCEs of $6 . 1 \%$ . Chen and coworkers utilized RD terminal and terthiophene $\pi$ -linker to offer DR3TDTN [104]. It exhibited strong crystallinity, however, because the large domain was unfavorable for exciton dissociation, the device only gave a PCE of $3 . 0 3 \%$ . They then utilized carbazole $\mathbf { \tau } ( \mathbf { C } \mathbf { z } )$ to replace the DTP and obtained DR3TCz [105]. Due to the weaker electron-donating ability of $\mathbf { C } \mathbf { z }$ , the absorption of DR3TCz was blue-shifted and HOMO energy level was down-shifted, and the device gave a PCE of $4 . 0 8 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 4 \mathrm { V } .$ Further fusing $\mathbf { C } \mathbf { z }$ with the inner thiophene of the terthiophene $\pi$ -linker, DR2TDTCz was obtained, which showed a red-shifted absorption and an obvious shoulder peak, suggesting the effective stacking in the solid state. And the final PCE was $7 . 0 3 \%$ with a high FF of 0.75, attributed to the balanced charge transport. The molecular structures and the detailed parameters are shown in Figure 2.8 and Table 2.8, respectively.
