(d) TEM and AFM images of PBDB-T:DTCN-C, PBDB-T:IDTCN-O, and PBDB-T:IDTCN--based blend flms. Source: Liu et a. [121/Rproduced with permission of JOHN WILEY & SONS, INC.

PCE of $9 . 5 8 \%$ and an outstanding $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 . 7 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ with an AVT of $3 7 \%$ . Considering the decreased AVT of Ag electrodes in NIR than in the visible region, the thickness of $\mathbf { A } \mathbf { g }$ electrode was reduced to increase the transmittance of visible light. As expected, the AVT exhibited an increasing trend at the expense of weakened $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF (Ag, 100-5 nm). At last, the PCE of $7 . 7 4 \%$ was obtained for PTB7-Th:ATT-2-based ST-OSCs $\left( \mathrm { A g } , 2 0 \mathrm { n m } \right)$ , which is the highest value at that time with such high transmittance.

Also coveting the advantages of NIR SMAs, Li's group designed a SMA, namely, T2 (also called IFIC-i-4F) [117], through adding fluorine atom into ester-substituted thieno[3,4-b]thiophene $\pi$ -bridge. End-capped with IC-F, T2 presented a $0 . 1 6 \mathrm { e V }$ upshifted HOMO and $0 . 0 6 \mathrm { e V }$ deeper LUMO than ATT-2 $( - 5 . 5 0 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 9 0 \mathrm { e V } )$ , corresponding to a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 3 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ Photo-induced force microscopy (PiFM) measurements revealed that the T2 can evenly mix with donor PTB7-Th, and proper phase separation can be observed with an average domain size $( \sim 2 0 \mathrm { n m } )$ at top surface of their blend after processing with $1 \%$ $\mathbf { \Pi } ( \mathbf { v } / \mathbf { v } )$ CN additive (Figure 4.16b). An optimal PCE of $1 0 . 8 7 \%$ was thus achieved with an outstanding $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 4 . 8 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 6 5 \mathrm { V }$ and a FF of 0.670. As widely recognized that the tandem OSCs consist of two individual subcells, and its $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ is the sum of the voltages of two subcells while the $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ was determined by the lowest one. By chance, the low $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of PTB7-Th:T2-based device are just suitable for fabricating tandem OSCs. The resultant tandem device (PBDB-T:ITIC as front cell and PTB7-Th:T2 as rear cell, Figure 4.16c) afforded a surprisingly high PCE of $1 4 . 6 4 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 5 6 \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { : } }$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 3 . 2 2 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.710.

Further $\pi$ -bridge engineering with methyl-3-thiophenecarboxylate generated a new SMA called IDT-3MT (Figure 4.15) [118]. Supramolecular $\mathrm { O } { - } \mathrm { S }$ non-covalent interactions can lock the flat conformation of the IDT-3MT acceptor, which significantly extends the effective conjugation and broadens the absorption spectrum. Besides, the photoluminescence (PL)-quenching measurements showed that the PBDB-T:IDT-3MT-based blend displayed a higher fluorescence quenching efficiency of over $9 5 \%$ than IDT-T-based one $( 6 7 \% )$ when excited at $7 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ suggesting efficient charge dissociation at the $\mathrm { D } / \mathrm { A }$ interface. Consequently, the PBDB-T:IDT-3MT-based device achieved a highly improved PCE of $8 . 4 0 \%$ than IDT-T-based cells $( 6 . 3 6 \% )$ without any additives (Table 4.6).

Then the vinyl was inserted as the $\pi$ -bridge into IDT-cored FREA IDT-IC, and the SJ-IC was designed and synthesized [119]. Compared with IDT-IC, the SJ-IC presents an obviously deeper LUMO of $- 3 . 9 4 \mathrm { e V }$ and an upshifted HOMO of $- 5 . 6 1 \mathrm { e V } ,$ corresponding to a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 9 \mathrm { e V }$ for high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ . In addition, the increased structural complexity induced by the introduction of $\mathrm { C } { = } \mathrm { C }$ bond weakens the crystallinity of SJ-IC, endowing the J61:SJ-IC-based blend suitable phased separation with pure acceptor domain after thermal annealing for efficient charge transport. A PCE of $9 . 2 7 \%$ was obtained by J61:SJ-IC-based OSCs with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 3 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 9 9 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.660, $2 5 \%$ higher than that of IDT-IC-based counterparts $( 6 . 9 5 \% )$ . In order to absorb more photos at short wavelength, thienylenevinylene thiophene (TVT) was introduced between IDT core and IC end groups for the synthesis of ITVT [120]. The conjugated TVT side chains provide ITVT a strong absorption at $3 0 0 { - } 5 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ with a narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ Featuring complementary absorption and matching energy levels with ITVT, the wide $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ PBZ was selected as donor and their blend film exhibited a fibrillar structure with a $\mu _ { \mathrm { e } }$ of $1 . 8 5 \times 1 0 ^ { - 4 } \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ . The as-cast PBZ:ITVT-based OSCs (D/A ratio $= 1 : 2$ ) obtained a moderate PCE of $5 . 8 4 \%$ with a low FF of 0.427.

Different from the modification in inner position of thiophene above mentioned, Bo and coworkers [121] explored three novel SMAs by inserting diverse alkyl chain into outer position of thiophene bridge including hexyl (IDTCN-C), hexyloxy (IDTCN-O), and hexylthio (IDTCN-S) (Figure 4.15). All three SMAs show strong absorption at $5 5 0 \mathrm { - } 8 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ in solution with molar absorption coefficient of $1 . 7 7 { - } 2 . 5 5 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { M ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ , and IDTCN-O exhibited a wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 5 3 \mathrm { e V }$ than $E _ { \mathbf { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ of both IDTCN-C and IDTCN-S $( 1 . 4 8 \mathrm { e V } )$ . Theoretical simulation indicated that alkyl chains connected to the $\beta$ position of thiophene restrict the free rotation of the terminal group for a stable dominant conformation. Moreover, compatible crystallization rate of donor and acceptor can form a good film morphology, and the IDTCN-O featuring strong crystallinity has a good miscibility with PBDB-T, which can be demonstrated by the decreased polymer fibrils in their blend (Figure 4.16d). As a result, the PBDB-T:IDTCN-O-based OSCs presented an outstanding PCE of $1 3 . 2 8 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 1 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 9 . 9 6 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.732, much higher than that of IDTCN-C- and IDTCN-S-based devices $( 1 1 . 9 2 \%$ and $1 0 . 6 0 \%$ respectively) (Table 4.6). The highest $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ can be attributed to the highest LUMO energy levels of IDTCN-O $\left( - 3 . 8 0 \mathrm { e V } \right)$ , which can also be confirmed by the highest energy of charge transfer state $( E _ { \mathrm { c t } } )$ . The $1 3 . 2 8 \%$ PCE is the highest value reported in literature at that time.

From the above strategies, we can obviously summarize that the planarity is an important guarantee for efficient charge transfer. And the non-covalent interaction formed in inner position of $\pi$ -bridge provides a planar backbone while that in outer position can lock the conformation between end groups and $\pi$ -bridge. Combining the advantages of these two, Bo's group [122] reported a novel SMA named ITOIC-2Cl utilizing bis(alkoxy)-substituted thiophene as $\pi$ -bridges (Figure 4.15). The better skeleton planarity can be obtained induced by double intramolecular sulfuroxygen (S-O) and oxygen-hydrogen (CH-O) interactions, which is not strong in solution to guarantee the solubility of SMAs. End-capped with strong electron-deficient di-chlorinated (IC-2Cl), the ITOIC-2Cl has a NIR film absorption approaching $9 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , accordingly a narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ The film blended with PBDB-T exhibited clear phase separation with uniformly distributed nano-sized structure, suggesting the formation of regular interpenetrating network for efficient exciton dissociation at $\mathrm { D } / \mathrm { A }$ interface and charge transport. The resulting as-cast OSCs based on PBDB-T:ITOIC-2Cl delivered a PCE of $9 . 3 7 \%$ (Table 4.6).

Furthermore, replacing oxygen atom with sulfur atom and lengthening the alkyl chains, Zhang and coworkers [123] designed the IDT2ST-4F end-capped with IC-2F. In terms of the wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 3 \mathrm { e V }$ in relative to ITOIC-2Cl, the as-cast PBDB-T:IDT2ST-4F-based device only achieved a PCE of $9 . 2 7 \%$ After annealing at $1 1 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for five minutes, the enhanced crystallinity of IDT2ST-4F induced a more uniform fibrous morphology for improved $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 9 . 4 4 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and FF of 0.693, thus a higher PCE of $1 1 . 4 3 \%$ . Coincidentally, Bo and coworkers [124] developed two novel SMAs using IDT as core and the bis(alkoxy)-substituted (IDT-BOC6) or dialkyl-substituted benzene (IDT-BC6) as conformational control units. Similar to ITOIC-2Cl and IDT2ST-4F mentioned above, the IDT-BOC6 presents a planar backbone due to dual non-covalent interaction, while the IDT-BC6 shows a distorted plane with large dihedral angles between $\pi$ bridge and IDT core/terminal groups. After treating with $1 \%$ DIO, the optimal PBDB-T:IDT-BOC6-based OSCs afforded a PCE of $9 . 6 0 \%$ with an impressive $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ over $1 . 0 0 \mathrm { V } .$ The irregular bulk phase separation morphology may be used to explain the poor PCE of PBDB-T:IDT-BOC6-based device $( 2 . 3 \% )$

To further explore best-performing SMA, Bo and coworkers inserted 3,4- propylenedioxythiophene (PDOT) and 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene (EDOT) bridging units for synthesizing two IDT-cored SMAs (IDT-PDOT and IDT-EDOT, respectively, Figure 4.15) [125]. The introduction of a tiny methylene group caused distinct structure-properties relationship. The IDT-EDOT has similar energy levels and absorption with IDT-PDOT, but about four times higher molar absorption coefficient of $1 . 9 5 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { M ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ than IDT-PDOT $( 4 . 8 6 \times 1 0 ^ { 4 } \mathrm { M ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } } )$ . Morphological study revealed that the neat IDT-EDOT film showed a smaller $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance of $3 . 4 5 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ than IDT-PDOT $( 3 . 6 4 \mathring \mathrm { A } )$ , indicating more compact intermolecular packing for high electron mobility. In addition, the PBDB-T:IDT-EDOT-based blend presents clear nanofiber-like interpenetrating network structure, which increases the $\mathrm { D } / \mathrm { A }$ contact interface for efficient exciton dissociation and charge transport. The optimal PBDB-T:IDT-EDOT-based OSCs (treated with $0 . 2 \%$ DIO) contributed to a salient PCE of $1 1 . 3 2 \%$ with a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 1 . 3 4 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 6 \mathrm { V }$ and a FF of O.620, surpassing the PBDB-T:IDT-PDOT-based ones $( 2 . 1 8 \% )$ and even the IEICO-4F-based devices $( 8 . 2 9 \% )$ (Table 4.6). The poor properties of IDT-PDOT-based cells can be attributed to inappropriate phase separation morphology. These results demonstrate that minor changes in molecule structures can seriously affect blend morphologies to cause unexpected intermolecular aggregation behavior, thus diverse device properties. And the best-performing SMAs can be explored via delicate molecule design strategies in $\pi$ bridge.

All the above molecular designs powerfully demonstrate the potential of $\pi$ -bridge, boosting the PCE increasing from $2 . 3 0 \%$ to $1 3 . 2 8 \%$ . Among them, almost all the as-cast OSCs have poor or moderate properties, and many efficient systems need post-processing including thermal annealing and additives which reduces the reproducibility and stability. As thus, a new strategy was proposed by Bo and coworkers [126] to attach two alkoxyl substituents at the 3,8-positions of IDT core. Coupling with two thiophene $\pi$ -bridge and IC-2F end groups generated the IDTOT2F (Figure 4.15). For comparison, the IDTT2F (without substituted alkyl) was also synthesized. IDTOT2F showed a better solubility than IDTT2F, and the middle-shrinking energy levels endow IDTOT2F a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ for high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ . The derived as-cast PBDB-T:IDTOT2F OSCs presented a record PCE of $1 2 . 7 9 \%$ , much higher than that of IDTT2F- $( 8 . 8 5 \% )$ and IEICO-4F- $( 8 . 6 6 \% )$ based counterparts (Table 4.6).

Similarly using O-S non-covalent interactions, Liu and coworker [128] explored the effects of different $\pi$ -bridges on device properties, and three novel SMAs were obtained by bridging thiophene (IDTO-T-4F), selenophene (IDTO-Se-4F) and thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (IDTO-TT-4F), respectively (Figure 4.15). All three SMAs exhibited similar LUMO energy levels around $- 3 . 8 9 \mathrm { e V }$ while the IDTO-TT-4F has a highest HOMO of $- 5 . 3 9 \mathrm { e V } .$ The strongest electron-donating ability provides IDTO-TT-4F enhanced ICT effect for a narrowest $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 3 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ GIWAXS results showed that the pristine SMAs films have diverse CCL $( 2 7 . 4 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ for IDTO-T-4F, $2 0 . 9 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ for IDTO-Se-4F and $1 9 . 0 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ for IDTO-TT-4F), the highest CCL of IDTO-T-4F is beneficial for the charge transport properties in corresponding film. In addition, the stronger (oio) diffraction peak than the other two can be observed in PBDB-T:IDTO-T-4F-based blend, suggesting more compact $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking for efficient charge transport. As a result, the PBDB-T:IDTO-T-4F-based device afforded a champion PCE of $1 2 . 6 2 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 6 \mathrm { V } ,$ a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 . 1 2 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a FF of 0.727, outperforming the other two counterparts ( $1 0 . 6 7 \%$ for PBDB-T:IDTO-Se-4F and $1 0 . 2 1 \%$ for PBDB-T:IDTO-TT-4F) (Table 4.6).

# 4.3.3.3 Asymmetric Cores

Unlike the widespread study of symmetric FREAs, asymmetric FREAs only shine from 2016. Featuring feasibility in chemical structure modulation and planar molecular backbones for efficient charge transport that symmetric FREAs owned, asymmetric FREAs additionally possess stronger intermolecular binding energy and larger dipole moment for high-performing OsCs. Generally, three main strategies including asymmetric core, asymmetric side chains, and asymmetric end groups were adopted into acceptors for structure optimization.

Thiophene and TT are the most common building blocks for molecule design, and the indacenodithiophene (IDT) and IDTT cores are successfully developed for efficient FREAs. Considering the advantages of asymmetric FREAs, Sun and coworkers [129] explored an asymmetric core named TPTT by flanking benzene with thiophene and TT unit. The $\pi$ -conjugation length, fused-ring numbers, and electron-donating ability of the TPTT core are in between the IDT and IDTT cores. Coupling with IC generated the novel asymmetric acceptor TPTT-IC (Figure 4.17). Compared with IDT-cored IC-1IDT-IC [130] $( - 5 . 9 1 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 8 3 \mathrm { e V } ,$ $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ o p t } } = 1 . 7 0 \mathrm { e V } )$ and IDTT-cored ITIC $( - 5 . 7 1 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 9 7 \mathrm { e V } _ { \mathrm { } }$ $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ o p t } } = 1 . 6 0 \mathrm { e V } $ , TPTT-IC has centered HOMO/LUMO of $- 5 . 7 8 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 9 5 \mathrm { e V }$ and $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 3 \mathrm { e V } .$ Comfortingly, the PBT1-C:TPTT-IC blend films expectantly presented a higher $\mu _ { \mathrm { e } }$ of $3 . 2 3 \times 1 0 ^ { - 4 } \ \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \ \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \ \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ than PBT1-C:ITIC-based blend $( \mu _ { \mathrm { e } } = 2 . 8 5 \times 1 0 ^ { - 4 } { \mathrm { c m } } ^ { 2 } { \mathrm { V } } ^ { - 1 } { \mathrm { s } } ^ { - 1 } )$ , which may be attributed to favorable morphology induced by dipole-dipole intermolecular interaction of asymmetric TPTT-IC. The derived PBT1-C:TPTT-IC-based OSCs achieved a slightly higher PCE of $1 0 . 3 \%$ than ITIC-based ones $( 1 0 . 0 \% )$ (Table 4.7).

In order to enhance the light-harvesting ability of acceptor for higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , the asymmetric acceptor TPTTT-2F [131] (Figure 4.17) was synthesized through adding a thiophene unit and end-capping mono-fluorinated IC (IC-F). The extended core conjugation endows TPTTT-2F broader absorption, upshifted LUMO of $- 3 . 4 4 \mathrm { e V }$ and more compact intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking (Figure 4.18a)

when compared with TPTT-cored counterpart (TPTT-2F, with IC-F end group). Consequently, the PBT1-C:TPTTT-2F-based OSCs obtained a higher PCE of $1 2 . 0 3 \%$ than TPTT-2F-based ones $( 1 0 . 1 7 \% )$ , along with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 2 \mathrm { V }$ due to the energy level difference between donor and acceptor. After that, Yang and coworkers [132] replaced IC-F end group with weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(6-oxo-5,6-dihydro- $4 H$ -cyclopenta[c]thiophen-4-ylidene) malononitrile (CPTCN), and the classic FREA named MeIC1 was synthesized (Figure 4.17). Due to the upshifted LUMO energy levels of $- 3 . 8 9 \mathrm { e V }$ and narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 5 4 \mathrm { e V }$ in relative to TPTTT-2F, the resulting PBDB-T:MeIC1-based device achieved an improved PCE of $1 2 . 5 8 \%$ (Table 4.7). Given the absorption, energy levels and well-defined face-on orientation of MeIC1, many groups generally added MeIC1 as a third component to optimize corresponding binary systems for high-performance ternary OSCs. For further enhancing the electron-donating ability of core, the strategy of heteroatom substitution is applied to molecular design. The acceptor SePTTT-2F [133] was thus designed by replacing the previous thiophene with selenophenol. In comparison to thiophene, selenophenol has a stronger electron-donating ability and decreased aromaticity, which increased effective conjugation length for a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 5 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ In addition, the large size and great polarizability of selenium are easy to induce intermolecular Se-Se/selenium-aromatic interaction in corresponding selenophene-based FREAs. As a result, the SePTTT-2F and PBT1-C showed good miscibility with the formation of nanostructured interpenetrating networks in their blends, boosting the FF over 0.750. The OSCs fabricated with PBT1-C:SePTTT-2F active layer delivered a PCE of $1 2 . 2 4 \%$ , outperforming the TPTTT-2F-based counterparts (Table 4.7).

It is widely accepted that the crystallinity of FREAs seriously affects the morphology of blend films and packing behavior, thereby greatly influencing the device properties. In 2019, Tang's group successfully developed an INP-cored acceptor named INPIC-4F, and the derived device achieved the highest PCE of $1 3 . 1 3 \%$ at that time. However, strong crystallinity of INPIC-4F limits its photovoltaic performance and is also not conducive to solution-process large-area OSCs. In this case, the asymmetric strategy was conducted by replacing dithieno[ $3 , 2 \cdot b : 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime }$ -d]pyrrole (DTP) block on one side of INP core with relatively weak electron-donating units including thiophene (T), thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT), or dithieno $[ 3 , 2 - b ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } - c$ l]thiophene (TTT). End-capped with IC-2F, three asymmetric FREAs (IPT-2F, IPTT-2F, and IPTTT-2F, the structures shown in Figure 4.17) were designed and synthesized, respectively [134]. Surprisingly, the weakest electron-donating IPT-cored IPT-2F presents the largest red-shifted absorption peaks (c. $3 6 \mathrm { n m } ,$ from solution to films, indicating a more well-aligned and compact intermolecular stacking in the solid state. Also, along with the expansion of $\pi$ conjugate system (from IPT, IPTT, to IPTTT), the HOMO energy levels gradually upshifted, while the LUMO energy levels exhibit a deepened trend. More interestingly, due to the O-S non-covalent interactions induced by the oxygen atoms on the end groups and the sulfur atom on donating core, three asymmetric FREAs show diverse preferred conformation (S-shaped conformations for IPT-2F and IPTTT-2F, C-shaped conformation for IPTT-2F, Figure 4.18b), which confirmed by theoretical calculations and electric potential simulations. Analysis of the active layer morphology found that S-shaped IPT-2F and IPTTT-2F assembled order textures with long nanofibrils for advantageous charge transport, while a heterogeneous morphology with irregular phase separation can be observed in C-shaped IPTT-2F-based blend. The OSCs based on PBDB-T:IPT-2F achieved a champion PCE of $1 4 . 0 0 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 6 \mathrm { V } ,$ a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 2 . 4 0 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.724, higher than that of IPTT-2F- and IPTTT-2F-based counterparts $( 1 2 . 3 \%$ and $1 1 . 4 \%$ , respectively) (Table 4.7). To the best of our knowledge, $1 4 \%$ PCE is among the highest PCE values in literature for asymmetric FREAs-based binary OSCs at that time. The more dominant face-on orientation with a stronger (010) $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking of IPT-2F-based blend can facilitate charge transfer in the vertical direction, which may be a reason of the higher FF and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ PBDB-T:IPT-2F obtained for better PCE in comparison to PBDB-T:IPTTT-2F. For further enhancing the electron-donating ability of core, the same group explored selenopheno $\left[ { 2 ^ { \prime \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime \prime } { : } 5 ^ { \prime } , 6 ^ { \prime } } \right] - s$ - indaceno $[ 2 ^ { \prime } , 1 ^ { \prime } { : } 4 , 5 ]$ thieno[3,2 - b]thieno[2,3 - d]pyrrole (DTPpse) core by replacing thiophene with selenophenol [135]. In order to systematically study the influence of terminal groups on molecular characteristics and device performance, three asymmetric FREAs were synthesized with enhanced electron-withdrawing end groups including IC (DTPPSe-IC), IC-F(DTPPSe-2F), and IC-2F (DTPPSe-4F) (Figure 4.17). The DTPPSe-2F showed the ${ \sim } 9 \mathrm { n m }$ red-shifted $\lambda _ { \mathrm { o n s e t } }$ than IPT-2F, corresponding to a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ Besides, the gradually deepened energy levels and narrowed $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ can be observed, along with the increasing electron-withdrawing abilities of end groups $( \mathrm { I C } < \mathrm { I C } { \cdot } \mathrm { F } < \mathrm { I C } { \cdot } 2 \mathrm { F } )$ Electrostatic potential (EsP) analysis shows that most parts of the surface have positive ESP, while the negative regions are only located at both ends of the acceptors (Figure 4.18c). Moreover, the increased fluorine atoms can expand the negative regions at both ends, which is more conducive to strengthen the intermolecular interactions with the donor to promote charge transfer. Surprisingly, the PBDB-T:DTPPSe-2F-based devices achieved the champion PCE of $1 3 . 7 6 \%$ among the three devices (Table 4.7), due to the better miscibility between donor and acceptor accompanied with uniformly fibrous phase separation morphology. The $1 3 . 7 6 \%$ PCE is the highest values for OSCs in literature using selenophene-containing FREAs.

Apart from heteroatom substitution, the strategy of halogenated end groups is another common strategy to narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ for enhanced intramolecular ICT. However, it can also easily induce excessive self-aggregation tendency. Alkyl- or aryl-based side chains engineering has proven to be quite effective in improving solubility and spontaneous molecular excessive aggregation, but too large or too small alkyl chains will also cause diverse intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance, thereby affecting charge transfer. In order to solve this dilemma, Tang and coworkers [136] further explored the relationship between the fluorinated/chlorinated end groups and octyl (C8)/2-butyl-1-octyl (BO) alkyl chains to modulate energy levels and balance aggregation and crystallinity. Four asymmetric FREAs were thus synthesized, namely, IPT-4F (fluorinated, C8), IPTBO-4F (fluorinated, BO), IPT-4Cl (chlorinated, C8) and IPTBO-4Cl (chlorinated, BO) (Figure 4.17). As presented in Figure 4.19a, the C8 chain located on DTP extends outward along the plane of backbone, and the rotation of C8 exerts negligible impact against the molecular aggregation. On the contrary, due to the steric hindrance with the phenylhexyl group on one side, one arm of the branched BO side chain exhibits an out-of-plane dominant conformation perpendicular to the backbone, which would effectively suppress molecular aggregation. On this basis, the maximum bare length of backbone $( L _ { \mathrm { b } } )$ is assumed to quantify the combined effect of halogenated end groups and side chains on aggregation and stacking behavior (Figure 4.19b). Consequently, the $L _ { \mathrm { b } }$ of IPT-4F, IPTBO-4F, IPT-4Cl, and IPTBO-4Cl is calculated to be 28.01, 24.31, 29.56, and $2 5 . 8 5 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ , respectively, suggesting that IPT-4F forms a more effective stacking than IPTBO-4F, while the IPTBO-4Cl get a better solubility and weakened crystallinity. In line with our prediction, by blending with PM6, the IPT-4F and IPTBO-4Cl-based devices outperformed IPTBO-4F- and IPT-4Cl-based ones, and the PM6:IPTBO-4Cl-based OSCs afforded the champion PCE of $1 5 . 0 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 9 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 3 . 1 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a FF of 0.726 (Table 4.7). The PCE defines a new record of asymmetric FREAs-based OSCs and verifies that dual molecular engineering for balanced crystallinity and solubility is an effective means to obtain best-performing OSCs.

Obviously, the thieno $\left[ { 2 ^ { \prime \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime \prime } ; 5 ^ { \prime } , 6 ^ { \prime } } \right]$ -s-indaceno $^ { 2 ^ { \prime } , 1 ^ { \prime } : 4 , 5 ] }$ dithieno $_ { 3 , 2 - b : 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 }$ -d] pyrrole (IPT) core is much potential to further develop efficient asymmetric acceptors. However, the IPT-4F and IPT-4Cl mentioned above remind us that enhancing the electron-withdrawing ability through halogenated end groups has only a negligible effect on the energy levels and $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ of the IPT-based acceptors, so that only two strategies can be conducted in IPT core: (i) modulation on flanked thiophene and (ii) $N$ functionalized side chains. Utilizing the first strategy, Tang and coworkers [137] tried to modulate the charge density of IPT core by introducing 2-ethylhexyloxy (INO-4F), 2-ethylhexyl (IN-4F), and chlorine (IPCl-4F), respectively, onto the $\beta$ position of thiophene (Figure 4.17). With the enhanced electron-withdrawing ability of the substituents, the LUMO energy level of the acceptors gradually deepened while the HOMO energy level did not show a linear trend, corresponding to gradually narrowing $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ All the films blended with PM6 displayed a face-on orientation with diversity intensities of (o1o) diffraction peaks, suggesting side chain engineering onto core seriously affects the intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking. In addition, the INO-4F and IPCl-4F exhibited poor miscibility along with their blends' enhanced $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking trends for strong crystallinity, which may influence exciton dissociation and charge transport process. In contrast, PM6:IN-4F blend film exhibited CCL of $7 . 5 3 \mathrm { n m }$ in in-plane direction, much smaller than that of PM6:IPT-4F-based blend $( 2 4 . 3 \mathrm { n m } )$ , indicating decreased crystallinity and restricted charge transport for poor $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF. As a result, $1 3 . 6 9 \%$ PCE was obtained with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 . 4 6 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.720 (Table 4.7). The moderate PCE in relative to PM6:IPT-4F-based OSCs $( 1 4 . 6 2 \% )$ reminds us the energy level matching, molecular stacking, and miscibility should also be taken into consideration while manipulating the charge density.

Inspired by the second strategy and the successful application of conjugated side chains on polymers, Tang and coworkers [138] reported a novel asymmetric FREA called IPT2F-TCl by replacing $n$ -octyl with 2D chlorinated hexylthiophene side chain. In relative to IPT-2F, the IPT2F-TCl has deeper energy levels and wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ resulting from the deflected 2D chlorinated side chain. When fabricated as a device, IPT2F-TCl and the polymer donor PBDB-T exhibit better miscibility with homogeneous and nanofibrous phase separation morphology than IPT-2F-based counterpart. Consequently, the PBDB-T:IPT2F-TCl-based OSCs delivered a PCE of $1 3 . 7 4 \%$ with an impressively high FF of 0.775, and the FF is among the highest values reported in the literature for asymmetric FREAs-based OSCs. The results demonstrate that 2D-chlorinated hexylthiophene side chain has great potential in designing FREAs for morphology manipulation to obtain a satisfactory FF.

Firstly applying $N$ -functionalized 2D side chain into asymmetric FREAs design, the same group further developed three novel FREAs attaching different 2D side chains onto DTP block in IPT core, including thiophene (IPT2F-Th), benzene (IPT2F-Ph), and thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (IPT2F-TT) (the structures shown in Figure 4.17) [139]. All three 2D FREAs have strong absorption at $6 0 0 { - } 8 7 0 \mathrm { n m }$ corresponding to $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 5 \mathrm { e V }$ for IPT2F-TT, $1 . 4 6 \mathrm { e V }$ for IPT2F-Ph, and $1 . 4 7 \mathrm { e V }$ for IPT2F-Th, respectively. In addition, the three two-dimensional materials have almost the same energy levels. The twisting of $N$ -conjugated side chains from backbone endows three FREAs with similar energy levels and light absorptions ${ \sim } 8 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ edge) (Figure $4 . 1 9 \mathrm { c } )$ . When PBDB-T was selected as the donor, the PBDB-T:IPT2F-TT-based blend displayed higher charge mobility, more orderly phase separation, and more suitable intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance than other two counterparts. Consequently, the device based on PBDB-T:IPT2F-TT achieved a PCE of $1 4 . 0 2 \%$ and a FF of 0.751, which is better than PBDB-T:IPT2F-Ph (PCE of $1 3 . 1 3 \%$ and FF of O.721), PBDB-T: IPT2F-Th (PCE of $1 2 . 5 2 \%$ and FF of 0.712), and PBDB-T: IPT-2F (PCE of $1 4 . 0 0 \%$ and FF of 0.724). The $1 4 . 0 2 \%$ PCE and 0.751 FF are the highest values of 2D-FREAs-based OSCs reported in the literature so far. More interestingly, the PBDB-T:IPT2F-TT-based devices surprisingly have high PCE retention rates of $9 0 . 2 2 \%$ and $8 6 . 6 7 \%$ , respectively, after 100 hours of continuous thermal aging or light aging, showing good thermal and light soaking stability (Figure 4.19d). This work proved that the $N$ -functionalized 2D side chain modification on the IPT core can effectively improve device performance, and

TT is better than benzene and thiophene. Besides, diverse 2D side chains lead to differences in stability, which provides ideas for subsequent use of simple molecular engineering to improve device stability.

For further extending the length of fused-ring core for stronger absorption, a thiophene unit was added into the IDTT core to synthesize a new eight-membered asymmetric core. The end groups properties relationship was explored, and three asymmetric acceptors named TTPTTT-IC, TTPTTT-2F, and TTPTTT-4F were thus designed and synthesized (Figure 4.17) [140]. The increase of fluorine atoms on the end groups deepens the energy levels and narrows the $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ Morphology studies showed that all three films blended with PBT1-C presented a face-on $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking. And compared with TTPTTT-IC based one, the fluorinated TTPTTT-2F and TTPTTT-4F-based blends exhibited more clear nanofiber phase separation with small RMS of 1.46 and $1 . 2 6 \mathrm { n m }$ , respectively. The resulting PBT1-C:TTPTTT-4F-based OSCs delivered a PCE of $1 2 . 0 5 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 6 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 9 . 3 6 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of O.721, outperforming PBT1-C:TTPTTT-IC $( 7 . 9 1 \% )$ and PBT1-C:TTPTTT-2F $( 1 1 . 5 2 \% )$ -based counterparts (Table 4.7). The salient properties of PBT1-C:TTPTTT-4F can be attributed to the high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ induced by red-shifted absorption.

Different from extending the conjugation in the horizontal direction, Yang and coworkers [141] inserted a 2D alkyl-thiophene side chain into asymmetric core to generate the a-BTTIC (Figure 4.17). The introduction of 2D side chain not only extends asymmetrical conjugation backbone with a narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 3 \mathrm { e V }$ but also offers a large dipole moment of 7.88 debye for stronger intermolecular dipole-dipole interaction and the promoted antiparallel molecule arrangement. Featuring clear phase separation and a well-developed nanostructured interpenetrating network, the PBDB-T:a-BTTIC-based OSCs achieved a high PCE of $1 3 . 6 0 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 0 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 . 3 1 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and a FF of 0.740, which is the highest PCE for commercialized PBDB-T-based OSCs (Table 4.7). The $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ was found to be as low as $0 . 5 3 \mathrm { e V } .$ More novelly, Yang and coworkers [142] convert IDTT symmetric core into asymmetric core by repalcing thieno [3,2-b]thiophene with thieno [2,3-b]thiophene. End capping with CPTCN, a novel asymmetric acceptor ITCNTC was synthesized. Compared with IDTT-cored ITCPTC $( 2 . 0 5 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { m o l ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \scriptsize ~ o p t } } ~ = ~ 1 . 5 8 \mathrm { e V } )$ ITCNTC has a ca. $4 7 \mathrm { n m }$ blue-shifted $\lambda _ { \mathrm { o n s e t } }$ with molar absorption coefficient of $1 . 8 0 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { m o l ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ , corresponding to a wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ In addition, the ITCNTC shows upshifted LUMO and down-shifted HOMO, that is, wider electrochemical bandgap. The ITCNTC featuring strong crystalline resulted in the oversized phase separation in J71:ITCNTC blends, which is not conductive to the charge transport and collection. The derived J71:ITCNTC OSCs only obtained a moderate PCE of $8 . 5 2 \%$ (Table 4.7). The poor PCE in relative to J71:ITCPTC $( 1 1 . 6 3 \% )$ can be ascribed to low $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF induced by weak absorption and poor morphology.

In terms of molecular design, side chains are critical as a manipulator in morphology and intermolecular stacking. For example, Yang's group performed side chain engineering on the asymmetric TPTT core mentioned above, and two FREAs were synthesized by embedding different side chains on cyclopentadiene, namely, IDT6CN (phenylhexyl substitution) and IDT6CN-Th (hexylthiophene substitution) (Figure 4.17) [143]. Obviously, c. $1 2 \mathrm { n m }$ red-shifted $\lambda _ { \mathrm { o n s e t } }$ can be observed in neat IDT6CN-Th film with a slightly molar extinction coefficients of $2 . 1 0 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { m o l ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ in relative to IDT6CN film. Besides, IDT6CN-Th showed deeper HOMO/LUMO energy levels of $- 5 . 7 1 \mathrm { e V } / \mathrm { - } 4 . 0 1 \mathrm { e V }$ than IDT6CN $( - 5 . 6 8 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 9 7 \mathrm { e V } )$ . After adding $0 . 5 \%$ additives and thermal annealing at $1 1 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for three minutes, the optimal PBDB-T:IDT6CN-Th-based device achieved a PCE of $1 0 . 4 1 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 0.81 V, a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 7 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an impressive FF of 0.767, higher than that of IDT6CN-based counterpart $( 9 . 2 7 \% )$ (Table 4.7). The excellent morphology accompanied with nanofibrous interpenetrating network accounts for the prominent FF.

Moreover, asymmetric side chains strategy was employed into molecule design to synthesize a novel FREAs named IDT-OB [76]. Compared to symmetric phenylhexyl substituted IDT-2B and $n$ -octyl substituted IDT-2O, IDT-OB has similar energy levels and strong absorption in between. Due to the stronger dipole-dipole interaction of asymmetric acceptors, a more ordered intermolecular arrangement will be formed to promote charge transport, which provides the PBDB-T:IDT-OB blend a higher $\mu _ { \mathrm { e } }$ of $2 . 7 1 \times 1 0 ^ { - 4 } \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ and more balanced $\mu _ { \mathrm { e } } / \mu _ { \mathrm { h } }$ of 1.30 for high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and PCE. Morphology studies indicated that PBDB-T:IDT-2O and PBDB-T:IDT-OB blends behave prioritized face-on (010) $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking in the OOP direction, while the face-on and edge-on crystallites co-exist in PBDB-T:IDT-2B-based blend film. In addition, the strong crystallinity of IDT-2O causes its corresponding blend strong aggregation for poor charge transport. In comparison, the fiber structure with a diameter of $1 0 { - } 2 0 \mathrm { n m }$ can be observed in PBDB-T:IDT-OB blend films, suggesting the formation of excellent charge transport network. As a result, the as-cast device based on PBDB-T:IDT-OB exhibited a champion PCE of $1 0 . 1 2 \%$ with a highest $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 1 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ . More interestingly, the PBDB-T:IDT-OB-based OSC is insensitive to film thickness, and a PCE of $9 . 1 7 \%$ can be maintained when the thickness is over $2 1 0 \mathrm { n m }$

Asymmetric side chains have been proved to be effective means to improve morphology, intermolecular packing and aggregation behavior, and photoelectric properties. However, the side chain modification has little effect on the energy levels, which limits us to screen suitable donors to match. In view of the electron-withdrawing A unit's powerful manipulation of energy levels as well as absorption and the advantages of asymmetric molecules, Hou and coworkers [144] used a one-pot method to prepare IDTT-cored asymmetric acceptor IT-3F (Figure 4.17) with asymmetric end groups in a $3 0 \%$ yield. For comparison, the other two symmetric FREAs were synthesized end-capping IC-F (IT-2F) and IC-2F (IT-4F). All three FREAs show strong absorption at $5 5 0 \mathrm { - } 8 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ with similar molar absorption coefficient of $\sim 1 . 2 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { m o l ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ . The energy levels are deepened accompanied with the increased fluorine atoms. The derived binary PM6:IT-3F OSCs achieved a higher PCE of $1 3 . 8 3 \%$ than IT-2F- and IT-4F-based cells $. 1 2 . 6 5 \%$ and $1 3 . 6 2 \%$ , respectively) (Table 4.7). When IT-2F and IT-4F are selected to fabricate ternary OSCs, an enhanced PCE of $1 4 . 0 4 \%$ was obtained. The transmission electron microscope (TEM) results obviously showed that the ternary blend films have little difference from three binary ones, suggesting good compatibility of three above FREAs. In this case, diversity IDTT-cored FREAs (IT-M, ITIC, IT-2F, IT-4F, and IT-4Cl) are used to explore the preparation of high-performing multi-component OSCs. Consequently, the optimal six-component OSCs (PM6:IT-M:ITIC:IT-2F:IT-4F:IT- $\cdot 4 \mathrm { C l } = 1 : 0 . 0 5 : 0 . 0 5 : 0 . 0 5 : 0 . 8 : 0 . 0 5 )$ delivered a PCE of $1 3 . 2 6 \%$ with improved $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 1 . 0 2 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$

# 4.3.3.4 Non-fused Cores

The development of FREAs typically adopted A-D-A type has promoted continuous breakthroughs in efficiency. Featuring fused ladder structures (usually over five rings) for potentially reducing the reorganization energy of molecules, the derived FREAs have expanded from 5 rings to 11 rings to utilize solar photos from visible to NIR. As thus, some efficient FREAs with medium/narrow $E _ { \mathbf { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } } \mathbf { s }$ (ITIC [72], INPIC [90], IMC6-4F [94], etc.) have been developed and the PCE has exceed $1 8 \%$ [145]. However, the commercial application of organic photovoltaics needs to take some other factors into account such as synthesis complexity and cost consumption. Apart from considerable PCE, the FREAs' complex synthesis and high cost will undoubtedly limit its further development. For example, the synthesis of the simplest IDT-cored FREA already has over four steps, which may also face low yield. To solve this challenge, acceptors with non-fused cores have caught our attention and began to shine. Derived from fused IDT, a novel non-fused core was developed by flanking two thiophene units on the benzene. End capping with IC end groups, a non-fused-ring acceptor (NFRA) named Ph-IC was synthesized (Figure 4.20) [146]. In Ph-IC, long alkoxy chain ensures the solubility of acceptor, while O-H and O-S non-covalent interactions limit the rotation of chemical bond for good backbone co-planarity. In terms of optical properties, Ph-IC has a significantly deep HOMO of $- 5 . 7 2 \mathrm { e V }$ and shallow LUMO of $- 3 . 7 9 \mathrm { e V } ,$ which is not conducive to hole transport and high $V _ { \mathrm { o c . } }$ The resultant OSCs blending with PBFTZ only presented a moderate PCE of $5 . 6 8 \%$ (Table 4.8).

Setting aside prejudices about low efficiency of Ph-IC, Chen and coworkers [147] adopted its simple structure for further molecular optimization. End-capped with IC-2F, several simple NFRAs were thus synthesized by introducing alkyl side chain at $\beta$ position of thiophene including hydrogen (PTICH), hexyl (PTIC), and hexyloxy (PTICO) (Figure 4.20). As displayed in Figure 4.21a, single-bond-linked NFRAs will cause different conformations due to the rotation of the bond. For PT rotamer (connecting fragments of benzene and thiophene), O-H geometry has a small rotation energy barrier of $4 . 4 \mathrm { k J } \mathrm { m o l } ^ { - 1 }$ than O-S geometry, suggesting $\mathrm { O - H }$ geometry is the energetically preferential conformation. Nevertheless, this $\mathrm { O - H }$ dominant conformation is thermodynamically convertible, and the hydrogen bond can be broken when the PT fragmentation barrier is overcome by heating up, which has been proven by temperature-dependent $^ 1 \mathrm { H }$ NMR (Figure 4.21b). For TIC rotamer (connecting fragments of thiophene and 2F-IC), rotamer based on substituted thiophene and 2F-IC exhibited a higher energy barrier of $4 5 \mathrm { k J } \mathrm { m o l } ^ { - 1 }$ than thiophene-based counterpart $( 6 . 2 5 \mathrm { k J m o l ^ { - 1 } } )$ , and the terminal single bond shows less rotation tendency. When choosing polymer PM6 as a donor, the PM6:PTIC achieved a champion PCE of $1 0 . 2 7 \%$ with a high a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 7 3 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an impressive FF of 0.660, outperforming PTICH- and PTICO-based counterparts $4 . 0 8 \%$ and $6 . 6 2 \%$ , respectively). The high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ can be attributed to the narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p } 1 }$ of PTIC than the other two. However, the Stokes shift (SS) measurement showed the SS values of NFRAs are higher than that of FREA ID-4F in solution, suggesting NFRAs are prone to more non-radiation energy loss. And this loss is significantly reduced due to changes in molecular packing after film formation.

In order to adjust packing for low energy loss, selecting cyclopentadithiophene (CPDT) as flanked building blocks, Bo and coworkers [148] thus designed a series of NFRAs by attaching diversity alkyl chains into intermediate benzene including hexyl (DC6-IC), hexyloxy (DOC6-IC), octyloxy (DOC8-IC), and 2-ethyl-hexyl (DOC2C6-IC) (Figure 4.20). All three alkoxy-substituted NFRAs presented upshifted energy levels than DC6-IC. In addition, O-S intramolecular interaction locks planar conformation to promote $\pi$ -electron delocalization for extended conjugation, endowing alkoxy-substituted NFRAs narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ (1.39-1.44 eV). Morphology analysis found that alkoxy-substituted NFRAs showed shorter $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance of $1 . 7 \mathring \mathrm { A } ^ { - 1 }$ than DC6-IC $( 3 . 7 \mathring \mathrm { A } )$ , and preferred face-on orientation can be observed only in DOC6-IC and DOC2C6-IC neat films. Besides, more efficient exciton dissociation can occur in PBDB-T:DOC6-IC and PBDB-T:DOC2C6-IC due to their smaller domain size than the other two devices. As a result, the PBDB-T:DOC2C6-IC-based OSCs delivered a highest PCE of $1 1 . 1 0 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { V }$ and a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 8 . 8 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , exceeding the PCEs $( 6 . 8 7 - 1 0 . 5 2 \%$ $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ over $0 . 9 0 \mathrm { V }$ ) of several others (Table 4.8). It can be noted that these high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } \mathrm { \bf s }$ at a solar cell with around $9 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ NIR absorption is rare, and the energy loss analysis was thus carried out. As shown (Figure 4.21c,d), emission of the neat film and their blends are approximative, and no apparent subgap absorption feature was observed, indicating the occurrence of small energy loss. The non-radiative recombination losses of NFRAs-based OSCs were finally calculated to be around $0 . 2 \mathrm { e V }$ $\mathrm { 0 } . 3 \mathrm { e V }$ for DC6-IC-based device), which is comparable to inorganic solar cells. Then the difluorinated end group strategy was employed to strengthen ICT effect and absorption, and an outstanding PCE of $1 3 . 2 4 \%$ was obtained by PBDB-T:DOC2C6-2F-based device with an enhanced $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 1 . 3 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ (Table 4.8).

Coincidentally, Chen's group [149] designed a novel NFRA named DF-PCIC (Figure 4.20) by inserting fluorine atoms onto the intermediate benzene. The DF-PCIC exhibited HOMO/LUMO energy levels of $- 5 . 4 8 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 7 7 \mathrm { e V }$ and a narrow $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 5 9 \mathrm { e V } .$ Besides, DF-PCIC features a low crystallinity, which can be strengthened after the thermal annealing treatment for higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF induced by the formation of bicontinuous crystalline networks in corresponding blend films. The optimal PCE of $1 0 . 1 4 \%$ can be achieved under the condition of $0 . 5 \%$ CN additive and $1 3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ annealing temperature. More interestingly, after thermal annealing at $1 8 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for three hours, uniform film can be preserved in PBDB-T:DF-PCIC-based blend (Figure 4.21e), suggesting good thermal stability. In contrast, PBDB-T $\mathrm { \mathrm { : P C } } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ blend appeared granular agglomerations which is unbearable to stand the high temperature for a long time. For further extending photos harvesting, 2F-ICs are end-capped into the above core DF-PCIC used, and the HF-PCIC was developed [150]. In order to explore the effect of intermediate core unit on device properties, the other two NFRAs are synthesized as comparison by substituted two fluorine atoms (OF-PCIC) and two methoxy groups (HFO-PCIC) (Figure 4.20). In relative to HF-PCIC $( - 5 . 5 3 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 8 3 \mathrm { e V }$ for HOMO/LUMO), OF-PCIC has deeper energy levels $( - 5 . 6 6 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 8 6 \mathrm { e V } )$ due to the introduced two strongly electronegative fluorine atoms on intermediate benzene, while the methoxy slightly upshifted the energy levels of HFO-PCIC $( - 5 . 5 0 \mathrm { e V } / - 3 . 8 1 \mathrm { e V } )$ . As film formation, all three NFRAs have a strong absorption at $5 0 0 { - } 8 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ with molar absorption coefficient of $\sim 2 . 0 0 \times 1 0 ^ { 5 } \mathrm { M ^ { - 1 } c m ^ { - 1 } }$ , and the HFO-PCIC shows the maximum $\lambda _ { \mathrm { o n s e t } }$ of $8 3 8 \mathrm { n m }$ $( E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 8 \mathrm { e V } ,$ . Single-crystal data indicated that the $\mathrm { F - H }$ non-covalent effect is the first choice, but it also includes the coexistence of other non-covalent effects, which affects the dihedral angles between benzene and CPDT for diversity aggregation behavior. When mixed with PM6, the highly crystalline HFO-PCIC caused a severe aggregation of the blend film, which destroyed the interpenetrating network constructed by the donor, resulting in the poor PCE of $8 . 3 6 \%$ in corresponding device. On the contrary, more smooth surfaces can be observed in HF-PCICand OF-PCIC-based blends with small RMS, and the PM6:HF-PCIC-based OSCs delivered a champion PCE of $1 0 . 9 7 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 2 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 6 . 0 1 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a FF of 0.724. Considering the weak crystallinity of HF-PCIC and the low boiling point of chloroform (CF), CF was used instead of chlorobenzene (CB) for solution spin coating to improve crystallinity. The GIwAxS showed that the PM6:HF-PCIC blend film spin coating with CF presented stronger lamellar peaks, suggesting enhanced crystallinity for optimized $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 7 . 8 1 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ . The PCE was thus increased to $1 1 . 4 9 \%$ (Table 4.8). After that, a novel NFRA named HF-TCIC was developed by Chen and coworkers with 3,4-difluorothiophene as central core [151]. The electron cloud distribution displayed that HOMO mainly located at the intermediate cores and LUMO is determined by the end groups at both ends. Therefore, in relative to HF-PCIC, the weakened electron-donating core endows HF-TCIC deeper HOMO energy level $( \mathrm { { \sim } 0 . 1 \mathrm { { e V } ) } }$ , corresponding to a wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 6 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ With an optimal donor: acceptor weight ratio $( 1 : 1 . 2 )$ , the device fabricated with PBDB-T:HF-TCIC active layer achieved a moderate PCE of $9 . 8 6 \%$ after adding $0 . 5 \%$ 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) and appropriate thermal annealing at $1 2 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$

It is noted from above that the modification of core is one of the most direct and effective methods for manipulating device properties. In addition, different from the rigid skeleton of FREAs, the modules making up the non-fused-ring skeleton are prone to a certain deflection due to steric hindrance. Therefore, side chain engineering on the core can also adjust the dihedral angle between the modules to change molecular packing for efficient NFRAs. Apart from above two, isomerization is also a strategy worth trying. As thus, linking CPDT at the 2,6- and 1,5-positions of naphthalene, two mutually isomer acceptors, NOC6F-1 and NOC6F-2 (Figure 4.20), were designed and synthesized by Bo and coworkers [152]. The steric hindrance induced by diverse connection modes provides these two isomers with distinguishing intermolecular $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking, leading to different absorption in the solid state. The as-developed NOC6F-1 thus has a ca. $4 8 \mathrm { n m }$ red-shifted absorption than NOC6F-2 $7 3 6 \mathrm { n m } )$ , corresponding to a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 5 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ Morphological study revealed that both films blended with PBDB-T exhibited nanostructured interpenetrating networks, and more compact $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking can be observed in NOC6F-1-based blend. As a result, more efficient charge carrier generation and transportation were achieved for the PBDB-T:NOC6F-1, leading to a higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 7 . 0 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , a FF of 0.658 and thus a higher PCE of $1 0 . 6 2 \%$ (Table 4.8). NOC6F-2-based OCSs obtained only $6 . 7 4 \%$ PCE. These results demonstrated that isomerization is also an effective way to explore high-performing NFRAs.

It is well known that the elements of the same main group have similar chemical properties, and the larger atomic number has a larger atomic radius, which is more conducive to electron delocalization. Therefore, $^ { 4 , 4 ^ { \prime } }$ -dioctyl-dithieno $[ 3 , 2 - b ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime }$ $d ]$ silole (DTS) was employed as flanked blocks. To prevent over-intermolecular aggregation, Chen and coworkers utilized 4,8-bis(5-ethylhexyl-2-thienyl)-benzo[1,2- $b { : } 4 , 5 { - } b { ' }$ |dithiophene (BDTT) as the central core, and two acceptors BDTS-4Cl and BDTC-4Cl (CPDT flanked) were synthesized (Figure 4.20) [153]. Both

NFRAs exhibited a strong absorption to NIR, and the BDTC-4Cl even has a $\lambda _ { \mathrm { o n s e t } }$ of $8 7 3 \mathrm { n m }$ with a narrower $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of $1 . 4 2 \mathrm { e V } .$ Consequently, more balanced $\mu _ { \mathrm { h } } / \mu _ { \mathrm { e } } = 1 . 6 1$ was obtained (3.13 for BDTs-4Cl-based blend), contributing to the PBDB-T:BDTC-4Cl-based OSCs a PCE of $9 . 5 4 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 6 \mathrm { V }$ and a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 8 . 5 6 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ . The poor efficiency of PBDB-T:BDTS-4Cl $( 3 . 7 3 \% )$ can be attributed to the low $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ induced by the deeper LUMO energy level and wider $E _ { \mathrm { g } } ^ { \mathrm { \ o p t } }$ of BDTS-4Cl. After adding $3 3 . 3 \% \ \mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ as a third component, the morphology with nanofibrous interpenetrating network is clearly visible, and the enhanced $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF increase the PCE to $1 2 . 1 9 \%$

# 4.4 A-DA'D-A-Type SMAs

As mentioned above, A-D-A-structured SMAs are extremely promising since they exhibit strong intramolecular charge transfer effect, superior energy level tunability, and good molecular crystallinity. Based on this successful design strategy, in 2017, Zou et al. developed a series of curve-shaped NFAs with an A-DA'D-A structure by inserting electron-withdrawing unit, such as benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) and benzo[d][1,2,3]triazoles (BTA), into the donor core as its fused-ring central unit.

In order to distinguish the A-D-A-type molecules, Zou and colleagues summarize several important features of A-DA'D-A-type SMAs: (i) the single crystal of the A-DA'D-A molecules confirms that the molecules configuration is an excellent combination of a ladder-type electron-deficient-core-based central fused-ring $\mathrm { ( D A ^ { \prime } D ) }$ , electron-accepting end group (A), and two $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 }$ -hybridized nitrogen atoms in the pyrrole motif of the fused ring in a C2 symmetric manner. Thus, the alkyl side chains onto the $N$ -atoms of the pyrrole motif could greatly influence the stacking of adjacent molecules; (ii) the slight twist $\mathrm { D A ^ { \prime } D }$ core has to be sterically hindered to prevent over aggregation and, at the same time, maintain an efficient intramolecular interaction due to the multiple $\mathrm { D } { - } \mathbf { A }$ interactions. Compared with the A-D-A molecules (like ITIC-series), it do not need to synthesize spiro-like structures; instead, the sterically hindered side chains adopt an orthogonal conformation to the main plane; (iii) with the specific molecular geometry of the $\mathbf { A } \mathbf { - } \mathbf { D } \mathbf { A } ^ { \prime } \mathbf { D - } \mathbf { A }$ family, the dimerization could be formed in a unit with a large quadrupole moment. Moreover, the relatively narrow density of state (DOs) both in the electron affinity and ionization energy could lead to a trap-free ambipolar transport. Such a high quantum efficiency in A-DA'D-A-type SMAs, coupled with high electroluminescence quantum efficiency, makes it possible to deliver high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , high FF, and also low voltage losses at the same time under one sun conditions.

Now we know that one of the most important features in design strategy of A-DA'D-A-type SMAs is to introduce an electron-deficient segment in the middle of the central core to form a fused $\mathrm { D A ^ { \prime } D }$ structure. Therefore, in this contribution, we will systematically review A-DA'D-A-type SMAs based on different electron-deficient segments $( \mathrm { A } ^ { \prime } )$ , such as BTA, BT, benzo[c][1,2,5]selenadiazole (BSe), and quinoxaline $\left( \mathbf { Q x } \right)$

# 4.4.1 BTA-Based A-DA'D-A SMAs

Since the first $\mathrm { \Delta A { - } D A ^ { \prime } D { - } A }$ pentacyclic SMA BZIC [154] by inserting an electron-withdrawing unit (benzo[d][1,2,3]triazoles, BTA) in the core of its fused-ring central unit reported in 2017, the electron-deficient-core-based fused ring opens a new door in the molecular design of high-performance acceptors. Compared to the classical A-D-A-type SMA ITIC [72], BZIC showed a red-shift absorption (c. $8 0 \mathrm { n m } ,$ and higher absorption coefficient. The wide absorption range makes the active layers absorb more photons, giving rise to a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$

After that, Yang and Zou extended the fused central ring by using a thieno[3,2-b] thiophene instead of a thiophene segment, and synthesized a new SMA Y1 (Figure 4.22) in collaboration with Prof. Gao's group from Linkoping University [155]. By introducing the central fused ring from pentacyclic to heptacycilc, the HOMO energy level and absorption of Y1 match well with those of the commercial donor polymer PBDB-T. As a result, the PBDB-T:Y1-based device afforded a high PCE of $1 3 . 4 0 \%$ with an impressive $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 2 . 4 4 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 8 \mathrm { V } ,$ and an FF of $6 9 . 1 \%$ (Table 4.9). The high performance was attributed to the relatively high electroluminescence quantum efficiency $( \mathrm { E Q E _ { E L } } ,$ ) of approximately $0 . 5 \times 1 0 ^ { - 4 }$ which indicated low nonradiative recombination loss of the blend. Later, in order to further narrow the bandgap of Y1 to obtain more photons, Y2 and Y3 (Figure 4.22) were designed and synthesized by using the dicyanomethylene derivatives (CPTCN and INCN-2F) [156]. By modifying the end group of Y1, the target SMAs Y2 and Y3 exhibited red-shifted absorption onset of 25 and $4 3 \mathrm { n m }$ , respectively. The Y2- and Y3-based devices showed the similar PCE of $1 3 . 4 0 \%$ and $1 3 . 2 4 \%$ with the $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of 23.56 and $2 4 . 1 0 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ when matched with polymer donor PBDB-T and PM6, respectively. Although the red-shift of the SMA absorption can reduce the bandgap for high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the devices will also decrease concomitantly. Hence, balancing this trade-off between $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ is a challenge.

To compensate for the trade-off between $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ , side chain engineering is an effective strategy for manipulating energy levels and meanwhile maintain the similar absorption. Wu and Zou added two "wings" (undecyl side chains) onto the terminal of the $\mathrm { D A ^ { \prime } D }$ core of Y3 to obtain a new SMA Y11 [157]. The optical absorption onset of Y11-based active layer is sharp, with an Urbach energy of $2 5 { - } 2 7 \mathrm { m e V }$ which is closer to the properties of classic inorganic semiconductors, such as crystalline silicon or organometallic lead-halide perovskite. The devices exhibited a high $\mathrm { E Q E } _ { \mathrm { E L } }$ of $0 . 1 4 \%$ , corresponding to a low nonradiative recombination loss of $0 . 1 7 \mathrm { e V } .$ As a direct consequence, an improved PCE of $1 6 . 5 4 \%$ and a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 5 \mathrm { V }$ with a significantly decreased voltage loss ( $\boldsymbol { V } _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ loss) of $0 . 5 1 \mathrm { e V }$ were achieved in the Y11-based device. Moreover, Y11 has high electron mobility due to the stable molecular conformation and rigid backbone. The mobility in OSC devices influences charge transport and recombination, consequently affecting the device performance, especially the FF. Although Y11 has made great success, the FF of Y11-based devices is only $7 3 . 1 \%$ , which still has much room for improvement. A high FF requires balanced mobilities of electrons and holes. To optimize the electron mobilities of Y11, Zou and coworkers performed molecular structure tailoring by reducing the alkyl chains from $n$ -undecyl to $n$ -hexyl on $\beta$ position of the $\mathrm { D A ^ { \prime } D }$ core that affords Y18 [158]. The reduced alkyl chains length of Y18-based BHJ blend showed more balanced hole and electron mobilities than Y11-based blend films, and therefore, resulting in the higher FF value of $7 6 . 4 \%$ in the OSCs. In order to further study the relation between the structure and properties, a series of alkylated BTA-based SMAs with various end groups (Y9, Y14, Y15, and Y16) were designed and synthesized [159-162].
