# Chlorinated Organic Solar Cells

Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu, and Feng He

Southern University of Science and Technology, Department of Chemistry, 1088 Xueyuan Blvd., Nanshan District, Shenzhen 518055, P.R. China

# 6.1 Introduction

Organic photovoltaic technology has attracted increasing interest over the past decade due to its synthetic versatility, low temperature processing, low material cost, light weight, and flexible application [1-6]. In recent years, based on material innovation and device technology progress, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OsCs) has exceeded $1 8 \%$ [1, 3, 4, 6]. Among them, D-A (donor-acceptor) type polymer donors and new non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) greatly promote the improvement of PCE. The efficient polymer donors with D and A structural units own strong absorption in visible region due to the enhanced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) from the push-pull of electrons between unit D and unit A. Various strategies of molecular design for novel D-A type polymers have been developed [7-10].

In past decade, the polymer donors in OsCs have mainly been the D-A type copolymers. The band gap of these polymers is regulated by the backbone, side-chain and molecular interaction. The typical characteristics include the alternating D-A units and quinoidal resonance structures. Besides, the acceptor-donor-acceptor (A-D-A) type small-molecule acceptors greatly contributed photocurrent in OSCs resulting from their strong light-harvesting capability compared to the conventional fullerene derivatives. The novel NFAs such as ITIC [11] and Y6 [12] derivatives have the extensive absorption in visible and near infrared (NIR) region to generate high short-circuit current density $( J _ { \mathrm { s c } } )$ and matched energy level to produce high open-circuit voltage $( V _ { \mathrm { o c } } )$

In design of materials, fluorination was extensively applied in donors and NFAs in recent years [13-15]. The fluorination lowers the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level of materials, improving the open-circuit voltage $( V _ { \mathrm { o c } } )$ of their polymer solar cells (PsCs). Although the fluorination is a practical way to enhance performance of photovoltaic device, the low yields of products, fussy reaction steps, and use of hazardous regents are the deficiencies of fluorination [16, 17]. To conquer these issues, an alternative method is chlorination. Among halogens, fluorine is the most electrophilic and with the smallest atom size. Chlorine with a larger atom radius is the second most electrophilic. In analogous circumstance, the chlorination reveals the similar affects as the fluorination in polymers and solar cells; meanwhile, the synthesis of the chlorinated polymers is facile [18-22]. Besides, chlorine contains empty 3d orbitals that can accept lone pair electrons or $\pi$ -electrons through Cl. . .S or $\mathbf { C l } \cdot \mathbf { \partial } \cdot \boldsymbol { \pi }$ noncovalent interactions, while fluorine can not [21-26]. Moreover, the dipole moment of the carbon-chlorine (C-Cl) bond is larger than that of the carbon-fluorine (C-F) bond according to density function theory (DFT) calculation. The large dipole moment of C--Cl bond facilitates the charge transport due to the enhanced ICT effect. He and coworkers designed and prepared many chlorinated polymer donors and NFAs in PSCs [2, 23-37].

In this chapter, we first introduce the characteristics of the chlorination and fluorination. Then, the research progress of chlorinated polymer and small-molecule donors, and small-molecule NFAs are summarized.

# 6.2 Chlorination Versus Fluorination: A Comprehensive Study

The effects of chlorination are comprehensive on the polymer donors and smallmolecule acceptors. The main characteristics of the chlorination versus fluorination are summarized in this section, which would be beneficial to deeply understand the chlorination in organic photovoltaics.

# 6.2.1  Synthesis

The main advantages of chlorination are high yield and low cost. The synthesis steps are few, the reaction conditions are mild, and the products are easy to purify [22, 38]. Introducing Cl into organic semiconductors is much easier than that of F. F are usually introduced through halogen-exchange reactions under strict conditions. And the yield is relatively low [39-42].

For example, the donor molecules PBDB-T-2Cl and PBDB-TF have very similar structures, and the difference is that PBDB-T-2F has fluorinated thiophene while PBDB-T-2Cl owns a side chain of chlorinated thiophene in a side chain. The synthetic routes of two polymers were systematically compared and analyzed in literature [22]. They were finally polymerized using the same method. The key precursors of PBDB-TF and PBDB-T-2Cl both rooted in BDT-T-based monomers in Figure 6.1. However, their syntheses are quite different. The fluorinated BDT-T-based monomer need four steps, resulting in high synthetic cost. Compared to the fluorinated BDT-T-based monomer, the chlorinated BDT-T-based monomer was facilely prepared from the low-cost 3-chlorothiophene raw material. The yield was high. From above, the synthesis cost of PBDT-T-2Cl is much lower than that of

![](images/265c42106d8c7324b4c2b6b7868e0943660848b027445abee909e488bda58bd9.jpg)  
Figure 6.1The key routes of PBDB-T-2Cl and PBDB-TF polymers. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu and Feng He.

PBDB-TF. Both as a promising photovoltaic material, the PBDB-T-2Cl has greater commercialization potential.

# 6.2.2 The Manipulation of Energy Level and Absorption

As halogen elements, the chlorine and fluorine had similar electronic structure and strong electronegativity. When they were introduced into the semiconductor molecule, the energy level and absorption spectra of material were largely changed. They could generate some similar effects on the HOMO and LUMO levels of molecule. And, the positions of chlorination and fluorination in molecule were diversified, optional sites could appear in donor or acceptor unit [15, 43, 44], even $\pi$ bridge [45] in donor and acceptor materials. However, the final $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ in device is up to the HOMO of donors and LUMO of acceptors [46, 47]. From our study, the influence of chlorine substitution is more obvious than that of fluorine substitution in terms of energy-level regulation. Although the electronegativity of fluorine was stronger than chlorine, the Cl with 3d empty orbitals could accommodate delocalized $\pi$ -electrons [20]. In the benzo $[ b ]$ thiophene material system, Bao and coworkers used molecular orbital diagrams to demonstrate that chlorination is more effective than fluorination in manipulation of HOMO and LUMO energy levels.

Changes in energy levels usually result in changes in the spectrum, and the effects of chlorination and fluorination on absorption are also complicated. In different material systems, similar positions of substitution produce very different results. For instance, the difluorothiophene in PBDT[2F]T and PGeTFDTBT [48, 49], the spectra shifts are disparate. Generally, the induced electron-withdrawing properties of fluorination bring about declined electron density in conjugated polymer, increasing the HOMO-LUMO bandgap [50-53]. Consequently, related absorption spectra present the blue-shift trend. But in some materials, as intramolecular F-H, F-F, and/or F. . .S interactions induced the fluorination enhance conjugation length, leading to the red-shift of absorption spectra [54-60]. In some special cases, two interactions exist in molecule, the spectral shift is rooted in the result of the two competitive mechanisms. Taking account of the molecular aggregations, fluorination enhance the intermolecular interactions generating red-shift in solution, which could be demonstrated by temperature-dependent absorption spectra. Based on some results of reported fluorinated copolymer donors, the fluorination causes a spectral blue-shift in most cases [61-84]. As for chlorination, according to the reported work, the trend is like that of fluorination. Regarding chlorination, the trend is like that of fluorination due to the relative lack of reported literature. However, the causes and mechanisms of spectral changes are different. The increase in steric hindrance is a factor for the blue-shift of the chlorination [31-36]. In small-molecule acceptors, fluorination and chlorination on end groups are much simplified compared to polymers, they all cause a red-shift of the spectrum in most cases [85-88]. At present, there are many reasons for the redshift. The mainstream explanations include the enhanced IACT effect [36], the inductance effect on the empty 3d orbital of chlorine, the delocalization of electrons and the increase of dipole moment [89-95]. In terms of extinction coefficient, both chlorination and fluorination can improve the extinction coefficient of organic semiconductors.

# 6.2.3 The Steric Hindrance and Morphology

Because the van der Waals radius of fluorine is just $1 . 4 7 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ the influence of steric hindrance could be ignored. But the van der Waals radius of chlorine is much larger, up to $1 . 7 6 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ . Generally, the strong electronegativity of $\mathrm { F }$ leads to the interaction between noncovalent molecules. With the different positions of chlorination, the situation of the chlorination reaction is more complicated and diverse, which determines the steric hindrance produced by the chlorination. In the case of large steric hindrance, the chlorination will distort the molecular configuration and reduce the crystallinity. Through some molecular designs, under the condition of reducing steric hindrance, the chlorination strengthens the interaction between molecules due to strong noncovalent interactions, such as Cl.. .S and $\mathrm { C l } \cdot \cdot \pi$

The dihedral angle between adjacent conjugated units is a key factor affecting the aggregation and morphology of conjugated polymers [54, 96, 97]. Introduction of chlorine atoms into the backbone of the conjugated polymer can increase the dihedral angle between adjacent conjugated units. For example, our previous research pointed out that in the PBDTClBT polymer, the dihedral angle of monochlorinated BT and Th that are close to each other is $5 3 . 1 3 ^ { \circ }$ , while the dihedral angle of monochlorinated BT and Th that are far apart is only $1 8 . 3 1 ^ { \circ }$ . Besides, the dihedral angle between Th near chlorine and adjacent BDT units is also just $2 0 . 0 5 ^ { \circ }$ [30]. A special case is that Pei and coworkers studied the strong preaggregation of F-IIDT in solution due to the interaction between the backbones of polymer, resulting in a large number of crystal fields without the preferred crystal orientation, and the chlorination changed the torsion angle to optimize crystallization of films and face-on orientation of molecular, generating a high PCE of Cl-IIDT-based devices [54].

Without considering other factors, the increase of the dihedral angle will destroy the coplanarity of the molecular framework and the IACT of the crystal. This is very important to D-A type organic semiconductors and is not conducive to the improvement of photoelectric performance. In order to reduce the influence of steric hindrance caused by chlorination, two methods containing chlorinated conjugated side chain and end group are usually adopted.

Hou and coworkers calculated the dihedral fluorination and chlorination of Th-based side group and BDT unit, the results pointed out that the two dihedral angles are the same, $5 3 ^ { \circ }$ in Figure 6.2 [22]. Chen and coworkers chlorinated the Th side chain of BDT in PBDT-Cl-3T2C polymer, the dihedral angle between backbone and side chain had a little increase [98]. Therefore, the effects on the dihedral angle between adjacent units were small.

Chlorination of end group is mainly used in non-fullerene small-molecule acceptor material systems. In this way, chlorinated materials can obtain a better coplanar structure [37, 99]. For example, Wei and coworkers used X-rays to analyze the single-crystal structure of $m$ -ITIC-OR-4Cl, the chlorinated end group molecule showed an approximate coplanar geometric structure [99]. The study of Hou and coworkers showed that the chlorinated end groups did not cause much change to the optimized molecular configuration, indicating that the steric hindrance effect of the chlorine atoms on the end groups in some material systems is not obvious. He and coworkers prepared two new molecules chlorinated IDIC-4Cl and fluorinated IDIC-4F, respectively. They analyzed the single-crystal structure and systematically studied the influence of the addition of F and Cl on the molecular configuration and packing. The data of single-crystal analysis show that the dihedral angles between the IDT core of IDIC-4H, IDIC-4F, and IDIC-4Cl and the corresponding IC end groups are $1 4 . 9 ^ { \circ }$ $1 6 . 3 ^ { \circ }$ , and $9 . 0 ^ { \circ }$ , respectively [35]. The addition of F slightly changed the distortion of the molecule, and the chlorination reduced the dihedral angle of the molecule. Although the atomic radius of Cl is larger than that of F, the chlorinated end groups will not cause distortion and accumulation of molecules. The $\pi { - } \pi$ distance of IDIC-4Cl with an interlocked network configuration is $3 . 4 1 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ in Figure 6.3. Compared with the other two molecules, there is a stronger $\mathrm { C l } \cdot \cdot \mathrm { \bf \cdot S }$ interaction among the molecules. Moreover, the adjacent IDIC-4Cl molecules are almost completely parallel, while the dihedral angles between the IDT cores of IDIC-4H and IDIC-4F are $2 0 . 8 ^ { \circ }$ and $1 9 . 3 ^ { \circ }$ respectively. The chlorinated DIC-4Cl molecule has good coplanarity, which is very conducive to the separation of excitons and the transfer of charges. There are also chlorine-substituted small molecules with smaller dihedral angles in other material systems [37].

# 6.2.4 The Synergistic Effect of Chlorination and Fluorination

Both chlorination and fluorination are effective strategies to improve the PCE of PSCs. The introduction of chlorine and fluorine atoms into certain material systems can combine their advantages. Some research groups have studied the synergistic effects of chlorination and fluorination.

The well-known D-A polymers (PTB) with TT and BDT units [100-103], such as PTB7 and PTB7-Th, were vastly studied. However, the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of PTB7 and

![](images/c8eec22e7dc333263eee40c77c0875ffc88d29e1088b69aa48e5bf214aff90bc.jpg)  
Figure 6.3X-ray crystallographic structures of (a) IDIC-4H, (b) IDIC4F, and (c) IDIC-4Cl. ( represents the dihedral angles between IDT cores of adjacent molecules). Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu and Feng He.

PTB7-Th-based PSCs are moderate, no more than $0 . 8 0 \mathrm { V }$ in general. For this reason, some new series chlorinated polymers named $\mathrm { P B T C l } _ { x }$ were designed and synthesized in He's group [27], the corresponding molecular structure is shown in Figure 6.4. The chlorinated TT (TT-Cl) was firstly brought in PTB family conjugated polymers. The optoelectronic properties of polymers and corresponding performance parameters of PSCs are summarized in Table 6.1. Remarkably, the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the terpolymer $\mathrm { P B T C l } _ { x }$ solar cells could be finely tuned from 0.79 to $0 . 9 2 \mathrm { V }$ via varying the content of TT-Cl units in terpolymer (Table 6.1). The effects of chlorination and fluorination on photovoltaic performance are different. F can lower the HOMO of the molecule without causing harmful steric effects. Cl can deepen the HOMO energy level more. However, it destroys the planarity of the polymer and affects the morphology, leading to poor $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF of devices. Considering the impact of chlorination and fluorination on the performance of the device, our group adopted a ternary polymerization strategy to synthesize a series of terpolymer $\mathrm { P B T C l } _ { x }$ With $2 5 \%$ Cl content in polymer, the PTBCl25-based device exhibited superior hole mobility and external quantum efficiency (EQE) response among all polymers. From the grazing incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GiwAX) analysis, the introduction of chlorine enlarges $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance in the activelayer. According to the calculated full width at half-maximum (FwHM) of scattering peaks, the $\mathrm { P B T C l } _ { 2 5 }$ -based film presents the highest crystallinity among all polymers. The optimal device based on $\mathrm { P B T C l } _ { 2 5 }$ had a decent efficiency of $8 . 3 1 \%$ which was higher than the PTB7-Th control device $( 7 . 9 1 \% )$

The synergistic effect of chlorination and fluorination has also been verified in other systems. Our group synthesized PCBT4T-2BO and PCBT4T-2OD by introducing chlorine into the position of the acceptor unit benthiadiazole on the backbone. PSCs based on these polymers and $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ were fabricated [29]. In terms of energy-level adjustment, chlorine can lower the energy level more effectively than fluorine, thereby further increasing $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . We also synthesized PCFBT4T-2OD, a polymer containing both fluorine and chlorine. The $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of PCFBT4T-2OD cells was further increased to $1 7 . 6 1 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and the PCE was up to $8 . 8 4 \%$ . Compared with PCBT4T-2BO with monochlorine, the introduction of fluorine atoms into the polymer further enhances the $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking, which is beneficial to the transport of charges in the active layer and improves the device performance of PsCs. These results all indicate that the synergistic effect of chlorination and fluorination is good for improving the efficiency of PSCs.

# 6.3 Recent Advances in Chlorinated Semiconductors

When chlorination just entered the field of organic optoelectronics, it was mainly used for the high and balanced bipolar transportation of organic field effect transistors (OFETs), because chlorination can lower the LUMO energy level, reduce the electrons of the charge injection barrier, and make electrons and holes could be transmitted at the same time. According to the research of Bao and coworkers, if the chlorination does not break the planarization of the conjugated core, the chlorinated molecule usually has a slightly smaller gap between the HOMO and LUMO energy levels and is even lower than the corresponding fluorine-containing LUMO, because Cl has an empty 3d orbital to fit the core of $\mathfrak { \pi }$ electron conjugation [20], while the fluorine atom does not have these unique properties. Since 2015, the application of chlorination in OSCs has received increasing attention [54, 104]. In just five years, the PCE of chlorine-based OSCs increased from $1 \%$ to $1 8 \%$ [22, 105].

# 6.3.1 Chlorination on the Donor Units of Polymer Donors

Chlorination of polymer is an effective way to increase the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the device, because the chlorine atom has a strong electronegativity and the ability to accommodate delocalized electrons, which can effectively reduce the HOMO and LUMO energy levels. The current high-performance D-A copolymer donor materials usually consist of D units, A units and functional groups to improve the solubility of the polymer. In order to reduce the influence of steric hindrance, it is sometimes necessary to build $\pi$ -bridge between the D and A units to improve the coplanarity of the molecules. In some cases, the coplanarity of backbone can be enhanced by modifying the conjugated side chain, thereby expanding the range of the absorption spectrum [1o0]. With the comprehensive study of chlorination reactions, chlorination is now introduced into D units, A units, $\pi$ -bridges, and conjugated side chains, which will be discussed separately.

# 6.3.1.1 Chlorination of the Donor Units in Backbone of Polymer Donors

Benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']-dithiophene (BDT) is currently one of the most used D units in high-performance D-A polymers. In 2016, Lavarda and coworkers synthesized 24 kinds of PTB7 series derivatives [106], which were substituted by choosing different substituents and different positions on the PTB7 monomer in Chart 6.1. According to the characterization results of electronic and optical properties, chlorinated polymers have good application prospects in OSCs. Among the three chlorinated PTB7 derivatives, PTB7-Cl-12 and $\mathrm { P C } _ { 6 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ have the best application prospects in OSCs because their parameters are close to the ideal values of $E _ { \mathrm { H O M O } }$ $E _ { \mathrm { L U M O } }$ and $\Delta E _ { \mathrm { H L } }$ which indicates that its $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ is greater than PTB7.

![](images/8063a16e6b9f546896a4756bb6531cd14cd86a14ed8622b7fe145e22955c0d11.jpg)  
Chart 6.1 Polymer donor-based chlorinated D unit backbone. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui $\mathsf { P u }$ , and Feng He.

Thiophene (Th) is also general and typical D unit. He and coworkers chlorinated a thiophene in the middle position in the benzothiazolyl-based tetrathiophene polymer to synthesize a new polymer donor PBT4T-Cl (see Chart 6.1). OSCs based on PBT4T-Cl have a better performance than the control analog without Cl, the excellent PCE was up to $1 1 . 8 \%$ and the related stability was also outstanding [23]. This is mainly because the 4-position chlorination reaction of thiophene in the middle will reduce the HOMO level of the polymer, but the twist on the backbone is very small, which is conducive to maintaining a satisfactory morphology and main orientation. Through DFT calculation, it is found that the dipole moments of the ground state and the excited state of PBT4T-Cl are quite different, indicating that there is less Coulomb binding of excitons. Therefore, the hole and electron mobility of PBT4T-Cl-based devices have been improved from the space charge limited current (SCLC) test. Besides, the chlorination stabilizes the two-phase nanostructure in the active layer and ensure its stability.

# 6.3.1.2 Chlorination of the Donor Units in Side Chain of Polymer Donors

Compared with the chlorination on backbone of the D unit, the chlorination on the side chain has received more attention. Thienyl is a commonly used side chain of conjugated polymers. It is usually applied to BDT units (BDT-T) to improve the coplanarity of the backbone of polymer molecules [1o0]. The current chlorinated side chains are based on the thienyl group in BDT-T [22, 24, 43, 86, 87, 98, 107, 108]. As a donor component of polymer, BDT has the virtues of high degree of conjugation, high planarity, and low steric hindrance. Because the main feature of the BDT-T unit is high planarity, whether the chlorination with a large atomic radius will destroy the planarity is the first issue that needs attention. Hou and coworkers studied the torsion barriers in BDT-T-2F and BDT-T-2Cl from the DFT calculation [22]. According to the results of simulation calculations, BDT-T-2Cl and BDT-T-2F have similar optimal dihedral angles and torsional barriers.

In 2018, He and coworkers chlorinated BDT-T into the classical polymer donor PTB7-Th, replacing BDT-T unit, and resulted a new polymer donor PBClT (see Chart 6.2) [25]. Chlorinated BDT-T did not increase the steric hindrance of the conjugated backbone and disrupt the packing interaction. Because of the unique effect of chlorine atoms, it effectively reduces the level of HOMO and obtains a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ over $1 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ in PBClT-based OSCs. The results of this study show that the side chain chlorination reaction can well control the energy level of the polymer without destroying the $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking interactions among the molecules.

![](images/f0883ec1d171558f21d400f53ae060e836a4b2baa8b31cb22ed1d38b9bccc512.jpg)  
Chart 6.2 Polymer donor-based chlorinated side chain of D unit. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui $\mathsf { P u }$ , and Feng He.

BDTT-alt-DTBTz is a classic D-A molecular skeleton [109-111]. On this basis, side chain engineering and halogenation have been used to synthesize many materials with strong light absorption, ordered molecular packing, and high hole mobility. The chlorination of thiophene side chain in the molecular skeleton has been reported in some literatures [24, 87, 107, 108]. In these material systems, He and coworkers had carefully studied the relationship between the position of chlorination and the number of chlorine atoms and the performance of the device. The results showed that chlorination had a large effect on energy level, absorption coefficient, molecular dipole moment, molecular packing, and film morphology. These comprehensive factors ultimately determined PCE of the device. Four wide-band gap polymers were synthesized, named PBT1Cl-Bz, PBT2Clas-Bz, PBT2Cl-Bz (PBZ-Cl, L68 or J52-Cl), and PBT4Cl-Bz. They have a similar LUMO energy level. As the number of chlorine atoms increases, the energy level gets lower and lower. This is due to the electron- withdrawing effect of chlorine and the covalent interaction between molecules Cl. . .S and $\mathbf { C l } \cdot \mathbf { \partial } \cdot \boldsymbol { \pi }$ causing the blue shift of the absorption. But the LUMO and HOMO energy levels of PBT2Clas-Bz and PBT2Cl-Bz are almost the same. When the number of chlorine atoms is the same, the position of the chlorine atom has little effect on the energy level. However, the temperature aggregation behavior caused by the difference in the position of chlorine atoms is obviously different. PBT4Cl-Bz exhibits the strongest shoulder peak in both solution and film conditions. Compared with the other three molecules, PBT4Cl-Bz has strong aggregation both in solution and film conditions. $\mathrm { P B T } 2 \mathrm { C l } ^ { a s } .$ Bz and PBT4Cl-Bz showed obvious temperature-dependent aggregation characteristics, and their side chains were in the third and fourth positions of the chlorine-substituted side chain. The control of the morphology during the film preparation is very important. The PBT4Cl-Bz-based PSCs reached the PCE of $9 . 2 5 \%$ , high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 9 6 \mathrm { V } ,$ and maintained a good $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ $1 6 . 0 4 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ Due to the deep HOMO energy level, the $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ is only $0 . 5 4 \mathrm { e V } .$ The single-crystal structure of BDT-T2Cl with symmetrical two chlorinated substituents and BDT-T4Cl with four symmetrical chlorinated substituents was analyzed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (see Figure 6.5) and the effect of chlorination on geometry and molecular packing influence. The dihedral angle between Th dichloride and the BDT core in BDT-T4Cl is $6 7 . 5 8 ^ { \circ }$ , which is smaller than the dihedral angle of BDT-T2Cl. Moreover, the distance between adjacent surfaces of BDT-T4Cl on the BDT plane is shorter than that of BDT-T2Cl, indicating that although BDT-T4Cl has more Cl atoms, its molecular packing is closer than that of BDT-T2CI.

When the chlorination strategy and side chain engineering work together, the energy level and morphology could be further optimized. Chen and coworkers synthesized three polymers containing BDT-2Cl and fluorobenzotriazole (FTAZ) unit with different alkyl chains [107]. Similar to the previous discussion, they found that chlorination enhanced the planarity and energy level of the molecule and increased the polymerization activity of the monomer. By optimizing the side chain unit in the FTAZ group, they found that $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , and FF vary greatly with the length of the side chain because the side chain has a significant effect on the energy level and molecular stacking orientation. Li and coworkers used alkylsilyl to replace the thienyl side chain on the BDT-T unit. The synthesized new polymer PBZ-ClSi (see Chart 6.2) has a deep HOMO energy level [87], which increases the absorption coefficient of the material and the charge mobility in related device. The PBZ-ClSi:IT-4F-based devices presented a high PCE of $1 2 . 8 \%$ with simultaneous enhanced $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } , J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ , FF. Amazingly, Zhou and coworkers obtained an outstanding $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 4 \mathrm { V }$ in the J52-Cl-based PSCs based on J52-Cl and a non-fullerene small-molecule BTA3 (see Figure 6.6) [108]. Interestingly, both polymers have the same benzotriazole unit, which they call the "same-A-strategy" (SAS).

Figure 6.5Structure of monomer M1 (BDT-T2Cl) (a) and monomer M2 (BDT-T4Cl) (d), the crystal structure of monomer BDT-T2Cls front view (b) and the packing diagrams (c); monomer BDT-T4Cl front view (e) and the packing diagrams (f). Note: H atoms and 2-ethylhexyl chains were omitted for clarity. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui $\mathsf { P u }$ , and Feng He.

BDT-T-alt-1,3-bis(4-(2-ethylhexyl)thiophen-2-yl)-5,7-bis(2-alkyl)benzo[1,2-c:4,5- $c ^ { \prime }$ |dithiophene-4,8-dione (BDD) is another typical backbone of conjugated polymers, and many efficiency polymer derivatives have been developed on this basis [22, 43, 86, 112, 113], such as PBDB-T-2Cl(PM7), which was synthesized by Hou and Zhang group independently. Compared to nonchlorinated PBDB-T, PBDB-T-2Cl had lower HOmO, enhanced absorption coefficient, improved crystallinity, and charge mobility. In addition, the PBDB-T-2Cl:IT-4F-based PSCs processed by nonhalogen solvent toluene [86], producing an excellent PCE of $1 3 . 1 \%$ while the control device based on PBDB-T just owned a low PCE of $5 . 8 \%$ (see Figure 6.7), showing that chlorinated materials have the characteristics of eco-friendly solvent processing. Compared with the fluorinated PBDB-TF (PM6), the synthesis cost of PBDB-T-2Cl is low, and the calculated differences in molecular configuration, absorption spectrum, aggregation, morphology, and hole mobility are negligible, but its HOMO level is deep, resulting in high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ in corresponding device. The device processed by CB had a very high PCE $1 4 . 4 \%$ , which was the top PCE of chlorinated OSCs at that time. The research on PBDE-T shows that chlorination is more competitive than fluorination in the development of efficient donor polymers.

![](images/2fa6f50010d7411d0a76ea11a8f8e7821d7ebf068f023d4a8a4363ffecc6a072.jpg)

![](images/b19c3b9beb582576ca9bdc4d46ca6cc3ab43289059bd85996f4a12f6f449790b.jpg)  
Figure 6.7Molecular structure and photovoltaic performance of PBDB-T and PBDB-T-2Cl. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu and Feng He.

The chlorinated BDT-T donor and thiophene (T) units are copolymerized to synthesize D-A type copolymer PBDT-Cl-3T2C [98]. The Chen and coworkers also synthesized the control fluorinated polymer PBDT-F-3T2C, as shown in Chart 6.2. The effect of the chlorination on the energy level is similar to the other chlorinated functional units in the polymer. Compared with fluorine atom, chlorine atom has a stronger energy level deepening ability. The smaller size of fluorine atom has stronger self-assembly ability and smaller steric hindrance, which makes the crystallinity and aggregation of PBDT-F-3T2C in solution higher than that of PBDT-Cl-3T2C. Thus, the fluorinated polymer PBDT-F-3T2C has an improved absorption coefficient, favorable morphology, higher and more balanced charge mobility than PBDT-Cl-3T2C, and its PCE is also higher.

From above discussion, the chlorination and fluorination have similarities and unique features. The comparison results of the final photovoltaic performance of the fluorinated and chlorinated copolymer are different. Therefore, we can choose appropriate strategies according to different polymer systems and improve the performance of OSCs.

# 6.3.2 Chlorination on the Acceptor Units of Polymer Donors

Now the chlorinated A units are mainly on isoindigo (IIDT) [54], thiophene (TT) [26-28], and benzothiazole (BT) groups [29-31]. In this section, they will be summarized and discussed. The structure and electronic and photovoltaic properties of related molecules are shown in Chart 6.3 and Table 6.2, respectively.

In 2013, in organic field-effect transistors (OFET), the electron mobility of chlorinated IIDT polymers increased significantly, indicating that chlorination can control the electronic properties of conjugated polymers [114]. Later, Zheng et al. chlorinated isoindigo (Cl-IIDT) in related polymer and found that in addition to adjusting the energy level, chlorination also increased the distortion of the polymer backbone [54]. From the computed results of DFT, the dihedral angle of F-IIDT backbone was $1 1 ^ { \circ }$ , and the length between F and H atom was $2 . 2 7 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ , indicating that there is a strong difference between F and H The interaction, resulting in the large crystal domain mixed with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ film and PCE is $1 . 1 9 \%$ . In contrast, chlorination distorted the Cl-IIDT framework, and the phenyl-phenyl torsion angle could reach ${ 4 0 } ^ { \circ }$ . Compared with fluorinated polymers, Cl-IIDT has suitable crystallinity and large planar conformation, which is beneficial to charge transfer. Cl-HIDT is fully mixed with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ in the solution to form a good morphology in the film, and the PCE is $4 . 6 0 \%$ obtaining a better photovoltaic performance at that time.

In order to reduce the torsion and steric hindrance of thiophene [3,b] caused by chlorination, He and coworkers adopted a 2D side chain design strategy to increase intermolecular interaction and aggregation [26]. 2D-PBTCl still has better blue shift absorption to match ITIC, and the HOMO level is deeper, and the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the device is higher. The PCE of ITIC and 2D-PBTC is $8 . 6 7 \%$ , which is higher than the PCE of PTB7-Th-based devices. These results indicated that the expansion of the conjugation 2D side-chain strategy and the chlorination had a synergistic effect in reducing steric effects and enhancing photovoltaic performance.

In 2017, He and coworkers chlorinated the BT unit of a special polymer, synthesized a series of asymmetric polymers, and studied the effect of chlorination on photovoltaic performance [30]. The chlorination on the BT unit would decline the HOMO levels, improving the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of devices using $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ as acceptor and obtaining a high PCE of $9 . 1 1 \%$ . Although chlorination caused molecular distortion, due to the large atomic size of the polymer, the polymer molecules could still maintain good orientation, thereby maintaining good photovoltaic performance.

![](images/56b98fe4a0b1c6ec450ef2d98d6179dde4a8148fba46978415dd6109dc09b802.jpg)  
Chart 6.3 Polymer donor-based chlorinated backbone of A unit. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu, and Feng He.

Conjugated polymer donors with benzothiadiazole (BT) moiety were widely synthesized and developed in past several years. The Cl numbers on BT moiety gave some impressive influences in relative polymer photovoltaic performance. The monotonical $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of PSCs-based polymer with the number of chlorine atoms on the BT moieties were presented in Table 6.2. The initial polymer PBT4T-2OD-based PSCs showed a PCE of $4 . 8 9 \%$ , with low $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 7 0 \mathrm { V }$ and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 0 . 5 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ . When added one Cl atom to BT in PCBT4T-2OD, the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } , J _ { \mathrm { s c } } ,$ and FF were simultaneously enhanced, giving rise to a high PCE of $8 . 2 1 \%$ . As added two $\mathrm { C l }$ atoms to BT in PCCBT4T-2OD [29], the expected high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $0 . 8 5 \mathrm { V }$ was achieved, the disappointed $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF led to a moderated PCE of $6 . 1 2 \%$ . The chlorinated BT units could change the aggregation of the polymers from solution and film UV-vis absorption spectra. The improved steric hindrance from Cl atoms could produce blueshift in absorption. Astoundingly, the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of PCBT4T-2OD is $0 . 7 3 \mathrm { V } ,$ which is a little improvement compared to PBT4T-2OD; the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of PCCBT4T-2OD is $0 . 8 5 \mathrm { V } ,$ which is much boosted via addition of another Cl atom in PCBT4T-2OD. The HOMO levels of polymers were deepened with increasing numbers of chlorine atoms from the CV measurement, and the HOMO values of PBT4T-2OD, PCBT4T-2OD, and PCCBT4T-2OD were 5.12, 5.26, and $5 . 3 2 \mathrm { e V } ,$ respectively. The PCCBT4T-2OD with two Cl atoms reduces the $\pi { - } \pi$ intermolecular interaction, the high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ could be obtained in PSCs device. The $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of benzodithiadiazole-based PSCs is able to finely tune through manipulation of Cl numbers on BT moieties.

In 2018, He and coworkers synthesized 2D chlorinated polymers using chlorinated BT units [31]. Compared with fluoropolymers, chlorinated polymers have a wider adsorption range. Among them, PBBCl1 $\mathrm { \cdot } \mathrm { T } 3 \mathrm { \cdot } \mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ -based device had the highest PCE, which was $6 . 8 7 \%$ . Since the side chain reduced the twist of the polymer chain caused by the chlorination, the conjugated side chain becomes longer, and the advantage of the chlorination over the fluorination was hindered. Although the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of dichlorinated PBBCl2-T3 is $0 . 8 7 \mathrm { V } ,$ its $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ is not ideal. This may be due to the chlorination destroying the planarity of the polymer backbone and the interaction between molecules.

![](images/08f42f5b0a0df9092c8e80c1ce2ba1952981840188c8ca706042a1382958b18d.jpg)  
Figure 6.8 Synthesis routes of P(Th) and P(Cl). Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui $\mathsf { P u }$ , and Feng He.

As a weak donor unit, thiophene exhibits the properties of an acceptor unit when it encounters a strong donor unit. The same is true for chlorinated thiophene (Cl-Th) [115-117]. Recently, with Cl-Th as acceptor unit, Moon and coworkers synthesized a D-A copolymer, P(Cl) [116]. The synthesis is simple, high yield, and low cost. The control molecule P(Th) without chlorination had a slight twist, and due to the larger atomic radius of Cl, P(Cl) had a larger twist from DFT computation. In addition, the molecular weight of the chlorination was higher, which enhances spectral absorption and red shifts, as presented in Figure 6.8. When mixed with ITIC-Th, the crystallinity of the film is higher and the stacking distance is smaller. The resulting device had an excellent PCE $1 2 . 1 4 \%$ and stability. Then, the Th side chain of the BDT unit was fluorinated and chlorinated to prepare P(F-Cl) and P(Cl-Cl), respectively (see Chart 6.3) [117]. The level of HOMO both had fallen, while the chlorinated polymer had fallen even more. Fluorination and chlorination will reduce solubility, thereby reducing molecular weight. In order to improve the solubility, they added a small proportion of BDD units, and the molecular weight and solubility were significantly increased. Using eco-friendly o-xylene as solvent to fabricated PSCs, P(F-Cl) $\mathrm { \Delta B D D } = 0 . 2$ ):IT-4F and $\operatorname { P } ( \mathbf { C l - C l } ) ( \mathbf { B D D } = 0 . 2 )$ :IT-4F:PN (99.5:0.5, v/v%) obtained PCE of $1 2 . 7 0 \%$ and $1 3 . 9 7 \%$ , respectively.

# 6.3.3 Chlorination of the $\pmb { \pi }$ -Bridge of the Polymer Donors

D-A type structure has been widely applied to design efficient polymer. The strong interaction between the D unit and the A unit can reduce the band gap of the material and increase the absorption of photons. With the deepening of research, $\pi$ -bridge is derived as the key connection between D and a unit and can adjust the backbone of conjugated polymer (Chart 6.4). $\pi$ -Bridge can effectively regulate the photoelectric properties of $\scriptstyle \mathrm { D - } \pi - \mathbf { A } - \pi$ type conjugated materials. It is also a classic strategy to construct highly efficient conjugated polymers.

Sun and coworkers synthesized a polymer PBT1-C-2Cl by chlorinating the thiophene $\pi$ -bridge of PBT1-C [45]. Through the study of DFT calculation, the dihedral angle between BDT and chlorinated Th unit increases due to the large size effect of Cl. The high electronegativity of chlorine and the molecular distortion play an important role in reducing the HOMO of PBT1-C-2Cl and help increase the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the related device. Using IT-4F as an acceptor, the PBT1-C-2Cl-based PSCs obtained a high PCE of $1 2 . 7 \%$ with increased $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and FF, the PCE of control device based on PBT1-C was just $1 0 . 9 \%$ in Table 6.3. According to the morphology analysis, the blend films have two different packing distances, owing to the interchain chalcogen-chalcogen interactions due to the chlorination. The mobility from the SCLC test also supported these results, the blend film with PBT1-C-2Cl had high and balanced carrier mobility, reducing the bimolecular recombination in device.

Hou and coworkers investigated different chlorinated thiophene orientation on polymer donors with $\scriptstyle \mathrm { D - } \pi - \mathbf { A } - \pi$ structure [118]. The two chlorinated polymer donors, PCl(3)BDB-T (P3) and PCl(4)BDB-T (P4), chlorinated Th group facing the BDD and BDT unit, respectively. Minor orientation changes result in huge differences in light absorption, molecular packing, carrier mobility, and device performance. In the chlorobenzene (CB) solution state, the absorption peaks of P3 and P4 are at 465 and $6 4 7 \mathrm { n m }$ , respectively, indicating that the electron delocalization of P4 molecules is more effective than that of P3. According to the temperature-dependent light absorption experiment, P4 shows stronger aggregation than P3. Through DFT theoretical calculation and analysis, the P3 molecule has a highly twisted conjugated backbone, and the electrons on the P4 HOmO energy level are not delocalized on the BDD unit, which limits the IACT effect. In charge dynamics, the neat P3 and blend films had no obvious carrier transport characteristic from the SCLC measurements. However, neat film of P4 exhibited hole mobility of $2 . 5 7 \times 1 0 ^ { - 5 } \ \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \ \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \ \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ , and the blend film had balance hole and electron mobility of $5 . 7 4 \times 1 0 ^ { - 6 } \ \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \ \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \ \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ and $5 . 1 6 \times 1 0 ^ { - 6 } \ \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \ \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \ \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ , respectively. From morphology analysis of X-ray diffraction (XRD) and atom force microscope (AFM), the film with P4 owned well-organized and favorable phase-separation size. Thus, the PSCs based on P4:IT-4F generated a high PCE of $1 2 . 3 3 \%$ . In control conditions, the P3-based PSCs obtained a very low PCE of $0 . 1 8 \%$

# 6.3.4 Chlorinated Small Molecular Donors

Compared with PSCs, the current research on all-small-molecule OSCs is relatively small, and the device efficiency also lags PSCs, mainly due to the lack of high-performance small-molecule donors. However, polymers often suffer from batch-to-batch variation and low reproducibility, which hinders the commercialization of OSCs [119, 120]. Small molecules have broad application prospects in OSCs due to their high purity, definite molecular structure, and high reproducibility. At present, the efficiency of all-small-molecule OsCs also approaches $1 6 \%$ [119]. A small BTR molecule has the characteristics of liquid crystallinity, exhibit strong intermolecular interactions, which are conducive to maintaining the order of long-range directions, and have high carrier mobility. Liu and coworkers replaced the two large hexyl groups on the core of the BTR with two negatively charged chlorine (Cl) atoms to reduce its energy level in Figure 6.9. The chlorinated BTR is expected to match the small-molecule NFAs with low energy levels. At the same time, the chlorination can also reduce the dihedral angle of the thiophenes, increase the planarity of the backbone, and strengthen the interaction between molecules. Using Y6 as an acceptor, the fabricated OSCs reaching a record $1 3 . 6 \%$ PCE at that time. Chlorination enhanced the crystallinity and highlighted the importance of morphology control in all-small-molecule OSCs and demonstrated the great prospects of in OsCs for liquid crystal materials. Thus, chlorination provides a reliable way to produce efficient and reproducible OSCs and is useful for the commercial application of OSCs.

# 6.3.5 Chlorinated Small Molecular Acceptors

Small-molecule NFAs are receiving more and more attention due to their strong near-infrared absorption and high mobility. In the past few years, small-molecule NFAs based on OsCs have developed rapidly, and the efficiency of single junction

![](images/898860f138bcac2901d626f86b429ac3ecb412a01e5d40f83021135ea7663416.jpg)  
Figure 6.9 Molecular structures of BTR and BTR-Cl. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui Pu, and Feng He.

PSCs has reached more than $1 8 \%$ after the structure of small-molecule NFAs has been optimized [1]. Halogenation is a strategy often used in organic semiconductors, such as chlorination and fluorination. When the small-molecule acceptor is chlorinated, some of its properties are consistent with the chlorinated polymer donor. For example, the HOmO levels have deepened to varying degrees. However, some properties are completely different, such as red and blue shift of light absorption. In this section, we will discuss the advances and photoelectric properties of chlorinated small-molecule acceptors.

# 6.3.5.1 Photovoltaic Performance of Chlorinated Small Molecular Acceptors

The IC (2-(3-oxo-2,3-dihydroindene-1-ylidene) dinitrile) is an electron-withdrawing unit and often used as an end group in low-band gap small-molecule acceptors with low-band gap, especially in the high-efficiency small-molecule acceptor-based PSCs in recent years. Chlorination treatment can effectively improve the electronic- withdrawal capability of IC. Small molecules with chlorinated IC as the terminal group extend the spectrum to the NIR.

In 2017, Li and coworker designed and synthesized a series of same conjugated core small molecules (see Chart 6.5) with or without halogens (F, Cl, I, and Br) and fabricated OFET and OSCs devices to study their photoelectric properties. They are all small molecules containing a single halogen atom, and the absorption spectrum ranges from 500 to $7 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ . The absorption peak shifts from H- to F-, Cl-, Br-, and I-ITIC in an orderly manner as the radius of the halogen atom increases, due to the induction effect and the delocalization of hetero electrons to the empty d orbitals of halogens. The HOMO and LUMO energy levels of F-, Cl-, and Br-ITIC have gradually dropped to a lower level, while I-ITIC shows a tiny high energy level compared with other halogenated ITIC. In addition, halogenated crystals have good crystallization properties. Using PTPDBDT as a donor, these halogenated ITIC derivative-based PSCs were fabricated. Except for fluorinated ITIC, the electron mobility of other halogenated molecules has improved. Due to the enhancement of $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF, the PCEs of all halogenated ITIC derivative-based devices are higher than that of H-ITIC based. Among these devices, Cl-ITIC-based device had the highest efficiency at $9 . 5 \%$ (see Table 6.4). In 2018, Chen and coworkers reported on 2,9-bis(2-methylene(3-(1,1-dicyanomethylene)indanone)-7,12-dihydro-4,4,7,7,12, 12-hexaoctyl-4H-cyclopenta $[ 2 ^ { \prime \prime } , 1 ^ { \prime \prime } ; 5 , 6 ; 3 ^ { \prime \prime } , 4 ^ { \prime \prime } ; 5 ^ { \prime } , 6 ^ { \prime } ]$ diindeno $[ 1 , 2 - b ; 1 ^ { \prime } , 2 ^ { \prime } - { \bf b } ^ { \prime } ]$ |dithiophene (FDICTF, F-H) molecules also showed the effects of different halogenation, and the interaction of FF, $\mathrm { F } { - } \mathrm { C l }$ , and $\mathrm { F - B r }$ was presented by halogen atom substitution. After these end groups are halogenated, the NFA molecules exhibit spectral shifts and stronger absorption, increased crystallinity, and higher carrier mobility. However, the substitution of different halogen atoms has different effects on energy level and mobility.

So far, due to the uncertain qualitative nature of the Cl site, NFAs with monochlorinated IC end groups are usually a mixture of two isomers [88, 89]. In order to determine the role of Cl in the terminal position, He used recrystallization to separate IC-Cl- all kinds of monomers, and successfully synthesized ITIC-2Cl-8 and ITIC-2Cl-. The precise positioning of the chlorine atom helps to cultivate single crystals, to study the properties of individual isomers and their influence on photovoltaic performance. Compared with ITIC-2Cl-8, ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ showed a high LUMO and a low HOMO, which resulted in a wider band gap and a slight blue-shift of the absorption spectrum. The LUMO and HOMO levels of ITIC-2Cl-m are between ITIC-2Cl-8 and ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ . The higher LUMO level of ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ the higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ was presented in corresponding devices. The precise position of Cl on the end group of ITIC-2Cl has a profound effect on the stacking of molecules. The ITIC-2Cl- $\gamma$ had better coplanarity and shorter $\pi { - } \pi$ packing distance from the single-crystal structure. In addition, ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ formed a 3D rectangular interpenetrating network, which was conducive to multidirectional charge transport, while ITIC-2Cl-8 just had a linear packing structure [33]. The results showed that the PCE of ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ PBDB-TF-based PSCs was up to $1 3 . 0 3 \%$ , attributing to the overall increase in $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ , FF, and $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ . Moreover, the stability of ITIC-2Cl $\gamma$ - based device was also best among the other control acceptor-based device. This study implied that the 3D network structure may be a promising strategy to design better NFAs to improve PCE and the stability of PSCs. However, in different systems, the precise Cl position on the IC end group has different effects on device performance. For example, with $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6$ as the electron-rich core, three new chlorinated acceptors [34], $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 \ – 2 \mathrm { C l } \ – \ y$ $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 \ – 2 \mathrm { C l } \ – \delta$ , and $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 { - } 2 \mathrm { C l - m }$ , were designed and synthesized. The $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 \ – 2 \mathrm { C l } \ – \ y$ PTB7-Th-based device had a slightly higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ than that of $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 \substack { - 2 \mathrm { C l } - 8 }$ -based device, and the $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 { - } 2 \mathrm { C l } { - } m$ -based device obtained a moderate $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . But the $\mathrm { C O } _ { i } 6 { - } 2 \mathrm { C l } { - } m$ -based devices exhibited a highest PCE of $9 . 3 0 \%$ among these acceptor-based devices.

According to above discussion of monochlorination, the introduction of Cl has a profound effect on energy level, light absorption, crystallinity, and morphology, mainly because Cl has a strong electronegativity and empty 3d orbits of Cl to accommodate $\pi$ electrons. We will discuss that the number of introduced chlorine is increased and the effect of chlorination on the device is based on these acceptors.

Hou and coworkers designed and synthesized IT-4Cl and compared with IT-2Cl (Cl-ITIC) [21]. Compared with ITIC, the incorporation of Cl in IT-2Cl and IT-4Cl hardly affected the molecular packing and the distribution of electron cloud, but the HOMO and LUMO levels have brought significant changes, which are $- 5 . 6 3$ and $- 3 . 5 3 \mathrm { e V }$ of IT-2Cl and $- 5 . 7 1$ and $- 3 . 6 2 \mathrm { e V }$ of IT-4Cl, respectively, indicating that the number of Cl increases from one to two at each end, HOMO and LUMO are further deepen, and the gap between HOMO and LUMO is reduced, which implied the reason why its absorption spectrum of IT-4Cl is further red shifted than that of IT-2Cl. The increase of Cl did not bring about an obvious optimal conformational change, indicating that the final organization of Cl would not generate an additional steric effect, although atomic radius of Cl is much large.

Compared with the absorption spectra of solution, the films absorption of IT-2Cl and IT-4Cl is red-shift, especially IT-4Cl is about $4 0 \mathrm { n m }$ red-shift related to IT-4F, attributing to the larger dipole moment of the chlorinated molecules and improved aggregation in film. Using PBDB-TF as donor, the PCE of corresponding are beyond $1 3 \%$ . Through the ternary strategy [90], a high PCE of $1 4 . 1 8 \%$ was obtained, the ratio of IT-2Cl and IT-4Cl was 2 : 8 in the active layer.

The introduction of end group with dichlorination into other acceptor cores can also obtain outstanding photovoltaic performance [35, 47, 90, 121, 122]. Chen and coworkers synthesized a small-molecule acceptor named NCBDT-4Cl, using PBB-T-SF as the donor, giving an efficient device with low $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ of $0 . 5 5 \mathrm { e V }$ [123]. The champion device achieved a high PCE of $1 4 . 1 \%$ . Another dichlorinated acceptor, IPIC-4Cl, has also been shown to improve device performance [121]. Compared with nonhalogenated and fluorinated, the blend of IPIC-4Cl and PBDB-T has higher crystallinity and better phase separation performance, which ensures the efficient dissociation of excitons and the collection of charges, and PCE with low $E _ { \mathrm { l o s s } }$ of $0 . 5 1 \mathrm { e V }$ reached $1 3 . 4 \%$ , the PCE was boosted up to $1 4 . 3 \%$ by ternary measurement of adding $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ as component.

Chlorination can also help OsCs work efficiently with a small driving force. Chen and coworkers also synthesized a dichlorinated small molecule, HC-PCIC. Compared with the related molecule without substituent, and with fluorination and methoxyl in IC group, chlorinated small molecule had a clear spectral red-shift and higher 0-0 peak, indicating that the chlorination has a stronger end-to-end arrangement. Because Cl has a larger atomic radius and dipole moment than H and F, it improves intermolecular interaction. By comparing the energy levels of three small-molecule acceptors and three polymer donors, a series of HOmO shifts are formed. The introduction of Cl enhanced the electron-withdrawing unit, enabling PSCs with small driving force to work efficiently. Therefore, the HC-PCIC-based PSCs obtained excellent PCE of $1 0 . 4 2 \%$ and $1 1 . 7 5 \%$ , and the HOMO offset was small, 0 and $0 . 0 6 \mathrm { e V } ,$ respectively.

# 6.3.5.2 The Investigation of the Crystal Structure of Chlorinated Small Molecular Acceptors

The crystal structure dispalys the specific configuration of the molecule, which has an important influence on the photoelectric properties. In order to further study the effect of chlorination on the stacking structure and photovoltaic performance, the single-crystal structure of some chlorinated NFAs was analyzed, and the relationship between structure and performance was deeply explored.

In 2018, He and coworkers analyzed the single-crystal structure of the small-molecule acceptor IDIC-4Cl and proved that the $\mathrm { C l } \cdot \cdot \mathrm { \bf \cdot S }$ interaction can achieve interlocking between molecules and form an effective linked molecular network [35]. The dihedral angle of IDIC-4Cl is very small, and the introduction of multiple chlorine atoms does not cause the distortion of the backbone, which makes the molecules more coplanar and more orderly. The parallel arrangement of IDIC-4Cl molecules forms a good J aggregation, which is conducive to charge transfer. The PSCs based on IDIC-4Cl:PBDB-T2Cl achieved a decent PCE of $9 . 2 4 \%$

![](images/d689257dbe279cb3aa066459d8e859d7e7eace26c80a1ebb45eec20811e40fcf.jpg)  
Figure 6.10 The molecule (a) and single-crystal, (b) structure of BTIC-BO-4Cl. Source: Hui Chen, Mingrui $\mathsf { P u }$ , and Feng He.

For R10-4Cl molecule, single-crystal structure analysis shows that it has two different molecular orientations [36]. The molecules form a close parallel arrangement in one direction, and the distance between the end groups of adjacent molecules is only $3 . 3 2 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ There is also an orientation effect that is inserted diagonally into these parallel molecules to interact with their end groups. The interpenetrating network formed from these two directions is conducive to the rapid transmission of carriers in multiple channels. Therefore, a high charge mobility is achieved in a device based on PBDB-T:R10-4Cl, and its PCE is $1 0 . 7 \%$ .

Recently, He and coworkers analyzed the single-crystal structure of the smallmolecule acceptor BTIC-BO-4Cl in Figure 6.10 [124]. The $\mathrm { { s } \cdot \cdot \mathrm { { o } } }$ distance is $2 . 6 7 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ for a single BTIC-BO-4Cl molecule, which gives the acceptor a good planarity with a small dihedral angle of $7 . 6 ^ { \circ }$ between core and end group of chlorination. The two 2-butyloctyl chains are in completely opposite directions, which proves that the length of the alkyl chain has a great influence on molecular stacking. Although 2-butyl chain (BTIC-BO-4Cl) and 1-dodecyl chain (BTIC-C12-4Cl) have the same number of carbon atoms, the linear length of C12-4Cl of BTIC-C12-4Cl molecule is relatively long, the $\pi { - } \pi$ distance is greater than that of BTIC-BO-4Cl molecules. Therefore, its efficiency is inferior to BTIC-BO-4Cl. The $\pi { - } \pi$ distance between adjacent molecules of BTIC-BO-4Cl is relatively short, ranging from 3.29 to $3 . 5 3 \mathring \mathrm { A }$ , leading to J-aggregation of the entire molecule. Although there are two larger chlorine atoms on the terminal group, the distance between the end groups of $\pi { - } \pi$ is $3 . 2 9 \mathring { \mathrm { A } }$ and almost completely overlaps, which is conducive to the efficient electronic hopping between these molecules. The short $\pi { - } \pi$ distance of BTIC-BO-4Cl comes from the multiple interlocking effects of $\mathrm { C l } { \cdot } \cdot { \cdot } \mathrm { S }$ and $\mathbf { C l } \cdot \mathbf { \partial } \cdot \boldsymbol { \pi }$ interactions. This makes BTIC-BO-4Cl present a closed spiral loop microstructure composed of some layers and molecules in the vertical direction. Each ring interacts with two adjacent molecules through a strong interaction, and finally forms a 3D interpenetrating network, which can bless the electron transfer in multiple directions. Using PBDB-TF as donor, the fabricated PSCs obtained a high PCE of $1 6 . 4 3 \%$ . The single crystal and device results show that the synergistic effect of chlorination and alkyl chain can optimize the photovoltaic performance of the material.

# 6.3.5.3 The Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Based on Chlorinated Small Molecular Acceptors

The chlorination of small-molecule acceptors leads to a red shift of the absorption spectrum, extending the spectrum to the NIR, so these acceptors have the potential to prepare semitransparent OSCs [77, 91, 125-127].

In 2016, Hou and coworkers designed and synthesized a small-molecule acceptor, IEICO-4Cl. The absorption spectrum of IEICO-4Cl is effectively red-shifted by the chlorination, and the absorption has shifted from 925 to $1 0 1 0 \mathrm { n m }$ compared with control molecule IEICO [127]. IEICO-4Cl mainly absorbs the region of $7 4 5 { - } 9 4 5 \mathrm { n m }$ which is very suitable for fabricating semitransparent OsCs. By optimizing the relationship between Au electrode thickness and average transmittance (AVT), devices with an average AVT $2 5 . 7 \%$ based on IEICO-4Cl and PTB7-Th have a PCE of $8 . 2 8 \%$ . When J52, PDBBT, and PTB7-Th are used as donors, respectively, the prepared blend films show different color changes, making IEICO-4Cl have greater application potential. This research showed that the chlorination would be a useful tool to fine-tune the energy level of the material to develop multifunction devices.

Next, Li and coworkers designed and synthesized an acceptor BT-ClC, with four Cl at a certain molecular site [126]. Compared to control molecule of BT-C, the red shift of the BT-ClC spectrum is about $6 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , suggesting an increase in IECT. Under thin film conditions, the absorption of BT-CIC is mainly distributed between 650 and $1 0 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ , which is very suitable for fabricating semitransparent PSCs. Cooperating BT-ClC with PTB7-Th, devices based on BT-ClC and PCE-10 showed a PCE of $1 1 . 2 \%$ Taking $1 0 \mathrm { n m \ A g }$ as semitransparent cathode, the semitransparent PSCs with AVT of $4 3 \%$ presented a PCE of $7 . 1 \%$ . These results implied that chlorination would be a good strategy for developing high-performance semitransparent OSCs.

In addition to the IEIcO-4Cl and BT-ClC discussed earlier, other chlorinated molecules such as ITIC-4Cl, ID-4Cl, and ITC-2Cl have also been reported to be used in the fabrication of efficient semitransparent OsCs. The chlorination is an effective method for synthesizing near-infrared materials. Compared with the control nonchlorinated molecules, the interaction between molecules is enhanced, the absorption coefficient is higher, and the absorption spectrum is red-shifted. Therefore, the chlorination provided a new way to fabricate high-performance semitransparent OSCs.

Recently, He and coworkers designed and synthesized low band-gap acceptor BTIC-2Cl- $\mathcal { \cdot } \mathcal { \Upsilon } \mathrm { C F } _ { 3 }$ [128], the molecule structure is shown in Figure 6.11a. It has strong absorption in the near-infrared region for allowing the most of visible light to penetrate, which is a candidate to fabricate high-performance semitransparent OSCs. When balanced the PCE and the transparency of device, the BTIC-2Cl $ { \gamma } \mathrm { C F } _ { 3 }$ -based semitransparent PSCs with $2 4 . 4 5 \%$ AVT yields a high PCE of $1 3 . 0 6 \%$ from same halogen-free solvent the value of AVT is around $2 5 \%$ in Figure 6.11b. The determined color coordinates $( x , y )$ of 10, 15, and $2 0 \mathrm { n m } \mathrm { A g } \mathrm { S }$ I devices were (0.29, 0.30), (0.26, 0.27), and (0.26, 0.26) in Figure 6.11c, respectively. Figure 6.11d exhibits an outdoor image through the related device, which shows good transparency, color sense, and transparency. These parameters indicated that BTIC-2Cl $ { \mathcal { I } } ^ { \mathrm { C F } _ { 3 } }$ is a very promising translucent photovoltaic material for semitransparent building integrated photovoltaic productions.

# 6.4 Conclusion and Outlook

In this chapter, the intrinsic properties of chlorination are introduced and compared with those of fluorination, the research progress of chlorinated polymers and small-molecule donors and small-molecule acceptors are summarized. Because chlorine atom has strong electronegativity (slightly lower than fluorine atoms) and unique 3d empty orbitals, which could accommodate lone pair electrons and promote delocalization of electrons, so chlorination can effectively deepen the energy level of material. In some specific material systems, it is more effective than fluorination in energy-level control. Although the chlorine atom has a larger atomic radius and steric hindrance, the influence of steric hindrance can be reduced through smart structural design. In addition, the C--Cl bond can form a larger dipole moment, expand the spectral absorption, and regulate the packing of molecules. The chlorination has a profound effect on the photoelectric properties of organic semiconductors. Generally, both the donor and acceptor molecules will simultaneously reduce their HOMO and LUMO levels. Compared with the effect on energy level, the effect of chlorination on light absorption is different for different materials. For the polymer donor, the chlorination reaction causes a blue shift of the spectrum, while for the small-molecule acceptor, the spectrum is red shifted. The effect of fluorination and chlorination on the photovoltaic performance of materials differs for different material systems. Therefore, it is necessary to choose a suitable strategy according to the specific material properties. However, considering the high yield and low cost in chemical synthesis, chlorination has greater commercial application potential.

# 7.1 Introduction

Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) based on a polymer-polymer (all-polymer) blend film are attractive due to not only their tunable optical, electrochemical, and structural properties, but also many superior features that are not readily available in conventional polymer-fullerene and polymer-nonfullerene molecule solar cells, including long-term stability, synthetic accessibility, and excellent film-forming properties suitable for large-scale manufacturing [1, 2]. During the past few years, we and a few other groups have developed efficient all-polymer solar cells (all-PSCs) through synergistic materials design and device engineering [2]. Quite recently, it has been shown that polymer acceptors can further extend the solar cell response spectrum, and power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) above $1 5 \%$ have been achieved in these all-polymer systems [3], demonstrating its great potential for future application.

Aromatic diimide-based conjugated polymers, especially containing naphthalene diimide (NDI) and perylene diimides (PDIs), have been proven to be the most efficient n-type polymers. For example, the benchmark n-type, P(ND12OD-T2), Polyera ActivInk N2200 [4], a copolymer composed of NDI and bithiophene, shows an excellent electron mobility value of $1 0 ^ { - 3 } \thinspace \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \thinspace \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \thinspace \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ in SCLC and $0 . 8 5 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ in the OTFT device, respectively. These are extremely desired for polymer acceptors in all-PSCs. The molecular structures of NDI polymers are largely modified from N2200, and the PCEs of the corresponding all-PSCs have been steadily improved. The PCEs of all-PSCs employing NDI polymers have achieved remarkable progress from below $3 \%$ in 2014 to approaching $1 2 \%$ now [5], which has surpassed state-of-the-art performance of fullerene OSCs. Except NDI and PDI, another member of aromatic diimide family, bithiophene diimide (BTI), was also adopted, which possesses relatively small five-membered thiophenes along with imide functionality bridged on bithiophene, significantly moderating steric hindrance. In addition, the open $\beta$ -positions of thiophene ring in BTI offer excellent opportunities for structural modification and backbone expansion [6]. The recent invention of BTI fused ring oligomers (BTIn) yields a new series of polymer acceptors, which have a different electronic structure from NDI polymers and featured tunable LUMO levels, thanks to their delocalized topology along molecule backbones. BTI polymer acceptors have gifted greatly improved PCEs in all-PSCs from ${ < } 1 \%$ in 2017 to ${ > } 1 5 \%$ now [3, 7]. Some other aromatic diimides were also developed, resulting in promising per. formances. With the exploration of more novel aromatic diimide electron-deficient building blocks, even higher efficiency of all-PSCs can be expected.

Organic boron chemistry offers a new toolbox to tune optoelectronic properties of organic/polymer semiconductors. A successful example is the design of n-type organic/polymer semiconductors with boron-nitrogen coordination bond $\mathrm { ( B  N ) }$ In 2015, Liu and coworkers reported the first n-type polymer containing $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ unit for application as electron acceptor in all-PsCs [8]. Then they developed a new kind of electron-deficient building block based on $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ unit, double $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ bridged bipyridine (BNBP) [9]. A striking feature of BNBP-based polymer acceptors is their tunable LUMO energy levels, which leads to high open-circuit voltage of all-PSCs. Furthermore, these BNBP-based polymers exhibit strong absorption in the visible range and show high electron mobility. Their all-polymer photovoltaic devices exhibit PCE of exceeding $1 0 \%$ under solar light irradiation and PCE of exceeding $2 7 \%$ under indoor light irradiation [10, 11]. In 2019, Huang and coworkers reported another electron-deficient building block based on $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ unit, BNIDT, which affords all-PSCs with PCE of $8 . 7 8 \%$ [12]. Based on these research progresses, polymer acceptors containing $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ unit have emerged as a new kind of high-efficiency polymer acceptors for all-PSCs.

Meanwhile, the development of device engineering in all-PsCs becomes very flourishing since 2015. The PCEs of all-PSCs surpassed $5 \%$ , which was considered as a threshold value for OPvs [13]. Studies of the widely investigated "classical" n-type polymer N2200 have demonstrated how controlling the phase separation between donor and acceptor polymer translates to desirable exciton separation, charge transport, and overall photovoltaic performance in the devices [14, 15]. Lots of efforts have been dedicated into optimizing the morphology of N2200-based all-polymer bulk heterojunction (BHJ) blends, adopting strategies such as solvent engineering, thermal annealing, processing additive [16-19]. Afterward, modified device structures such as planar heterojunction, ternary and tandem structures have been incorporated to further enhance the light absorption and charge transport, leading to significantly improved PCE to over $1 0 \%$ [20-22]. Most importantly, multiple reports have shown that the presence of polymer-based acceptors in the photoactive layer represents a great assistance to device stability due to the intrinsic stability merits of conjugated polymers against thermal, photo, and mechanical stresses [2, 23]. Besides, these all-polymer blends exhibit reduced sensitivity to donor-acceptor (D-A) blend ratios, processing environment, and device area, compared with the polymer-fullerene and polymer-molecule systems. This progres. sion demonstrates the unique potential of all-PsCs and its opportunities for further design to achieve efficient and stable solar cells for large-scale applications.
