# 8.2.2.2IC and Its Derivatives-Based A-D-A-Type SMAs

Besides the PDI-based SMAs mentioned above, A-D-A type linear small molecules with a fused ring ladder-type core have also achieved impressive device performance. In 2015, Zhan and coworkers firstly designed a novel acceptor ITIC based on a seven-ring fused core (indacenodithieno[3,2-b]thiophene, IT) and IC terminals [41]. Subsequently, the IDT-based SMA family rapidly grew, and the corresponding PCEs also increased from the initial $6 . 8 0 \%$ to $1 4 \%$ [71]. However, the strong in-chain CT between the donor and acceptor moieties in these types of SMAs usually affords them narrow bandgaps $( \small { \sim } 1 . 6 \mathrm { - } 1 . 2 \mathrm { e V } )$ and down-shifted LUMO levels, giving rise to a low $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } < 1 \mathrm { V } .$ With the development of polymer donors and careful design of SMAs, several high-voltage systems have emerged. Figure 8.4 depicts the chemical structures of the IC-based SMAs, and Table 8.2 summarizes the energy levels and device properties.

In 2017, Hou and coworkers reported a new A-D-A-structured SMA ITCC by simple end-group modification, which introduced thienyl-fused indanone as end groups on a previously reported SMA ITIC. They found ITCC showed a close $\pi { - } \pi$ stacking distance, high electron mobility, and a high-lying LUMO level of $- 3 . 7 6 \mathrm { e V } .$ The OSCs consisting of PBDB-T as the polymer donor obtain an impressive $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of greater than $_ { 1 \mathrm { V } }$ and a high PCE of $1 1 . 4 \%$ [57]. In 2018, they applied the fluorinated polymer (PBDB-TF) as the electron donor and ITIC as the electron acceptor to construct OSCs. Benefited from the deep HOMO level of PBDB-TF, the resulted devices showed a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 1 \mathrm { V }$ and a PCE of $1 0 . 3 \%$ [58]. Again, they used PBDB-TF as the donor to pair with the acceptor of IT-M, which contains a methyl modified IC as terminals. The corresponding devices also yield a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 2 \mathrm { V }$ and a similar PCE of $1 0 . 5 \%$ [59]. Yan and coworkers synthesized an A-D-A-type acceptor (C8-ITCC) with tetraoctyl-substituted IT unit as core and thienyl-fused indanone as end groups. With PBDB-TF as the donor, C8-ITCC-based devices can achieve a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V }$ and a PCE of $1 0 . 8 \%$ [60].

In 2017, Bo and coworkers designed a new SMA IDT-BOC6 by introducing conformational locking with IDT as a central core unit, bis(alkoxy)-substituted benzene ring as conformational control units and cyanoindanones as end-capping units. IDT-BOC6 exhibits a quite good planarity in the solid state, which endows a high fluorescence quantum yield and reduced energy loss. As a result, the devices showed a decreased non-radiative recombination loss, giving rise to a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . With PBDB-T as the electron donor, IDT-BOC6 based device achieved a PCE of $9 . 6 \%$ and a very high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.01 V [61]. Zhang and his coworkers synthesized a wide-bandgap polymer donor PBPD-Th composed of meta-alkoxyphenyl benzodithiophene-alt-thienyl benzodithiophene-4,8-dione and thienyl benzodithiophene-4,8-dione (BDD-Th). PBPD-Th shows strong absorption in the short wavelength of $3 0 0 { - } 6 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ with a bandgap of $1 . 9 1 \mathrm { e V }$ and a deep HOMO level of $- 5 . 4 2 \mathrm { e V } .$ As a result, the optimal PSCs based on PBPD-Th:ITIC showed a PCE of $1 0 . 8 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.01 V [62]. They also synthesized a D-A-type wide-bandgap polymer PSTZ by copolymerizing

![](images/518a4fb2d9b052b333ecd146fb2cf41b1f26ac76e55bda62c48d87d35c00bbea.jpg)  
Figure 8.4The representative molecular structures of SMAs containing IC units. Source: Ailing Tang, Yuze Lin, and Erjun Zhou.

2,5-bis(5-bromo-4-(2-ethylhexyl)thiophen-2-yl)-thiazolo[5,4-d]thiazole (TTz) and 4,8-bis(5-(2-butyloctylthio)thiophen-2-yl)-benzol $[ 1 , 2 - b ; 4 , 5 - b ^ { \prime } ]$ |dithiophene (BDTTS) to pair ITIC. Owing to the low HOMO level and high hole mobility of PSTZ, the PSTZ:ITIC-based PSCs achieved a PCE of $8 . 1 3 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.01 V [72]. In 2019, they utilized an asymmetrical acceptor (IDT6CN-M) to design high-voltage PSCs. IDT6CN-M contains a ladder-type 4,4,9,9-tetrakis(4-hexylphenyl)-4,9- dihydro-s-indaceno[1,2-b]thiophene-alt-[5,6-d]thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (IDT6) core and methyl-substituted 2-(6-oxo-5,6-dihydro- $4 H$ -cyclopenta[c]thiophen-4-ylidene) malononitrile (CPTCN-M). The asymmetrical IDT6CN-M shows impressively large dipole moments that can enhance the intermolecular interaction and alter the molecular stacking form. Using the fluorinated polymer PM6 or chlorinated polymer PM7 as the donor, the small energy offsets $( \Delta E _ { \mathrm { H O M O } } )$ of 0.10 and $0 . 0 8 \mathrm { e V }$ helped both the PM6:IDT6CN-M and PM7:IDT6CN-M-based PSCs achieve a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.04 and $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V } ,$ respectively [28].

Peng and coworkers developed a novel wide-bandgap copolymer of PBDT-ODZ based on BDT and 1,3,4-oxadiazole (ODZ) blocks, which possessed a wide bandgap of $2 . 1 2 \mathrm { e V }$ and a low-lying HOMO level of $- 5 . 6 8 \mathrm { e V } .$ Blending with 3,9-bis(2- methylene-(3-(1,1-dicyanomethylene)-indanone)-5,5,11,11-tetrakis(4-hexylthienyl)- dithieno $2 , 3 \ – d : 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } \ – d ^ { \prime } ]$ -s-indaceno $^ { 1 , 2 - b : 5 , 6 - b ^ { \prime } ] }$ -dithiophene) (ITIC-Th), the PBDTODZ:ITIC-Th devices exhibit a large $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 8 \mathrm { V }$ and a PCE of $1 0 . 1 2 \%$ . After incorporating $4 \%$ of copper(I) iodide (CuI) as an additive, the PCE is increased to $1 2 . 3 4 \%$ [63]. By copolymerizing 1,3,4-thiadiazole (TDZ) and BDT building blocks, they attained the other two wide-bandgap copolymers, PBDT-TDZ and PBDTS-TDZ. PBDT-TDZ exhibits a low-lying HOMO level of $- 5 . 3 5 \mathrm { e V } .$ Using ITIC as an acceptor, the resulting devices based on PBDT-TDZ exhibited a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.01 V. PBDTS-TDZ with alkylthio side chains exhibits stronger optical absorption, lower-lying HOMO level, and higher crystallinity. PBDTs-TDZ:ITIC devices exhibited a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 0 \mathrm { V } ,$ higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 7 . 7 8 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , giving rise to a higher PCE of $1 2 . 8 0 \%$ without any additive and posttreatment [64]. They attained a medium-bandgap polymer, PBDTSF-FBT, based on BDT unit modified with fluorinated alkylthienyl side chains as donor block and fluorinated BT as acceptor block. Owing to the fluorination and sulfuration strategies, PBDTSF-FBT exhibits a down-shifted HOMO energy level value and high crystalinity. PBDTSF-FBT:ITIC-based devices showed a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 3 \mathrm { V }$ and a high PCE of $1 0 . 6 9 \%$ [65]. In 2019, Sun and coworkers used a weak acceptor unit, methyl 2,5-dibromo-4-fluorothiophene-3-carboxylate (FE-T), to combine with BDT unit, affording a wide-bandgap polymer P1. P1 shows a much deep HOMO level of $- 5 . 6 0 \mathrm { e V } .$ When blended with ITIC-Th, it can achieve a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 1 \mathrm { V }$ and a high PCE of $1 1 . 3 9 \%$ [67]. They also designed two wide-bandgap polymers (P3 and P4) by incorporating thiophene-flanked phenylene as an electron-donating unit and quinoxaline as an electron-accepting co-unit. Paired with IDIC, P3 with two F atoms attains a large $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 0 \mathrm { V }$ and a large $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 5 . 9 9 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , yielding a PCE of $9 . 7 \%$ Further fluorination affords the polymer P4 the increased chain-twisting and down-lying HOMO level, leading to an increase of $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 6 \mathrm { V } .$ Because of the unsuitable HOMO level with IDIC, the corresponding device gave rise to the lowest PCE of $2 . 9 3 \%$ [68].

Tobin J. Marks designed two isomeric IDTT-based acceptors 3,9-bis(2-methylene(3-(1,1-dicyanomethylene)-benz-(5,6)indanone)-5,5,11,11-tetrakis(4-nonylphenyl)- dithieno $[ 2 , 3 - d ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } - d ^ { \prime } ]$ -s-indaceno[] $\_ { 2 - b : 5 , 6 - b ^ { \prime } }$ ldi-thiophene (ITN-C9) and 3,9-bis (2-methylene-(3-(1,1-dicyanomethylene)-benz(6,7)indanone))-5,5,11,11-tetrakis (4-nonylphenyl)-dithieno $[ 2 , 3 - d ; 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } - d ^ { \prime } ]$ -s-indaceno[1 $, 2 - b : 5 , 6 - b ^ { \prime }$ |dithiophene (ITzN-C9). Compared with ITN-C9, ITzN-C9 has an elevated LUMO level. The PBDB-TF:ITzN-C9-based devices show a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V }$ than that of the devices based on PBDB-TF:ITN-C9-based devices (0.93 V). Single-crystal structures of ITN-C9 and ITzN-C9 reveal that the $\pi$ -extended naphthyl end groups assemble in vertical columns with $\pi$ stacking distance as small as $3 . 3 1 ( 1 ) \mathring \mathrm { A }$ with electronic coupling integrals as large as $3 8 \mathrm { m e V } ,$ and internal reorganization energies as small as $0 . 1 3 3 \mathrm { e V } ,$ which afford the devices a high PCE near $1 0 \%$ [66]. Yang and coworkers prepared an acceptor IT-DM with indacenodithieno[3,2-b]thiophene (IDTT) as the central core and 5,6-dimethyl-3-dicycanovinylindan-1-one as terminals. The J71:IT-DM-based device showed a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 2 \mathrm { V }$ with a high PCE of $1 2 . 0 5 \%$ [69].

# 8.2.2.3 $\begin{array} { r } { \mathsf { A } _ { 2 } ^ { - } \mathsf { A } _ { 1 } ^ { - } \mathsf { D } ^ { - } \mathsf { A } _ { 1 } ^ { - } \mathsf { A } _ { 2 } } \end{array}$ -Type SMAs with BT as $\mathsf { \pmb A } _ { 1 }$ Units

Benzothiadiazole (BT) is a well-known building block used in p-type small molecules and polymers for its strong electron affinity and strong absorption in the visible spectrum when coupled with electron-rich units. Recently, BT as a building block has also been used for constructing the NFAs. Among them, $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { D } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ -type NFAs with BT as $\mathbf { A } _ { 1 }$ units have achieved a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ above 1 V and a PCE of $1 1 \%$ . The relevant chemical structure of the BT-based SMAs is shown in Figure 8.5, and the energy levels and device properties are listed in Table 8.3.

In 2015, McCulloch and coworkers reported an $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { D } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ type BT-based NFA, FBR, which contained 9,9-dioctylfluorene as the core, BT as $\mathbf { A } _ { 1 }$ unit, and 3-ethylrhodanine as $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ unit [83]. Subsequently, they synthesized another NFA called IDTBR via replacement of the fluorene core in FBR with an n-octyl substituted indacenodithiophene unit [84]. In 2016, they used a low-bandgap polymer PffBT4T-2DT to pair with these two BT-based NFAs. The resulting PCEs for FBR and IDTBR are as high as $7 . 8 \%$ and $9 . 9 5 \%$ , respectively. The most remarkable aspects of the devices are the high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 2 \mathrm { V } ,$ with high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ $\mathrm { 1 1 . 5 m A c m ^ { - 2 } }$ for PffBT4T-2DT:FBR and the high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 7 \mathrm { V }$ with $7 5 \%$ EQE $( J _ { \mathrm { s c } } = 1 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 } )$ for PffBT4T-2DT:IDTBR devices [39]. In addition, they applied PffBT4T-2DT to pair another acceptor, EH-IDTBR, which used a 2-ethylhexyl substituted indacenodithiophene as the core. Compared with chlorobenzene, using mesitylene as the solvent, an improved PCE of $1 1 . 1 \%$ with a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 2 \mathrm { V }$ was achieved without the need for pre- or post-treatments [73]. In 2018, they reported PBDTTT-EFT-based devices with EH-IDTBR as acceptor, which can achieve high efficiencies of $1 2 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } > 1 \mathrm { V } .$ They found the charges can dissociate with negligible geminate recombination losses, resulting in a high EQE value around $9 0 \%$ and a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $2 0 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ [74]. They also synthesized a new indenofluorene analogue of IDTBR, named IDFBR. They used PCE10 as donor and IDTBR and IDFBR as the acceptors to fabricate the ternary OSCs. The higher-lying LUMO level of IDFBR than that of IDTBR will enhance the cascade effect in the ternary, and the devices can achieve a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 3 \mathrm { V }$ with a high PCE of $1 1 . 0 \%$ [75]. Zhan and coworkers used PTB7-Th as a donor to blend with IDT-2BR, resulting in a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V }$ and a PCE of $8 . 5 \%$ . They further employed PDI-2DTT (perylene diimide moiety flanked with two dithienothiophene) as the third component in the active layer. PDI-2DTT showed lower LUMO and HOMO energy levels than those of IDT-2BR, which can be used as an energy driver to enhance the driving force for CT, and simultaneously achieved a minimal energy loss $( 0 . 5 5 \mathrm { e V } )$ . PTB7-Th/IDT-2BR blend showed a very high PCE $( > 1 0 \% )$ [78]. Yan and Ma designed a novel wide-bandgap $( 2 . 0 5 \mathrm { e V } )$ polymer donor named PvBDTTAZ, composed of a BDT and a difluorinated triazole unit, to pair with the narrow-bandgap SMA (O-IDTBR). Differently from the conventional BDT-based polymers where the BDT units are linked into the polymer backbone via the $\alpha$ positions of the thiophene units, the BDT units in PvBDTTAZ are connected along the polymer backbone via the phenyl group of the BDT unit. The resulted OSCs showed a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 8 \mathrm { V }$ and a small voltage loss of $0 . 5 5 \mathrm { V } .$ Benefited from the highly favorable film morphology with crystalline and small domains and effective CT, the devices showed a high EQE above $7 0 \%$ giving rise to a high PCE of $1 1 . 6 \%$ [76]. Lim and coworkers utilized T2-ORH consisted of a bithiophene core and octylsubstituted rhodanine ends as the third component in ternary-blend solar cells with PTB7-Th and EH-IDTBR as host materials. The ternary device with a $1 { : } 1 { : } 1$ blend ratio achieved a PCE of $1 1 . 5 5 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V }$ [77].

Zheng and coworkers utilized an angular-shaped dithienonaphthalene flanked by 3-ethylrhodanine units via BT bridges to attain a novel NFA, named as DTNR. It exhibited a high-lying LUMO level of $- 3 . 7 5 \mathrm { e V }$ and strong absorption. Combined with a low-bandgap polymer, PTB7-Th, DTNR obtained a high PCE of $9 . 5 1 \%$ with a large $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 8 \mathrm { V } ,$ owing to an extremely low energy loss of $0 . 5 0 \mathrm { e V }$ [79]. Chen and Zhan designed a kind of "donor-acceptor (D-A) combined $\pi$ -bridge' based on the monofluoro-substituted benzothiadiazole (FBT) to link a thiophene ring, which is used as bridge to link a IDT central core and 3-octyl-2-(1,1-dicyanomethylene)rhodanine terminal groups, and they constructed a new A $\pi$ -D- $\pi$ -A-type small molecular acceptor (IDT-FBTR). This "offset effect" of the D-A combined $\pi$ -bridge can regulate the HOMO-LUMO energy levels of the molecule, yielding a relatively high LUMO energy level of IDT-FBTR, which is helpful to increase the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . As a result, the OSCs based on the PTB7-Th and IDT-FBTR showed a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 2 \mathrm { V }$ with a PCE of $9 . 1 4 \%$ [80]. Xu and coworkers designed two $\mathbf { A } _ { 1 } { \cdot } \mathbf { A } _ { 2 } { \cdot } \pi { \cdot } \mathbf { D } { \cdot } \mathbf { A } _ { 2 } { \cdot } \mathbf { A } _ { 1 }$ structural SMAs, TIDT-BT-R2 and TIDT-BT-R6, by using thiophene-indenothiophene (TIDT) as the core and benzothiadiazolerhodanine (BT-R) as the end groups. Compared with TIDT-BT-R6 with hexyl as alkyl chain, TIDT-BT-R2 with shorter alkyl chain (ethyl) showed enhanced photo-induced charge separation, better charge transport and collection properties. TIDT-BT-R2 exhibited a larger $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V }$ and a higher PCE of $8 . 7 \%$ [81]. Jenekhe and coworkers designed an $\scriptstyle \mathrm { A = C H - D - C H = A }$ type NFAs incorporating rylene-imide end-capping groups via methine bridges in D-A architectures. NIBT is composed of an IDT core and BT bridged bis(naphthalene-imide)arylenelidenes (BNIAs), which can attain a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V }$ and high PCE of up to $1 0 . 8 \%$ with PBDB-T as the donor [82]. Compared with NIBT, NIDT without BT bridge shows a higher-lying

LUMO level of $- 3 . 5 8 \mathrm { e V . }$ The resulting NIDT:PBDB-T-based devices show a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } } \left( 1 . 1 4 \mathrm { V } \right)$ and high PCE of up to $1 0 . 0 \%$ [82].

# 8.2.2.4 $\begin{array} { r } { \mathsf { A } _ { 2 } { \boldsymbol { - } } \mathsf { A } _ { 1 } { \boldsymbol { - } } \mathsf { D } { \boldsymbol { - } } \mathsf { A } _ { 1 } { \boldsymbol { - } } \mathsf { A } _ { 2 } } \end{array}$ -Type SMAs with BTA or $\pmb { \varrho \times }$ as $\pmb { \mathsf { A } } _ { 1 }$ Units

Replacing the S atom in the BT unit with N atom affords another electron-withdraw building block, BTA. Compared with BT, the incorporation of $\mathbf { N }$ atom in BTA weakens its electron-withdrawing ability, which could up-shift its LUMO energy level. The design of the alkyl chain on the $_ \mathrm { N }$ atoms facilitates to fine-tune the solubility and crystallinity of the molecules. BTA has been employed to construct a series of medium-bandgap polymer donors. In 2017, Zhou and coworkers used BTA as $\mathbf { A } _ { 1 }$ unit to link the different middle D unit and terminal $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ unit, affording the $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { D } – \mathbf { A } _ { 1 } – \mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ type SMAs. Benefiting from the weak electron-withdrawing ability of BTA, the resulted SMAs showed the up-lying LUMO levels and endowed the devices a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . To fine-tune the optoelectronic properties of SMAs, Zhou and coworkers have carefully designed the central core, terminals, and alkyl chains. Figure 8.6 lists the corresponding molecular structures, and the device parameters are listed in Table 8.4. Firstly, by using P3HT as electron donor, BTA1 and BTA2 can realize high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.02 and $1 . 2 2 \mathrm { V }$ with moderate PCEs of $5 . 2 4 \%$ [85] and $4 . 5 0 \%$ [86], respectively.

Subsequently, considering that the LUMO energy level mainly depends on the electron-withdrawing segment in the D-A-type copolymer, Zhou and coworkers chose the D-A copolymers containing BTA units to pair with their BTA-based SMAs, namely "Same-A-Strategy' (SAS), which may contribute to realize the close LUmO levels and decrease the voltage loss. As a result, they have achieved a series of high-voltage PSCs $\mathrm { ( { > } 1 . 1 0 V ) }$ . Firstly, they chose J61 containing alkylthio substituted BDT units and difluorine substituted BTA units as an electron donor to blend with BTA3. The resulted devices can yield a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 5 \mathrm { V }$ and a high PCE of $8 . 2 5 \%$ [87]. And then, they synthesized two new BTA-based polymers to pair BTA3. PE1 was derived from the polymer J61 by replacing the thiophene $\pi$ -bridge with thieno[3,2-b]thiophene, and PE2 was synthesized by introducing fluorine atoms to the thiophene side chain in PE1. PE1 can realize a PCE of $8 . 4 3 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 1 \mathrm { V }$ [88]. Furthermore, the low-lying HOMO level of J71 with alkylsilyl modified BDT unit afforded the PSCs based on J71:BTA3 a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 0 \mathrm { V }$ with a PCE of $8 . 6 0 \%$ [89]. Then, chlorine atoms are introduced into the conjugated side chain of the BDT unit of the p-type polymer to fine-tune the optoelectronic properties. The chlorinated polymer J52-Cl, blended with BTA3, yields very small energy offsets and a decreased non-radiative recombination loss of $0 . 2 4 \mathrm { e V } .$ J52-Cl:BTA3 device delivered a very high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 4 \mathrm { V } ,$ a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 3 . 1 6 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , and an FF of $6 6 . 6 2 \%$ giving rise to a promising PCE of $1 0 . 5 \%$ , while the non-chlorinated counterpart (J52) gives rise to a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 7 \mathrm { V }$ with a PCE of $9 . 4 1 \%$ [40]. In addition, a fused BTA-based copolymer (PfBTAZT-Cl) containing 6-fluoro-thieno $[ 2 ^ { \prime } , 3 ^ { \prime } { : } 4 , 5 ]$ benzo[1,2-d]-[1,2,3]triazole (fBTAZT) and chlorine atoms substituted BDT unit, when blended with BTA3, can also attain a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ above $1 . 2 0 \mathrm { V }$ [90]. In 2021, Hou and coworkers reported a wide-bandgap polymer named PBQx-TCl to pair with BTA3. Benefited to the high $\mathrm { E Q E } _ { \mathrm { E L } }$ approaching $2 \times 1 0 ^ { - 3 }$ the PBQx-TCl:BTA3-based device yielded an impressively high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 4 \mathrm { V } .$ The high carrier mobilities and suppressing bimolecular recombination afforded the PBQx-TCl:BTA3 a high PCE of $1 2 . 2 \%$ . They fabricated ternary cells with PBQx-TCl, BTA3 and BTP-eC9, which showed a PCE of $2 8 . 5 \%$ for a $1 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ device and $2 6 . 0 \%$ for $1 0 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ device under $1 0 0 0 \mathrm { { l x } }$ LED illumination [91].

Compared with BTA3 with IDT core, BTA13 with IDTT as central unit shows up-shifted HOMO and LUMO levels. Blended with BTA13, the fluorinated polymer of J52-F shows a high PCE of $8 . 3 6 \%$ with an improved $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 8 \mathrm { V }$ and a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $1 1 . 5 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ [92]. They also investigated the effect of the substituent groups in the $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ unit on the molecular stacking model. BTA3 with ethyl substituent in RCN shows heterogeneous interaction between $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 }$ and $\mathbf { A } _ { 1 }$ unit while BTA5 with the benzyl substituted RCN exhibits homogeneous packing of $\mathbf { A } _ { 2 } ^ { \phantom { } } - \mathbf { A } _ { 2 } ^ { \phantom { } }$ model. The substitutes on the terminals have little influence on the energy levels. BTA3 and BTA5 blended with J52-F could achieve ultrahigh $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of 1.19 and $1 . 1 7 \mathrm { V } ,$ respectively. Benefited from the good molecular packing, BTA5 realized an improved PCE of $1 1 . 2 7 \%$ , obviously higher than that of BTA3 $( \mathrm { P C E } = 9 . 0 4 \%$ [93]. They chose BTA5 as electron acceptor and four BTA-based polymer donors to construct OSCs with tetrahydrofuran (THF) as processing solvent. They investigated the influence of the substitutents (-H, ${ \cdot \mathrm { O C H } _ { 3 } }$ , -F, -Cl) on the BTA units of the polymers. All of the four polymers can achieve a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ above $1 . 1 0 \mathrm { V } .$ PE31 with the unsubstituted BTA unit showed the efficient hole transfer and more balanced charge mobilities, thus leading to the highest PCE of $1 0 . 0 8 \%$ due to the efficient hole transfer and balanced carriers mobilities, while the methoxy-substituted polymer PE32 exhibited the lowest PCE of $7 . 4 0 \%$ With the down-shifted HOMO levels of fluorinated PE33 and chlorinated J52-Cl, they showed the higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ values of 1.16 and $1 . 2 1 \mathrm { V } ,$ respectively [94]. When using another kind of medium-bandgap D--A polymer (PBT1-C) as electron donor, PBT1-C:BTA3-based devices can also achieve high-energy CT state around $1 . 7 6 \mathrm { e V }$ and low non-radiative recombination loss about $0 . 2 4 \mathrm { e V } .$ As a result, the PBT1-C:BTA3-based devices can yield a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 1 \mathrm { V }$ [95].

To modify the molecular properties of BTA3, they further introduce fluorine atoms to BTA units and attain a new SMA, named F-BTA3. Compared with BTA3, F-BTA3 exhibits a higher molar extinction coefficient, larger CT driving force, and suppressed bimolecular recombination. Pyrrolo[3,4-f]benzotriazole-5,7-dione (TzBI)-based polymer is chosen as an electron donor, which possessed the low-lying HOMO levels. The resulted F-BTA3-based devices showed a very high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 2 5 \mathrm { V }$ and a PCE of $8 . 3 8 \%$ [96]. In 2021, Zhou and coworkers investigated the effect of the electron-donating units (D) in polymer donors on the photovoltaic performance, with F-BTA3 as acceptor. They design three polymers (J52-Cl, F11, and PE52) with BDT unit, benzo[1,2-b:4,5. $\mathbf { \nabla } \cdot  { b ^ { \prime } }$ ]difurans (BDF), and dithieno $[ 2 , 3 \mathrm { - d } ; 2 ^ { \prime }$ $3 ^ { \prime } – d ^ { \prime }$ ]benzo[1,2-b;4,5-b']dithiophenes (DTBDT) as the electron-donating unit, respectively. The tricyclic D units show better PCE than the pentacyclic D unit - $1 0 \%$ versus $6 . 8 \%$ ). F11 with BDF units exhibits a slightly lower $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 2 \mathrm { V }$ than those of the J52-Cl and PE52-based devices (1.14 V) [97].

In 2021, Zhou and coworkers chose quinoxaline (Qx) instead of BTA as the A unit to construct two new small molecular acceptors $\mathrm { \nabla } Q \mathrm { x } 3 \mathrm { b }$ and F-Qx3b). They investigated the relative photovoltic performance by introducing the fluorine atom to the thiophene side chains of the p-type polymer and Qx units of the n-type small molecule. The photovoltaic device based on PE61:Qx3b achieved a PCE of $8 . 2 4 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 2 \mathrm { V } ,$ while the PE62:F-Qx3b-based device obtained a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ as high as $1 . 0 9 \mathrm { V }$ with a slightly high PCE at $9 . 7 8 \%$ . That result indicated that the Qx unit is also a good choice to attain high-voltage solar cells [98].

# 8.3 n-Type Polymers

All-PsCs, fabricated with polymer donor and polymer acceptor, have attracted a lot of attention due to their tunable light harvesting, easy large-scale/large area manufacturing, and long-term stability. Recently, the PCE of the all-PSCs has reached up to $1 5 . 0 \%$ [99, 100]. Simultaneous adjustment of polymer donor and polymer acceptor energy levels can improve the light harvesting and increase the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ . As a result, an increasing number of all-PSCs have achieved a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ above $1 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ with the PCE above $5 \%$ Figure 8.7 lists the relevant molecular structures of the polymer acceptors, and the device parameters are listed in Table 8.5.

Guo and coworkers designed a new electron-accepting building block, bithiophene imide, namely BTI. Thiophene ring fusion can extend the $\pi$ -conjugation length, broaden the absorption, and improve the electron mobility. They designed a series of n-type terpolymers BTI2-xTPD by copolymerizing a fused BTI dimer, TPD unit with a difluorinated thiophene unit. The incorporation of a TPD unit facilitates balancing crystallinity and miscibility. The noncovalent S. . -O interactions between TPD and thiophene unit increase the backbone planarity and improve the in-chain charge transport. BTI2-30TPD achieves an optimal PCE of $8 . 2 8 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V }$ [101]. They also developed a series of BTI2 and 3,4-difluorothiophene-based random copolymers PBTI2(xDT)-FT, by changing the ratios of 2-decyltetradecyl (DT) and

2-octyldodecyl (OD) side chains on BTI2. The side-chain engineering of PA could improve the blend film morphology and yield balanced charge carrier mobilities. The optimal polymer PBTI2(50DT)-FT blended with PTB7-Th achieved a promising PCE of $8 . 3 2 \%$ with a large $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 1 \mathrm { V }$ [102]. They further synthesized a fluorine atom functionalized $f$ -BTI2 unit, namely di(fluorothienyl)thienothiophene diimide $f$ -FBTI2). By copolymerizing the $f$ -FBTI2 and thiophene unit, they attained a high-performance n-type polymer, $f$ FBTI2-T, which showed a reduced bandgap and low-lying LUMO level. With PTB7-Th as polymer donor, the resulted all-PSCs based on $f$ FBTI2-T can yield a high PCE of $8 . 0 \%$ with a $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 5 \mathrm { V }$ [103].

Liu and coworkers have reported a new kind of amorphous polymer acceptors containing boron-nitrogen coordination bond ( $\mathrm { B } {  } \mathrm { N }$ unit), which can match various polymer donors to give efficient all-PSCs. They synthesized two amorphous polymer acceptors (PBN-14 and PBN-15), by copolymerizing an electron-deficient double $\mathbf { B } { \gets } \mathbf { N }$ bridged bipyridine (BNBP) unit with an electron-deficient BT or difluorinated BT unit. They utilized a small molecular donor, BD3T, composed of carbazolyl substituted benzodithiophene core, $^ { 3 , 4 ^ { \prime } }$ -dioctyl- $\cdot 2 , 2 ^ { \prime } { : } 5 ^ { \prime } , 2 ^ { \prime \prime }$ -terthiophene (3T) bridge unit, and 3-ethylrhodanine terminals, to combine with PBN-14 and PBN-15, respectively. The BD3T:PBN-14-based devices showed a higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 1 2 \mathrm { V }$ and a medium PCE of $5 . 0 6 \%$ . Compared with PBN-14, PBN-15 possesses two extra fluorine substitutes on the BT unit, which afforded it a stronger aggregation tendency and lower LUMO level, suppressed bimolecular recombination. As a result, PBN-15-based devices showed a higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF, giving rise to a higher PCE of $9 . 5 \%$ with a decreased $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V }$ [44]. Another polymer acceptor, PBN-11 containing BNBP and $^ { 2 , 2 ^ { \prime } }$ -(perfluoro-1,4-phenylene)dithiophene (4fPT) units is chosen to blend with a small molecule donor DR3TBDTC. DR3TBDTC is composed of carbazolyl substituted BDT core, $^ { 3 , 3 ^ { \prime \prime } }$ -dioctyl- $\cdot 2 , 2 ^ { \prime } { : } 5 ^ { \prime } , 2 ^ { \prime \prime }$ -terthiophene (3T) and 3-ethylrhodanine. The DR3TBDTC:PBN-11-based devices exhibit a high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of $1 . 0 4 \mathrm { V } .$ The active layer showed a small-size phase separation, contributed to a high PCE of $8 . 0 \%$ [104].

# 8.4 Conclusion and Outlook

One of the design rules for the high-voltage OsCs is to decrease the energy offset between the donor and acceptor molecular energy levels. With the development of the electron donors and electron acceptors, substantial progress has been achieved in the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ of the OSCs. The $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ has been approaching $1 . 3 \mathrm { V }$ with a decreased energy loss of about $0 . 5 \mathrm { - } 0 . 6 \mathrm { e V } .$ and the PCE of the high-voltage system has also exceeded $1 3 \%$ . There is still room for further improvements in $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and PCE. In this work, we summarized the recent progress of the electron acceptors in the high-voltage systems with $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ above $1 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ and PCE above $8 \%$ . Different molecular design strategies containing the core, end groups, and $\pi$ -bridges, as well as their substituents, have been employed to tune the energy levels and improve the photovoltage. However, it is still unclear how these subtle structural changes influence voltage and device performance.

Compared with the increasingly enriched material systems, the relative lack of the investigation on the physical origins of different energy loss pathways in OSCs comes upon a growing problem. Among the energy loss, the CT loss and the non-radiative recombination loss are the main loss pathways. The non-radiative recombination loss can drastically decrease as the up-shift of the CT state while the up-shifted CT state will decrease the charge generation efficiency. However, some systems have achieved an excellent balance between the high $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and charge generation efficiency by designing highly luminescent material and suppressing the possible recombination pathways. Unfortunately, these design methods are materials-dependent in most cases. It is necessary to focus on the photovoltaic mechanisms in OSCs.

The current data have demonstrated a bright future due to the efforts devoted to new material design and device fabrication. Combining the in-depth analysis of the existing materials with the device physics will guide us to design the promising materials. In the future, it is expected that these high-voltage OSCs will open a new avenue for indoor light recycling applications.

# 9.1 Introduction

Organic solar cells (OsCs) as sustainable photovoltaic technology have shown promising commercial prospects, such as indoor energy for the Internet of Things, solar powered windows, and greenhouses [1, 2]. Besides, flexible and lightweight OSCs can be potentially applied to portable facilities, electronic skins, etc. [3-5]. All of these applications rely on three key parameters: power conversion efficiencies (PCEs), stability, and cost [6]. Currently, two-component photo-active layers containing physically blended electron donors (Ds) and acceptors (As), namely the "bulk-heterojunction' (BHJ) active layers (ALs), predominate the OSC field [7-12]. Due to the fast development of the fused-ring electron acceptors, the certified PCEs of bulk-heterojunction organic solar cells (BHJOsCs) are improved to an unprecedented and unexpected degree, and PCEs over $1 8 \%$ have been obtained in the state-of-the-art studies [13-15]. Nevertheless, the performance of BHJOsCs tends to be degraded under thermal and light stress, and the long-term stability in BHJOsCs is still difficult to realize in low-cost solution-processing manufacture. The degree of performance degradation in the OSCs depends on the stability of the conjugated materials in the photo-active layers, the interfacial layers, and the electrodes. It is acknowledged that, after a long-term operation, the donor/acceptor components tend to convert into thermodynamically-stable microstructures, typically consisting of large-scale self-aggregated domains, which are detrimental to charge separation and transport [16]. A straight approach to prevent self-aggregation in the BHJ systems is to covalently connect the donor with acceptor units, which is used to fabricate the so-called "single-component organic solar cells (ScOsCs)' [17]. Recent studies have demonstrated the significantly enhanced photo and thermal stability of the sCOsCs, compared with related

BHJOsCs [18, 19]. Therefore, degradation of photovoltaic performance is alleviated in SCOsCs, suggesting a promising potential technology for the fabrication of large-area rugged devices.

In the early development stage of SCOsCs, pristine conjugated materials without the intramolecular heterojunction structures were introduced to manufacture the photovoltaic devices. However, the PCEs of the SCOsCs based on pristine conjugated materials were below $0 . 1 \%$ [20], illustrating that dissociation of the photo-induced exciton is inefficient. With the development of the BHJ concept, single component (SC)-conjugated materials with covalently linked electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups started to attract attention and materials with the intramolecular heterojunction structures, such as molecular dyads, block copolymers (BCPs), and double-cable conjugated polymers (DCPs), were prepared for the high-performance SCOsCs. Although much progress has been achieved during the last two decades, the efforts spent on promoting development of the SCOSCs were less, and thus related cell performance is much lower than those of BHJOSCs. Herein, we will summarize the development of SCOSCs from the aspect of conjugated materials and microstructures, analyze the scientific challenges, and then discuss the opportunity of SCOSCs.

# 9.2 Single-Component Conjugated Materials for ScosCs

Single-component conjugated materials with the intramolecular D-A structures, such as molecular dyads and conjugated polymers, have been widely used as the photo-active layers to fabricate SCOsCs, which exhibited the advantages of definite structures and excellent reproducibility [17]. Additionally, the development of donor units that appeared in SCOsCs was influenced by the development of conjugated molecules for BHJOsCs. As for the acceptor units, the fullerene and its derivatives as the efficient acceptor predominated the evolution of the performances of SCOSCs while the perylene bisimides (PBI) showed outstanding performance in some studies.

# 9.2.1 Molecular Dyads

# 9.2.1.1 Fullerene-Based "In-Chain" Molecular Dyads

Plenty of dyads combining fullerenes with molecular $\pi$ -conjugated systems have been intensively studied for a long period. As shown in Figures 9.1 and 9.2, many fullerene-based "in-chain' molecular dyads have been reported. In the "in-chain" molecule dyads, the fullerene units were directly connected to the donor units.

Two fullerene-based dyads (SM01 and SM02) [21, 22] reported by Nierengarte and coworkers were designed as SC materials for SCOSCs, in which two phenylenevinylene oligomers ( $\dot { n }$ -PVs) were covalently linked with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ through a pyrrolidine group. The best results were obtained with the PCE of approximately $0 . 3 \%$ under monochromatic irradiation. Scheme 9.1 illustrated the synthetic route of dyad SM02, and the formation of the donor segments with quantified aldehyde groups is the key process in the molecular synthesis.

![](images/380b18ed8f4c2298c39db9c1b3870316fc0ea1290090b18fc7b324fa74301f2c.jpg)  
Figure 9.1 Chemical structures of fullerene-based "in-chain" molecular dyads.

Janssen and coworkers carried out a series of $n$ -PV-fullerene dyads (SM03-06) for application in SCOsCs [23]. The best result was achieved in the SM06-based cells, providing a short-circuit current density $( J _ { \mathrm { s c } } )$ of $0 . 2 3 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and the PCE of $0 . 0 4 \%$ under a white light with the power of $6 5 \mathrm { m W } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ . To improve the performance of SCOsCs, Sariciftci and coworkers developed three molecular dyads SM07-09, in which the thiophene or naphthalene groups were introduced to replace the benzene in the $n$ -PV. The optimized devices showed the best PCE of $0 . 2 \%$ under the irradiation of white light $( 8 0 \mathrm { m W } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 } )$ ) [24].

Although molecular dyads contained $n$ -PV and the derivatives have been used for SCOSCs, the low performance indicates that PV was not a good backbone to construct these molecules. Compared with $n$ -PVs, the oligothiophenes showed broader photoresponse, higher hole mobilities, and better crystallinity. Therefore, the molecular dyads based on oligothiophenes grafted with fullerene were investigated to improve the photovoltaic performance in sCOsCs. Yamashiro et al. reported the design and synthesis of molecular dyads that contained oligothiophenes as D unit and single $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ as A unit (SM10-13) [25, 26]. These molecules were used as photo-active layers to construct SCOsCs, in which the effect of the length of oligothiophenes on the photovoltaic performance was carefully studied. The research illustrated that a relatively high PCE of $0 . 4 \%$ was achieved with $1 6 \mathrm { T - C } _ { 6 0 }$ (SM13) as the active layer in the SCOSC with a long conjugated backbone.

![](images/d4347e3872da44506b975900988f3bea73d250939cf7f5f528a659d8187859be.jpg)  
Figure 9.2 Chemical structures of multiple fullerene-based "in-chain" molecular dyads.

![](images/c77ae2173e497ba47d8b79a02c56316ff4d3b516182c26dec1c1c78e5ed158aa.jpg)  
Scheme 9.1 The synthetic route of fullerene-based "in-chain" molecular dyad SM02. (i) $p$ -methylstyrene, ${ \mathsf { P d } } ( { \mathsf { O A c } } ) _ { 2 }$ , tri- $o$ -tolylphosphine, $\mathsf { E t } _ { 3 } \mathsf { N } ,$ Xylene, $1 3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathsf C ,$ 48 hours; (ii) 2,2-dimethylpropane-1,3-diol, $p$ -TsOH, ${ \mathsf C } _ { 6 } { \mathsf H } _ { 6 }$ , reflux, Dean-Stark trap, 24 hours; (iii) $\mathsf { M n O } _ { 2 }$ $\mathsf { C H } _ { 2 } \mathsf { C l } _ { 2 }$ , rt, 1 hours; (iv) aniline, ${ \mathsf C } _ { 6 } { \mathsf H } _ { 6 }$ , reflux, Dean-Stark trap, 24 hours; () $t { \cdot } \mathsf { B u O K } ,$ DMF, $8 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathsf { C }$ 2 hours; (vi) ${ \mathsf { C F } } _ { 3 } { \mathsf { C O } } _ { 2 } { \mathsf { H } }$ $\mathsf { C H } _ { 2 } \mathsf { C l } _ { 2 }$ ${ \mathsf { H } } _ { 2 } 0$ , room temp., 4 hours; (vi) $\mathsf { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , sarcosine, toluene, reflux, 16 hours.

Singh and coworkers further introduced highly crystalline oligothiophenediketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) into the conjugated backbone to extend the absorption spectra to the near-infrared (NIR) region, and the corresponding molecular dyad SM14 showed the broad absorption band in the $3 0 0 { - } 8 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ region [27]. The NIR photoresponse in the as-cast films of SM14 was essentially dominated by the absorption of the bis-dithienyl-DPP with a maximum absorption peak at $6 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ . SCOSCs fabricated with the configuration of (indium tin oxide) $\mathrm { I T O / M o O } _ { x } / \mathrm { S M } 1 4 / \mathrm { C a } / \mathrm { A l }$ were tested under monochromatic and white light irradiation. The photoresponse extends from 400 to $8 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ with a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 0.38 at $6 7 0 \mathrm { n m }$ . Under simulated solar light, the cell gives a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $6 . 7 0 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a PCE of $2 . 1 7 \%$ , which ranks among the highest values reported for molecular dyads.

Despite the molecular engineering of the donor segments, another rational method to improve the efficiency of the SCOsCs is to change the number of acceptors in SC materials. Under the guidance of this principle, two or more $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ were introduced into the molecular dyads, as shown in Figure 9.2. The synthesis of SM15, SM16 was reported by T. Yamashiro and coworkers [28]. Also, N. Negishi et al. reported a series of oligothiophenes grafted with two $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ at the end (SM17-20) [29]. With the increasing content of $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , the device containing SM20 as the photo-active layer gave a PCE of $0 . 6 5 \%$ . Nonetheless, poor device performances were obtained when another two $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ were added (SM21-22) [30]. In another study, Janssen and coworkers reported the synthesis of molecular dyads based on the $p$ -styrene (SM23) or $p$ -phenylacetylene (SM24) oligomers as the donor core, with which four $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ were introduced [31]. A very low PCE of $0 . 0 1 5 \%$ was obtained in the SCOSCs with the structure of Glass/ITO/PEDOT:PSS/AL/LiF/Al. The photovoltaic properties have not been significantly improved as predicted with the increasing proportion of $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ , which may originate from unbalanced carrier mobilities and poor nanophase separation.

# 9.2.1.2 Fullerene-Based "Side-Chain" D-A Molecular Dyads

In the fullerene-based "in-chain' D-A molecules, conjugated donor parts were directly linked with $\mathrm { C } _ { 6 0 }$ through the carbon-carbon single bond, which results in inappropriate phase separation and poor charge transport. Hence, researchers introduced flexible chains as linkers between the donor and acceptor segment to improve the photovoltaic performance in SCOsCs. Many studies emphasized that the nature and length of the flexible linkers are the determining factors for the nanophase separation of D and A parts in these materials.

![](images/7504c2475f48e2a826c81fddee4690e2d12cfc1984afa2339dd752c240447209.jpg)  
Figure 9.3Chemical structures of fullerene-based "side-chain" D-A molecular dyads.

As shown in Figure 9.3, K. Hashimoto and coworkers described the synthesis of the molecular dyad sM25, combining the thiophene heptamer as donor with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 6 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ attached at the median thiophene ring via an oligo(oxyethylene) chain as acceptor in 2007 [32, 33]. Interestingly, the absorption of SM25 showed a blue shift in the as-cast film due to the formation of $H$ -aggregate of oligothiophenes in the solid state. The device with the configuration of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/SM25/Al gave a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $0 . 9 3 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a PCE of $0 . 1 5 \%$ . Furthermore, SM26, an $n$ -PV containing five phenyl rings with $\mathrm { P C } _ { 6 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ attached to the middle of the chain by a polyether linker, was developed by the same group. A PCE of $1 . 2 8 \%$ was achieved in the devices that contained SM26 as the photo-active layer, and the sharply increased PCE compared with SM25 confirms the importance of the molecular packing and crystallinity [34].

The influence of $\mathrm { D } / \mathrm { A }$ ratio in sCOsCs was studied through a series of DPP-oligothiophene/fullerene dyads (SM27-29) developed by Tajima and coworkers [35]. Resulting from the oligothiophene elongated, the $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and FF (fill factor) of SCOSCs increased and the optimized device gave the best PCE of $1 . 1 1 \%$ . Besides, the length of the linkers between donor and acceptor units was investigated by B. Ma and coworkers. Several DPP-containing oligothiophene-fullerene triads (SM30-32) were designed and synthesized to verify the effect of varying lengths of linkers [36]. The charge-transport properties of SM30-32 were determined in field-effect transistor (FET) devices. These three molecules exhibited the appropriate electron mobilities around $1 . 5 \times 1 0 ^ { - 3 } \ : \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } \ : \mathrm { V } ^ { - 1 } \ : \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }$ while the hole mobilities were rarely obtained. The best PCE of $0 . 4 9 \%$ was achieved in the SM32-based devices. Despite the relatively poor performance, the results indicated that the performance of the device was associated with the alkyl spacers. And in the control experiment, the BHJOSCs with the P3HT as the donor and SM30-32 as the acceptor were prepared and gave the best PCE of $2 . 4 1 \%$ . This result revealed that the excessive phenyl- $C _ { 6 1 }$ -butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) in the SCOSC system adversely affected the aggregation of the donor units.

Nguyen et al. [37, 38] reported the synthesis of a different type of dumbbell molecule (SM33) consisting of a conjugated block with a central di(thiophen-yl) benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b'ldithiophene (DT-BDT) unit with two dioctyl terthienyl side blocks and two rhodanine terminal moieties on which PCBM was linked by 6-carbon alkyl spacer, and the synthetic route of SM33 was illustrated in Scheme 9.2.

The SM33 presents a broad absorption band in the $3 0 0 { - } 7 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ region with a maximum peak at $5 5 7 \mathrm { n m }$ in solution. And sCOsCs with the structure of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/SM33/ZnO/Al were fabricated and evaluated under simulated solar light. The best devices provided a high $J _ { \mathrm { s c } } > 7 . 0 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a PCE of $2 . 3 1 \%$ . Stability tests performed at $8 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ under an inert atmosphere revealed that the SM33-based sCOsC presented excellent morphological stabilities, with no degradation of performance after annealing at $8 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for 100 hours. Recently, Min and coworkers described the donor-acceptor type dyads (SM34) in which a single $\mathrm { P C } _ { 7 1 } \mathrm { B M }$ unit as the acceptor was attached to the 3T-BDT-3T donor block [39]. With the decrease of fullerene content, the best devices with sM34 gave a higher $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $7 . 5 \mathrm { m A c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a PCE of $3 . 2 2 \%$ than that of cells based on SM33. The results demonstrate that the asymmetric molecular design is an efficient route to develop new molecular dyads toward high-performance SCOSCs.

# 9.2.1.3 PBI-Based Molecular Dyads

Besides the fullerene-based molecules, the perylene bisimide (PBI) and its derivatives were also used as the acceptor to design molecular dyads for SCOsCs. Figure 9.4 illustrates the chemical structures of dyads with PBIs for application in SCOSCs.

In 2009, Geng and coworkers reported the synthesis of three smectic liquid crystal molecules (SM35-37) with the structure of substituted fluorene-alt-bithiophene as the donor and single PBI as the acceptor [40] (Scheme 9.3).

Devices with the architecture of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/SM37/HBL/LiF/Al, where the hole-blocking layer (HBL) is $N \mathbf { \mathcal { N } ^ { \prime } }$ -bis(1-ethylpropyl) substituted PBI, were fabricated. The PCE was significantly improved by thermal or solvent annealing processes, and the devices based on SM37 with the longest conjugated backbone provided the best results. The PCE was $0 . 5 0 \%$ for the pristine thin film, increasing to $0 . 7 0 \%$ after thermal treatment, and to $1 . 5 0 \%$ with $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $4 . 4 9 \mathrm { m A } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ , after solvent annealing and insertion of an HBL in the device. The same group also synthesized a series of similar conjugated materials (SM38-40) [41], in which the hexyl chain attached at the nitrogen atom of PBI was replaced by a branched neopentyl group. This modification improved the photovoltaic performance with an enhanced PCE of $1 . 7 5 \%$ . After that, Geng and coworkers extended their approach to the synthesis of related systems in which the terminal PBI was attached to the hybrid conjugated backbones linked with alkyl spacers containing two, four, and six carbons (SM41-43) [42]. The absorption spectra of SM43 in solution are identical to that of sm4o, indicating that even without an alkyl spacer, the electronic interactions between the $\pi$ -conjugated donor chain and the PBI acceptor are negligible in SM4o. This is probably due to a large twist angle around the connecting bond due to steric interactions. The photovoltaic properties with sM41-43 were characterized with the same type of device configuration as compounds SM38. Three compounds lead to rather comparable results with PCE values in the range of $2 . 0 \%$ , which is consistent with the EQE responses. To extend absorption of the conjugated donor, benzodithiazole (BT) was introduced (SM44), and this modification enhanced the absorption in the $5 0 0 { - } 6 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ region, resulting in a further improvement of performances with a $J _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $5 . 3 2 \mathrm { m A } \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 2 }$ and a PCE of $2 . 7 0 \%$ . Recently, W. Li and coworkers have reported a new series of "double-cable type" molecules (SM45-47) with BDT-DPP-BDT as donor block and pendant PBIs as acceptor groups [43]. The pendant PBI groups were connected to the conjugated backbone by flexible dodecyl linkages while the effects of substitution of the lateral thienyl group of DT-BDT were investigated. These molecules were synthesized by Stille coupling using a dibromo-2T-DPP carrying two PBI side groups with three different distannyl-BDT compounds substituted by 2-(2-ethylhexyl)-thiophene, 2-((2-ethylhexyl)thio)-thiophene, and 2-((2-ethylhexyl)thio)-3-fluorothiophene. With systematic studies on the effect of the sulfur and fluorine atoms in the donor blocks, the results revealed that the additional sulfur atom in the side chain of 2T-DPP unit (SM46) enhanced the crystallinity of materials and elevated photovoltaic properties with a PCE of $2 . 5 2 \%$
